'''Adore Me''' is a [[direct-to-consumer]] women's intimate apparel brand based in New York City.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=206832967|title=Adore Me, Inc.: Private Company Information - Bloomberg|website=www.bloomberg.com|access-date=2019-06-10}}</ref> The company was started by Morgan Hermand-Waiche in 2010 while he was an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] student at [[Harvard Business School]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/02/12/business/smallbusiness/adore-me-takes-on-victorias-secret-and-other-bigger-lingerie-rival.html|title=For Valentine's Day, Adore Me Takes On Victoria's Secret and Other Bigger Lingerie Rivals|last=Max|first=Sarah|date=2015-02-11|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-12-05|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and is a Certified B Corporation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bcorporation.net/en-us/find-a-b-corp/company/adore-me|title=B Adore Me - Certified B Corp|date=2022-09-06}}</ref>

==History==
Adore Me was founded by Morgan Hermand-Waiche.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Perez |first=Sarah |date=2012-06-06 |title=Adore Me Raises $2.5 Million For Personalized Lingerie Showrooms |work=[[TechCrunch]] |url=https://techcrunch.com/2012/06/06/adore-me-raises-2-5-million-for-personalized-lingerie-showrooms/ |access-date=2023-07-26}}</ref> He got the idea of starting a lingerie company in 2010 during his second year at Harvard Business School's M.B.A program, when he could not find lingerie that was both high quality and affordable.<ref name=":2" /> Hermand-Waiche spent three years working at [[management consulting]] firm [[McKinsey & Company]] prior to Adore Me<ref>{{cite web|title=The First Five Years: Morgan Hermand-Waiche (MBA 2010)| date=26 February 2014 |url=https://www.alumni.hbs.edu/stories/Pages/story-bulletin.aspx?num=3228|publisher=Harvard Business School|accessdate=6 July 2015}}</ref> where he met Romain Liot, who joined with him at Adore Me. Gary Bravard joined early on as co-founder.<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Profile: Gary Bravard |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/gary-bravard/ |access-date=July 6, 2021 |website=Forbes}}</ref>

Initial investors in Adore Me include Hermand-Waiche's Harvard professors,<ref name=":2" /> and [[Angel investor|angel investors]] [[Fabrice Grinda]] and José Marín.<ref name=":3" /> The company officially launched its website in March 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Carney|first1=Michael|title=Intimates etailer Adore Me pads its bank with $8.5 million in Series B funding|url=https://pando.com/2013/07/09/intimates-etailer-adore-me-pads-its-bank-with-8-5-million-in-series-b-funding/|publisher=Pando|accessdate=6 July 2015|date=2013-07-09}}</ref> In the same year, Adore Me raised $2.5 million in its second round of funding with investments from Redhills Ventures, Jaina Capital, Ventech Capital, and other US angel investors.<ref name=":3" /> Adore Me reportedly sold 100,000 items in their first year of business.<ref name="8.5 million">{{cite web|last1=Shontell|first1=Alyson|title=Man Raises $8.5 Million For Victoria's Secret Killer, AdoreMe, Which Sells Half-Price Lingerie|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/adoreme-raises-85-million-2013-7|publisher=Business Insider|accessdate=6 July 2015}}</ref>

In July 2013, Adore Me raised $8.5 million from investors in a [[Venture capital financing#Fourth stage|Series B round of funding]]. Investors included [[Upfront Ventures]], Redhills Ventures, and [[Mousse Partners]].<ref name="8.5 million" /><ref name=xconomy>{{cite web|last1=Ruth|first1=João-Pierre S.|title=Lingerie E-Commerce Site Adore Me, Developed at Harvard, Raises $8.5M|url=http://www.xconomy.com/new-york/2013/07/09/lingerie-e-commerce-site-adore-me-developed-at-harvard-raises-8-5m/|publisher=Xconomy|accessdate=6 July 2015|date=2013-07-09}}</ref> This brought Adore Me's total funding to $11.2 million.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brooke |first=Eliza |date=2013-07-09 |title=Fast Fashion Lingerie E-Tailer Adore Me Takes $8.5M In Series B Funding |work=[[TechCrunch]] |url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/07/09/fast-fashion-lingerie-e-tailer-adore-me-takes-8-5m-in-series-b-funding/ |access-date=2023-07-26}}</ref>

In 2014, Adore Me was listed as the second fastest-growing private retail company on the [[Inc. (magazine)|Inc. 5000]] list based on their 2013 sales of $5.6 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=The 2014 Inc. 5000|url=http://www.inc.com/inc5000/list/2014/industry/retail/|publisher=Inc.|accessdate=6 July 2015}}</ref> They went on to generate $16.2 million in sales in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zaroban |first1=Stefany |date=2015-05-12 |title=Second 500 newcomers skip ahead of their older rivals |url=https://www.internetretailer.com/2015/05/12/second-500-newcomers-skip-ahead-their-older-rivals |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706234629/https://www.internetretailer.com/2015/05/12/second-500-newcomers-skip-ahead-their-older-rivals |archive-date=2015-07-06 |accessdate=2023-07-23 |website=InternetRetailer.com |publisher=Internet Retailer}}</ref>

In 2016, Adore Me was ranked #9 on [[Crain Communications|Crain's list]] of New York's 50 Fastest-Growing Companies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.crainsnewyork.com/features/2016-fast50#adore-me|title=Crain's names 50 fastest-growing companies in 2016|website=Crain's New York Business|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref> Revenue for 2016 was $83.9 million.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.inc.com/profile/adore-me|title=Adore Me|website=Inc.com|language=en|access-date=2017-09-18}}</ref>

In 2017, Adore Me was named one of the Internet Retailer Top 1000 companies from DigitalCommerce360 and was listed on the [[Inc. (magazine)|Inc. 5000]] list for the third time in four years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loechner |first=Jack |date=2017-04-25 |title=Online Retail Eclipses Brick & Mortar By 6 to 1 |url=https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/299666/online-retail-eclipses-brick-mortar-by-6-to-1.html |access-date=2017-05-22 |website=MediaPost |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> As of 2017, Adore Me had 121 full-time employees.<ref name=":1" />

In November 2022, it was announced Adore Me had been acquired by [[Victoria's Secret]] for $400 million USD.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schulz |first=Madeline |date=2022-11-01 |title=Victoria's Secret will acquire Adore Me for $400 million to fuel comeback |url=https://www.voguebusiness.com/companies/victorias-secret-will-acquire-adore-me-for-dollar400-million-to-fuel-comeback |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=[[Vogue (magazine) | Vogue Business]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-01 |title=Victoria's Secret & Co. Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Adore Me, Inc. |url=https://www.victoriassecretandco.com/news-releases/news-release-details/victorias-secret-co-signs-definitive-agreement-acquire-adore-me |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Victoria’s Secret & Co. Press Releases}}</ref> Victoria's Secret & Co made the decision to purchase Adore Me in part because of the subscription service, with the hope of retaining consumers beyond the traditional reliance of brand loyalty.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kestenbaum |first=Richard |date=2022-11-01 |title=Why Victoria's Secret Is Buying AdoreMe |work=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/richardkestenbaum/2022/11/01/why-victorias-secret-is-buying-adoreme/ |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref>

== Products and services==
Initially, Adore Me products included [[lingerie]], [[Nightwear|sleepwear]], [[Swimsuit|swimwear]], and related apparel, including [[Plus-size clothing|plus sizes]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=O'Brien |first1=Sara Ashley |date=2015-05-05 |title=Plus-size models sell more bras |url=http://money.cnn.com/2015/03/17/technology/startup-adore-me/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320003232/http://money.cnn.com/2015/03/17/technology/startup-adore-me |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 20, 2015 |accessdate=2023-07-26 |website=[[CNN Business]] |publisher=CNN Money}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chapin |first=Adele |date=2016-06-17 |title=Adore Me Bras and Panties Land in Nordstrom Today |url=http://www.racked.com/2016/6/17/11963362/nordstrom-adore-me-lingerie-bras |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=[[Vox_Media#Racked | Racked]]}}</ref> In October 2016, Adore Me launched an [[Sportswear|active wear]] collection, ranging in size from petite to plus.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Borchardt |first=Debra |date=2016-09-19 |title=Adore Me Launching All Size Activewear Collection |language=en-US |newspaper=[[Women's Wear Daily | WWD]] |url=http://wwd.com/fashion-news/fashion-scoops/adore-me-activewear-plus-size-10554405/ |access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fraser |first=Kristopher |date=2016-09-19 |title=Adore Me to launch all size activewear |work=[[FashionUnited]] |url=https://fashionunited.com/news/fashion/adore-me-to-launch-all-size-activewear/2016091912947 |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Novellino |first=Teresa |date=2016-09-30 |title=Adore me expands to active wear, playing up plus-size in ad campaign |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/newyork/news/2016/09/30/adore-me-expands-to-active-wear-plays-up-plus-size.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=www.bizjournals.com}}</ref> In April 2017, Adore Me announced their newest swim collection, with 88 pieces for standard and plus-sized women.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mantor |first=Cassidy |date=2017-04-17 |title=Adore Me makes big splash into swimwear |language=en-US |work=FashionNetwork.com |url=http://us.fashionnetwork.com/news/Adore-Me-makes-big-splash-into-swimwear,817390.html#.WQtLSFPyvEZ |access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref> Head of design, Helen Mears, formerly worked as head designer of the Angels brand at Victoria's Secret.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schwartzmann |first1=Rachel |others=Graphics by Jane Espirtu; Photos by Erin Yamagata |title=AdoreMe |url=http://thestyleline.com/adoreme/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015175735/https://www.thestyleline.com/adoreme/ |archive-date=2013-10-15 |accessdate=2023-07-23 |website=The Style Line}}</ref>

The brand has been compared to [[Zara (retailer)|Zara]] regarding pricing and its practice of [[Fast fashion|fast-fashion]] production.<ref name="8.5 million" /><ref name="xconomy" /> Adore Me primarily sells its products online. Customers shop through personalized "showrooms" and can purchase products a-la-carte on a one time basis or as part of a monthly subscription, known as "VIP Membership."

In December 2017, Adore Me launched their Bijou Collection.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/adore-me-launches-a-luxury-designer-collection-at-an-affordable-price-point--blurring-the-lines-between-fast-fashion-and-luxury-retail-300567130.html|title=Adore Me Launches a Luxury Designer Collection at an Affordable Price Point - Blurring the Lines Between Fast-Fashion and Luxury Retail|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2018-11-14}}</ref> This luxury designer collection used fabrics such as velvet, French lace as well as gold logo plates and piercings.

As of July 2021, Adore Me carried various product categories, including bras and panties, lingerie, sleepwear, gifts, activewear, corsets and bralettes.

The company uses a style quiz and associated algorithm to recommend products and sizes to customers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pina |first=Tanisha |date=2018-02-08 |title=The Best Places to Shop for Lingerie, Bras, and Underwear |work=Vox |url=https://www.vox.com/2018/2/8/16965818/best-lingerie-boutiques-online |url-status=usurped |access-date=2023-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019001803/https://www.vox.com/2018/2/8/16965818/best-lingerie-boutiques-online |archive-date=2018-10-19}}</ref>

== Expansion into retail ==
In April 2016, Adore Me opened their first retail store as a showroom at their New York City headquarters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2016/02/24/adore-mes-latest-plan-to-upend-victorias-secret.html|title=Adore Me's new plan to upend Victoria's Secret|last=Booth|first=Barbara|date=2016-02-24|website=CNBC|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref> In June 2016, Adore Me partnered with [[Nordstrom]] to begin selling products in Nordstrom stores and on the company's e-commerce site.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://wwd.com/fashion-news/fashion-scoops/adore-me-nordstrom-lingerie-10456616/|title=Online Retailer Adore Me to Sell in Select Nordstrom Stores|last=Borchardt|first=Debra|date=2016-06-15|newspaper=WWD|access-date=2016-11-28|language=en-US}}</ref> As of October 2016, Adore Me also partnered with Lord and Taylor to begin selling products in the Manhattan flagship store and online.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Novellino |first=Teresa |date=2016-10-25 |title=Exclusive: Adore Me strikes lingerie deal with Lord & Taylor - New York Business Journal |newspaper=[[American City Business Journals | New York Business Journal]] |url=http://www.bizjournals.com/newyork/news/2016/10/25/exclusive-adore-me-strikes-lingerie-deal-with-lord.html |access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref>

Adore Me opened its first permanent brick and mortar retail store in June, 2018. The first store was located in [[Staten Island Mall|Staten Island Mall, NY]], developed in partnership with Brookfield.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/adore-me-takes-aim-at-victorias-secret-with-up-to-300-stores-1522155600|title=E-Commerce Lingerie Brand Gets Physical (With Stores), in Challenge to Victoria's Secret|last=Safdar|first=Khadeeja|date=2018-03-27|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=2019-02-06|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Daphne |date=2018-03-28 |title=Lingerie e-tailer Adore Me plots up to 300 stores |url=https://www.retaildive.com/news/lingerie-e-tailer-adore-me-plots-up-to-300-stores/520152/ |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=[[Industry Dive | Retail Dive]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

The store also has "smart" fitting rooms:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roshitsh |first=Kaley |date=2019-01-16 |title=Fitting Rooms Get Techy: Adore Me, StoreAdvise Bring IoT to Intimates |url=https://wwd.com/business-news/technology/adore-me-storeadvise-fitting-room-experience-1202964609/ |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=[[Women's Wear Daily | WWD]] |language=en}}</ref> the Adore Me customer can place an item, embedded with a radio frequency identification tag, on the hook in her fitting room to activate the fitting-room display screen. It will indicate the item chosen in full detail — revealing a product image, as well as size run and colors available.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wassel |first=Bryan |date=2019-01-18 |title=AdoreMe Rolls Out Smart Display-Enabled Fitting Rooms |url=https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/features/news-briefs/adoreme-rolls-out-smart-display-enabled-fitting-rooms |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=www.retailtouchpoints.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Marianne |date=2019-01-13 |title=Adore Me brings modern tech to in-store lingerie shopping |url=https://www.chainstoreage.com/technology/adore-me-brings-modern-tech-to-in-store-lingerie-shopping/ |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=Chain Store Age |language=en-US}}</ref>

On [[Black Friday (shopping)|Black Friday]] of 2018, at 6 am Eastern, Adore Me opened its second retail store, located in [[Bridgewater Commons|Bridgewater Commons Mall]], [[Bridgewater Township, New Jersey|Bridgewater, NJ]]. The store is 3,600 square-foot in size — which is double the size of its first location which opened in June 2018 at Staten Island Mall, in the Staten Island borough of New York City.<ref name="retaildive.com">{{Cite web |last=Howland |first=Daphne |date=2018-11-26 |title=Adore Me opens 1st store outside of New York |url=https://www.retaildive.com/news/adore-me-opens-1st-store-outside-of-new-york/542906/ |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=[[Industry Dive | Retail Dive]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The larger store incorporates lounge areas to encourage involvement with the space. The two stores were designed by New York City-based Lawrence Group.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Marianne |date=2018-11-20 |title=Online lingerie startup begins retail store push |url=https://www.chainstoreage.com/real-estate/online-lingerie-startup-begins-retail-store-push/ |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=Chain Store Age |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2018, it was reported that the company planned to open 300 stores during the upcoming five years.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2018/adore-me-victorias-secret-lingerie/|title=Adore Me Opens Brick-And-Mortar Lingerie Stores|date=2018-03-28|website=PYMNTS.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wylie |first=Melissa |date=2018-03-29 |title=Adore Me plans hundreds of stores |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/bizwomen/news/latest-news/2018/03/adore-me-plans-hundreds-of-stores.html |access-date=2019-02-06 |website=[[American City Business Journals | bizjournals.com]]}}</ref> In April 2019, Adore Me opened its third retail location at [[Providence Place|Providence Place Mall]] in [[Providence, Rhode Island]]. In May 2019 a fourth location was opened in Willowbrook, New Jersey. Both of these locations are owned by [[Brookfield Properties]].

== The Adore Me Group brands ==
2019 started a string of acquisitions and development of new brands.

In February 2019, Adore Me purchased maternity brand Belabumbum.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retaildive.com/news/adore-me-eyes-sales-bump-with-belabumbum-acquisition/549345/|title=Adore Me eyes sales bump with Belabumbum acquisition|website=Retail Dive|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chainstoreage.com/technology/adore-me-shows-love-to-expecting-new-moms-with-acquisition|title=Adore Me shows love to expecting, new moms with acquisition|website=Chain Store Age|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref> Adore Me states that "the acquisition was part of Adore Me's strategy to boost further growth by broadening the product offering to serve new phases of a woman's life".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://digiday.com/retail/retail-briefing-adore-me-acquires-maternity-brand-brand-portfolio/|title=Adore Me acquires maternity brand as it seeks to build brand portfolio|last=Milnes|first=Hilary|date=2019-02-27|website=Digiday|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref> Belabumbum offers intimate apparel, sleep, lounge, and activewear for expecting and new moms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://belabumbum.com/|title=Belabumbum maternity & nursing clothes for new and pregnant moms|website=Belabumbum|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref>

In June 2019, Adore Me launched its first satellite brand, called Walkpop, a brand specifically offering legwear, [[leggings]], tights, and socks in a range of sizes, styles, and skin tones.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://walkpop.com/pages/about-us|title=About Us|website=Walkpop|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref>

In January 2020, Adore Me launched period panties brand, Joyja.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc-7.com/story/41627555/adore-me-introduces-joyja-an-ultra-inclusive-brand-of-period-panties|title=Adore Me introduces Joyja - an ultra-inclusive brand of period panties|website=www.abc-7.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref> The panties come in sizes XS-4X.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.trendhunter.com/trends/menstruation-underwear|title=Inclusive Menstruation Underwear Menstruation Underwear|website=TrendHunter.com|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref> With the tagline "The Happy Period Panties," Joyja wants to bring more joy to "that time of the month" with bright colors, quirky prints, easy usage, and a significantly lower environmental impact than plastic tampons and pads. The brand also wants to improve access of period products for menstruating people in the US living below the poverty line. They do this through affordable pricing and by product donations<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marketwatch.com/press-release/adore-me-introduces-joyja---an-ultra-inclusive-brand-of-period-panties-2020-01-29|title=Adore Me introduces Joyja - an ultra-inclusive brand of period panties|website=MarketWatch|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.joyja.com/pages/our-mission|title=Our mission|website=Joyja|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref>

== Branding campaigns ==
During [[International Women's Day]] and the month of March 2019, Adore Me partnered with non-profit organization Girls Inc., which offered support, mentoring and guidance for girls. Adore Me sold a collection of panties featuring female-empowering prints with 100% of proceeds donated to Girls Inc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BvexYKKDNrI/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/instagram/girlsinc/2008259648306338504 |archive-date=2021-12-25 |url-access=registration|title=Girls Inc. on Instagram: "There's still time to support our PANTIES FOR A CAUSE partnership with @adoreme celebrating all #Fearless girls and women. Shop the…"|website=Instagram|language=en|access-date=2019-05-16}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://milled.com/adore-me/introducing-panties-for-a-cause-100-of-proceeds-will-go-to-girls-inc-upKBoGintkiUHYaW|title=Adore Me: Introducing Panties for a Cause!|website=Milled|language=en|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref>

In 2018, Adore Me conducted an artistic portrait series together with New York-based photojournalist Aude Adrien, highlighting women working at Adore Me, and their stories of how they got to where they are now, what inspires them, and how they define empowerment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.audeadrien.com/adoreme|title=Building Confidence For All|website=Aude Adrien Photography & Journalism|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adorememagazine.com/team|title=Team|website=Adore Me Magazine|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref>

== TV appearances ==
Adore Me was featured on the final season of ''Project Runway: All Stars''.<ref name="prnewswire.com">{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/adore-me-featured-in-the-final-season-of-project-runway-all-stars-300783936.html|title=Adore Me Featured In The Final Season Of Project Runway: All Stars|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2019-08-09}}</ref> Adore Me's Head Designer Helen Mears<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://villagegreennj.com/arts/maplewoods-helen-mears/|title=Maplewood's Helen Mears Leads 'Adore Me' Corset Challenge on Project Runway All Stars|date=2019-01-23|website=The Village Green|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-09}}</ref> introduced the challenge for the third episode. The challenge was to create an outfit that used innerwear as outerwear,{{CN|date=November 2023}} specifically, a corset. Christina Exie<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mylifetime.com/shows/project-runway-all-stars/cast/christina-exie|title=Lifetime}}</ref> won the challenge and had her winning corset sold on AdoreMe.com after the episode aired.<ref name="prnewswire.com"/>

== International expansion ==
Until 2017, Adore Me primarily focused on the North American market, delivering its products to all states in the U.S., as well as Canada, Australia, and the UK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2018/11/05/adore-me-makes-a-brand-push-into-canada-australia/|title=Adore Me makes a brand push into Canada, Australia|first=Allison|last=Enright|date=2018-11-05|website=Digital Commerce 360|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crainsnewyork.com/awards/adore-me|title=Fast 50 - Adore Me|website=Crain's New York Business|language=en|access-date=2019-01-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chainstoreage.com/real-estate/online-lingerie-startup-begins-retail-store-push/|title=Online lingerie startup begins retail store push|date=2018-11-20|website=Chain Store Age|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-07}}</ref>

In September 2018, Adore Me officially announced its expansion to start selling in China. The brand has begun launching its products using the interactive livestream platform and global shopping marketplace service, ShopShops.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/adore-announces-launch-china-130700150.html|title=Adore Me Announces its Launch in China|website=finance.yahoo.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/adore-me-announces-its-launch-in-china-1027562918|title=Adore Me Announces its Launch in China|website=markets.businessinsider.com|access-date=2019-01-07}}</ref>

== Technology ==
Adore Me was one of the first retailers to use Google's [[AngularJS|Angular]] technology, a JavaScript-based, open-source, front-end web application framework, for its mobile and desktop websites.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-02-13 |title=How Adore Me Wants To Bring The Love Back To Lingerie |url=https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2018/adore-me-lingerie-valentines-day/ |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=www.pymnts.com |publisher=What’s Next Media & Analytics |language=en-US}}</ref>

Adore Me exploits its data on customer preferences from its Style Quiz in order to create a "personalized shopping experience".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/06/13/victorias-secret-fumbles-open-the-door-for-thirdlove-adore-me.html|title=Victoria's Secret's fumbles open the door for ThirdLove, Adore Me|last=Thomas|first=Lauren|date=2018-06-13|website=www.cnbc.com|language=en|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref> In 2018, Adore Me won a Nexty award for 'Best Use of Data in Marketing'.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klein |first=Rachel |date=2018-08-02 |title=2018 Nexty Award Winners Announced |url=https://commercenext.com/2018-nexty-award-winners-announced/ |access-date=2019-05-08 |website=CommerceNext |language=en-US}}</ref>

Adore Me is the founder of New York Hearts Tech (NYHT), a community for tech-focused startups located in NYC.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Novellino |first=Teresa |date=2016-02-08 |title=Now you can shop Silicon Alley at New York Hearts Tech e-commerce site |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/newyork/news/2016/02/08/now-you-can-shop-silicon-alley-at-new-york-hearts.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2019-05-08 |website=[[American City Business Journals | bizjournals.com]]}}</ref>

Adore Me utilizes Kubernetes in its [[proprietary software]] tools — the open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/kubernetes-comic|title=Deploy code faster: with CI/CD and Kubernetes|website=Google Cloud|language=en|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref> Adore Me is an early adopter of the system and hosts regular meetups in their European HQ for other practitioners, aiming to share knowledge about emerging technologies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://devfest.ro/|title=GDG DevFest Romania {{!}} Bucharest 2018|website=devfest.ro|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.meetup.com/Cloud-Native-Computing-Bucharest/events/266460612/|title=Cloud Native Computing Bucharest #1: New Beginnings|website=Meetup|language=en|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.meetup.com/GDG-Cloud-Bucharest/events/263189114/|title=Application Development on Kubernetes - GDG/BJUG Joint Meetup|website=Meetup|language=en|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref>

== Models ==
Adore Me has promoted "body positivity" and "inclusivity" within the brand.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/adore-me-is-using-one-of-victorias-secrets-models-2016-8|title=This lingerie company is using one of Victoria's Secret's own models to compete with the brand|newspaper=Business Insider|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref> They have worked with models such as [[Iskra Lawrence]], a spokesmodel for body positive campaigns;<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cosmopolitan.co.uk/reports/news/a46169/iskra-lawrence-death-threat-internet-troll/|title=Iskra Lawrence received a death threat from terrifying internet troll|date=2016-09-26|newspaper=Cosmopolitan|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/adore-me-behind-the-scenes-photo-2016-8|title=Victoria's Secret's main competitor is releasing a lingerie commercial that's unlike anything we've ever seen|newspaper=Business Insider|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref> [[transgender]] [[Internet celebrity|influencer]] [[Rose Montoya]]; and [[Nina Agdal]], a [[Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue|Sports Illustrated swimsuit model]];<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/swim-daily/2016/08/08/nina-agdal-adore-me-swimwear-campaign-bikini|title=Nina Agdal is the new face of Adore Me Swimwear|last=Hendrix|first=Kelsey|newspaper=SI.com|access-date=2016-11-28}}</ref> In 2016 Adore Me worked with [[Plus-size model|plus model]] [[Sophie Simmons|Sophie Tweed-Simmons]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://people.com/bodies/sophie-tweed-simmons-says-she-was-told-she-wasnt-small-enough-to-model/|title=Sophie Tweed-Simmons Says She Was Told She Wasn't 'Small Enough' to Model|work=PEOPLE.com|access-date=2018-11-14|language=en}}</ref>

On February 4, 2021, Adore Me took to its Twitter account<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-02-04 |title=We're taking a break from tweeting about lingerie today to have an important conversation about TikTok. |url=https://twitter.com/AdoreMe/status/1357379769667624960? |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref> to claim that [[TikTok]] "was openly built with [[discrimination]] at its core." They claimed that several videos that featured [[African Americans|African-American]] and [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic-American]] models, as well as videos with Caucasian models who are not [[Supermodel|supermodels]], were removed from the platform. Adore Me's vice president of strategy, Ranjan Roy, explained that the models sending content for the brand to use on TikTok would then ask if they needed to supply a video with them modeling more or different lingerie sets. He expressed his frustration that the social media platform was putting such pressure on the company's models.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Onibada |first=Ade |date=2021-02-08 |title=A Lingerie Brand Is Claiming TikTok Has Been Removing Its Content Featuring Plus-Size Women And Women Of Color |work=[[BuzzFeed News]] |url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/adeonibada/lingerie-adore-me-tiktok-poc-plus-sized-women |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref>

== Adore Me Services ==
Adore Me owns and operates its own distribution center, Adore Me Services (AMS), based in Secaucus, New Jersey.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adoremeservices.com/|title=Adore Me Services|website=Adore Me Services|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref> The brand opened the new distribution center in January 2019. According to Morgan Hermand-Waiche, building the new center would support the fulfillment of product to the stores.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/adore-me-distribution-centre/|title=Adore Me unveils new distribution centre with robotics technology|date=2019-01-14|website=Verdict Retail|language=en-GB|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref> The opening of AMS was part of the company's second phase into expanding internationally. The solution combines a high-density robotic storage and order picking system with automated put walls and conveyor belts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmh.com/article/adore_me_services_small_space_big_automation|title=Adore Me Services: Small space, big automation|website=www.mmh.com|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref>

Hermand-Waiche stated in a 2020 post to the Adore Me group on [[Medium (website)|Medium]] that AMS was one of the "most rewarding decisions we've ever made" because it allowed the company to move towards sustainability more quickly, it facilitated the launch and fulfillment of Adore Me's satellite brands, and it helped the try-at-home service become "the fastest-growing segment" of the company's revenue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hermand-Waiche |first=Morgan |date=2020-06-11 |title=Resilient Retail: How Adore Me approaches ecommerce |url=https://medium.com/adore-me-group/resilient-retail-how-adore-me-approaches-ecommerce-305012ac1906 |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Adore Me Group |language=en}}</ref>

== Customer service ==
Customer reviews are visible and available for each product on adoreme.com, assisting customers to see product fit, satisfaction and beyond.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yotpo.com/blog/how-adore-me-skyrocketed-growth-with-reviews/|title=Adore Me Uses AI to Analyze Customer Feedback|date=2018-04-02|website=Yotpo|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref>

Adore Me received Retail TouchPoints' Customer Engagement Awards' in 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/features/awards/11-retailers-win-2017-customer-engagement-awards|title=11 Retailers Win 2017 Customer Engagement Awards - Retail TouchPoints|last=Hauss|first=Debbie|website=www.retailtouchpoints.com|date=3 January 2017 |language=en-gb|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref> and 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.retailtouchpoints.com/features/special-reports/2018-customer-engagement-awards|title=2018 Customer Engagement Awards - Retail TouchPoints|website=www.retailtouchpoints.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref> The brand won the Excellence Awards as Best in 2018 Class Omnichannel Experience during Customer Contact Week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.customercontactweekdigital.com/customer-experience/news/2018-ccw-excellence-awards-winners-who-delivers-the-worlds-best-customer-experiences|title=2018 CCW Excellence Awards Winners: Who Delivers The World's Best Customer Experiences?|last=Cantor|first=Brian|date=2018-06-25|website=CCW Digital {{!}} Customer Experience Tips, Research & News|language=en|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref>

In December 2017, the company implemented a hybrid-bot on its website. The hybrid-bot enables Adore Me customers to receive live support via several messaging platforms.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chainstoreage.com/news/adore-customer-service-innovation-facebook/|title=Adore Me in customer service innovation with Facebook {{!}}Chain Store Age|date=2017-11-10|work=Chain Store Age|access-date=2018-11-01|language=en-US}}</ref>

Before securing series B funding, Hermand-Waiche went on record stating that the company had 50,000 members with double that number in visits to the website each month. He stated that the revenue had been increasing by 40 percent each month from January through June 2012. At that time, the company model provided an individual showroom for each customer consisting of "bras, briefs, babydolls, slips, underwear, corsets, bustiers, shapewear,  legwear and swimwear," with the sixth set purchased being free for members.<ref name=":3" />

Once fully funded, reports emerged detailing customer complaints about the implementation of the controversial practice of [[negative option billing]]. Adore Me offered the customers the choice of buying a product at full price or of buying the same product at a substantial discount by joining a membership club.  The club then billed customers a fixed amount each month unless the customer bought lingerie or opted out for the month.  While the membership may be cancelled, the customers have found it difficult to cancel.<ref name="Bloomy">{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2016-adore-me/|title=The Future of Shopping: Trapping You in a Club You Didn't Know You Joined|last1=Greenfield|first1=Rebecca|date=April 28, 2016|accessdate=April 5, 2017|publisher=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]|last2=Bhasin|first2=Kim}}</ref><ref name="BInsider">{{cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/adore-me-shoppers-complain-of-scam-2016-1|title=Furious customers are calling a hot lingerie startup a scam because of its sales model|last1=Schlossberg|first1=Mallory|date=January 12, 2016|accessdate=April 5, 2017|publisher=[[Business Insider]]}}</ref> Customer Kathy Lira filed suit against Adore Me seeking damages, [[Injunction|injunctive relief]], and court costs as [[Restitution and unjust enrichment|restitution]] for the financial damages incurred from having her card automatically billed.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Torres |first=Louis |date=2016-10-17 |title=Woman files class action against AdoreMe |work=Legal Newsline |url=https://legalnewsline.com/stories/511018964-law-courts-woman-files-class-action-against-adoreme |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref> Following an investigation filed by the [[Federal Trade Commission]] about Adore Me's deceptive billing practices, the company agreed to refund up to $1.38 million to customers that had previously forfeited their store credits and to clearly disclose how much customers would pay on its monthly subscription plan.<ref name="NovBloom2017">{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-11-21/lingerie-startup-settles-ftc-suit-over-deceptive-subscriptions|title=Lingerie Startup Settles FTC Suit Over Deceptive Subscriptions, Adore Me is one of many retail startups accused of tricking customers into hard-to-cancel memberships.|last1=Bhasin|first1=Kim|date=November 21, 2017|accessdate=December 3, 2017|publisher=Bloomberg|last2=Greenfield|first2=Rebecca}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Kliot |first1=Hannah |last2=Day |first2=Andrea |last3=Zamost |first3=Scott |last4=Wu |first4=Jasmine |last5=Schlesinger |first5=Jennifer |date=2018-11-19 |title=Buyer beware: Online lingerie retailer Adore Me under fire by FTC over 'deceptive' subscription service |work=[[CNBC]] |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/11/16/locked-in-cnbc-investigates-online-subscription-models.html |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref>

In 2017, Adore Me announced the launch of its scholarship program, offering a $1,000 scholarship to support women pursuing a degree in business. The company began awarding female students who had either started their own business or were planning to do so in the future.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://us.fashionnetwork.com/news/Amid-legal-dispute-Adore-Me-launches-scholarship-program-for-women-in-business,828406.html#.WXd2sdPyvL9|title=Amid legal dispute, Adore Me launches scholarship program for women in business|last=Mantor|first=Cassidy|work=FashionNetwork.com|access-date=2017-09-18|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022, Adore Me became the first US-based lingerie brand to be granted certification by [[B Lab]], a [[Nonprofit organization|nonprofit]] assessing company performance in order to determine [[corporate sustainability]]. Adore Me announced the certification saying they were "on a mission" to make shopping "more accessible to all consumers".<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-09-21 |title=Adore Me Earns Status As The Only U.S. Lingerie Brand Certified as a B Corporation |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/adore-me-earns-status-as-the-only-us-lingerie-brand-certified-as-a-b-corporation-301629743.html |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Daniels |first=Melissa |date=2022-09-21 |title=Adore Me earns B Corp status in push to become more sustainable |work=ModernRetail |publisher=[[Digiday]] |url=https://www.modernretail.co/operations/adore-me-earns-b-corp-status-in-push-to-become-more-sustainable/ |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Nishimura |first=Kate |date=2022-09-21 |title=Adore Me Is Now a B Corp |work=Sourcing Journal |url=https://sourcingjournal.com/sustainability/sustainability-news/adore-me-b-corp-lingerie-intimates-sustainability-nudea-retail-expansion-373221/ |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Roshitsh |first=Kaley |date=2022-09-21 |title=Reformation Backs New Cotton Coalition, Adore Me as B Corp, U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol News: Short Takes |work=[[Women's Wear Daily | WWD]] |url=https://wwd.com/sustainability/business/short-takes-reformation-new-c4-cotton-coalition-adore-me-b-corp-news-september-1235340401/ |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref> The company faces a potential [[Class action|class action lawsuit]] related to the [[Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990|Americans with Disabilities Act]]. As of April 7, 2023, Kevin Yan Luis has filed suit in the Southern District of New York claiming that the site cannot be accessed by the visually impaired.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-19 |title=Class Action Reporter |url=http://www.bankrupt.com/CAR_Public/230419.mbx |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=Class Action Reporter |via=Bankrupt.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Styf |first=Jon |date=2023-04-26 |title=Adore Me class action claims website not accessible to blind, visually impaired users |url=https://topclassactions.com/disability-class-action-lawsuit/adore-me-class-action-claims-website-not-accessible-to-blind-visually-impaired-users/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Top Class Actions |language=en}}</ref> A similar suit filed June 27, 2022 by Marta Hanyzkiewicz was dismissed with prejudice by [[Nina Gershon|Judge Nina Gershon]] on November 21, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-21 |title=PACER Monitor, Case 1:22-cv-03752 |url=https://www.pacermonitor.com/public/case/45047421/Hanyzkiewicz_v_Adore_Me,_Inc |access-date=2023-07-23 |website=[[PACER (law) | PACER]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jewett |first=Abraham |date=2022-07-01 |title=Urban Decay, Adore Me class actions violate Americans with Disabilities Act |url=https://topclassactions.com/disability-class-action-lawsuit/urban-decay-adore-me-class-actions-violate-americans-with-disabilities-act/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Top Class Actions |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, the company was once again sued for deceptive billing practices, this time by thirty-one states and the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]]. Included in the plaintiffs' arguments was that consumers who cancelled their membership in the VIP program were required to forfeit all of the accrued store credits in doing so. These credits had been accumulated through the monthly billing of the VIP program and consumers not having made a purchase between the first and the sixth of the month.<ref>{{Cite web |last=TFL |date=2023-06-20 |title=Adore Me Reaches $2.35M Settlement Over "Deceptive" Marketing |url=https://www.thefashionlaw.com/adoreme-reaches-2-35m-settlement-over-deceptive-marketing/ |access-date=2023-07-18 |website=The Fashion Law |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Stempel |first=Jonathan |date=2023-06-16 |title=Adore Me lingerie retailer settles US states' deceptive billing claims |language=en |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/adore-me-lingerie-retailer-settles-us-states-deceptive-billing-claims-2023-06-16/ |access-date=2023-07-18}}</ref> They settled the case in June 2023 for $2.35 million, to be split amongst the plaintiffs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-09 |title=Settlement Agreement, DocuSign: 0FD3876A-ABD2-4D16-BB17-890B17D27DF8 |url=https://truthinadvertising.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/NC_AdoreMe_Settlement-Agreement.pdf |access-date=2023-07-18 |website=[[Truth in Advertising (organization)]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alegre |first=J. P. |date=2023-06-21 |title=Exposed: Online Lingerie Retailer Pays Millions To Settle Deceptive Marketing Claims |url=https://thedeepdive.ca/exposed-online-lingerie-retailer-pays-millions-to-settle-deceptive-marketing-claims/ |access-date=2023-07-18 |website=the deep dive |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Santoni |first=Matthew |date=2023-06-16 |title=Lingerie Co. Inks $2.3M Deal In 31 States Over Recurring Fees - Law360 |url=https://www.law360.com/articles/1689971/lingerie-co-inks-2-3m-deal-in-31-states-over-recurring-fees |access-date=2023-07-18 |website=www.law360.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Housler |first=Kaitlin |date=2023-06-20 |title=Tennessee AG Skrmetti Secures Settlement Payout from Lawsuit Against Online Retailer |work=[[Tennessee Star]] |url=https://tennesseestar.com/news/tennessee-ag-skrmetti-secures-settlement-payout-from-lawsuit-against-online-retailer/khousler/2023/06/20/ |access-date=2023-07-23}}</ref>

<!--Brief introduction-->'''Amazon.com, Inc.'''<ref name=10K>{{cite web | url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000004/amzn-20241231.htm | title=Amazon.com, Inc. 2024 Form 10-K Annual Report | publisher=[[US Securities and Exchange Commission]] | date=February 7, 2025 | access-date=February 7, 2025 | archive-date=February 7, 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207163728/https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000004/amzn-20241231.htm | url-status=live }}</ref> ([[doing business as]] '''Amazon'''){{efn|{{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|m|ə|z|ɒ|n|audio=LL-Q1860 (eng)-Flame, not lame-Amazon (company).wav}}, {{respell|AM|ə|zon}}; {{IPAc-en|Ukalso|ˈ|æ|m|ə|z|ə|n}}, {{respell|AM|ə|zən}}}} is an American multinational conglomerate engaged in [[e-commerce]], [[retail]], [[cloud computing]], [[online advertising]], [[digital streaming]], [[entertainment]], and [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Amazon Empire: The Rise and Reign of Jeff Bezos|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/documentary/amazon-empire/?|publisher=[[PBS]]|access-date=February 15, 2020|archive-date=January 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116035015/https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/film/amazon-empire/|url-status=live}}</ref> Founded in 1994 by [[Jeff Bezos]] in [[Bellevue, Washington]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Amazon's John Schoettler has helped change how we think of corporate campuses |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417003045/https://www.bizjournals.com/seattle/news/2020/11/17/skyline-shaper-john-schoettler.html |archive-date=April 17, 2021 |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/seattle/news/2020/11/17/skyline-shaper-john-schoettler.html |date=November 17, 2020 |last1=Guevara |first1=Natalie |work=[[Puget Sound Business Journal]] |access-date=March 9, 2021}}</ref> the company started as an online book marketplace that gradually expanded to include virtually all consumer products as well as many other categories, positioned as "The Everything Store".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kakutani|first=Michiko|date=October 28, 2013|title=Selling as Hard as He Can|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/29/books/the-everything-store-jeff-bezos-and-the-age-of-amazon.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029073241/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/29/books/the-everything-store-jeff-bezos-and-the-age-of-amazon.html |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-access=limited|url-status=live|access-date=December 20, 2021|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

As of 2026 it was the world's biggest online [[retailer]]. Amazon sells [[books]], [[electronics]], [[pharmacy|pharmaceuticals]], [[car parts]], [[video games]], [[dining]] products, [[jewelry]], [[food]], [[music]], and [[sports equipment]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Amazon: From Books to Everything|url=https://quartr.com/insights/company-research/amazon-from-books-to-everything|date=June 17, 2024|access-date=17 January 2026|archive-date=January 2, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102133246/https://quartr.com/insights/company-research/amazon-from-books-to-everything|url-status=live}}</ref>

<!--END Brief introduction; do not overload this section with details--><!--Operations and products:-->The company has multiple subsidiaries, including [[Amazon Web Services]] (AWS), which provides cloud computing; [[Zoox (company)|Zoox]], a [[self-driving car]] division; satellite Internet provider [[Kuiper Systems]]; and [[Amazon Lab126]], a computer hardware [[R&D]] provider. Other subsidiaries include [[Ring (company)|Ring]], [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]], [[IMDb]], and grocer [[Whole Foods Market]]. Amazon distributes downloadable and streaming content through its [[Amazon Prime Video]], [[MGM+]], [[Amazon Music]], Twitch, [[Audible (service)|Audible]], and [[Wondery]]<ref>{{cite news |last=Carman |first=Ashley |date=December 30, 2020 |title=Amazon buys Wondery, setting itself up to compete against Spotify for podcast domination |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/30/22098312/amazon-music-wondery-acquire-buy-podcast-industry |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=The Verge |language=en |archive-date=September 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929181931/https://www.theverge.com/2020/12/30/22098312/amazon-music-wondery-acquire-buy-podcast-industry |url-status=live }}</ref> units through its Entertainment division. It publishes books through its publishing arm, [[Amazon Publishing]]; produces and distributes film and television content through [[Amazon MGM Studios]], including the [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] studio; and owns Brilliance Audio and [[Audible (service)|Audible]], which produce and distribute [[audiobook]]s, respectively. Amazon produces consumer electronics, most notably [[Amazon Kindle|Kindle]] e-readers, [[Amazon Echo|Echo]] devices, [[Amazon Fire|Fire]] tablets, and [[Amazon Fire TV|Fire]] TVs.<!--END Operations and products-->

== History ==
{{main|History of Amazon}}

=== 1994–2010 ===
[[File:Amazon's founding site in Bellevue, Washington - exterior.jpg|thumb|right|Jeff Bezos's home in [[Bellevue, Washington]], where the company was founded in 1994]]
On July 5, 1994, Amazon was founded as "Cadabra" by [[Jeff Bezos]], after he relocated from [[New York City]] to [[Bellevue, Washington]], to operate an online bookstore. Bezos chose Seattle for its abundance of technical talent from [[Microsoft]] and the [[University of Washington]], as well as its smaller population and the proximity to a major book distribution warehouse in [[Roseburg, Oregon]]. Seattle beat out [[Portland, Oregon]] and [[Boulder, Colorado]].<ref name="SeattleTimes-25">{{cite news |last=Romano |first=Benjamin |date=June 29, 2019 |title=Amazon at 25: The magic that changed everything |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/amazon-25-the-magic-that-changed-everything/ |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 7, 2024 |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708183908/https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/amazon-25-the-magic-that-changed-everything/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In November 1994, Bezos renamed the company Amazon to reflect his ambitions for his company. (Amazon is the world's largest river.)<ref>{{cite news |last=Spector |first=Robert |date=April 16, 2000 |title=Homegrown Amazon |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=20000416&slug=4015638 |work=The Seattle Times |access-date=July 7, 2024}}</ref>

On July 16, 1995, the Amazon website launched, initially sourcing its books directly from wholesalers and publishers.<ref name="SeattleTimes-25"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Perez |first=Elizabeth |date=June 28, 2019 |title=Store on internet is open book — Amazon.com boasts more than 1 million titles on web |page=E1 |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/store-on-internet-is-open-book-amazon-com-boasts-more-than-1-million-titles-on-web-from-the-archives/ |work=The Seattle Times |access-date=July 7, 2024 |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708183910/https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/store-on-internet-is-open-book-amazon-com-boasts-more-than-1-million-titles-on-web-from-the-archives/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 1997, Amazon went [[public company|public]].<ref name="anders1999a"/><ref name="anders1999b"/>

In 1998, Amazon began selling music and videos. It began international operations by acquiring online booksellers in the UK and Germany. In 1999, it expanded to sell more products, including music, video games, consumer electronics, home improvement items, software, games, and toys.<ref name="anders1999a">{{Cite news |last1=Anders |first1=George |last2=Tessler |first2=Joelle |date=June 8, 1999 |title=Amazon.com Steps Into World Of Online, Downloadable Music |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB92877726979442347 |access-date=September 27, 2022 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927184149/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB92877726979442347 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="anders1999b">{{Cite news |last=Anders |first=George |date=July 13, 1999 |title=Amazon.com Unveils Plans to Open Two More 'Stores' on Its Web Site |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB931823473942188601 |access-date=September 27, 2022 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927184149/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB931823473942188601 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2000, US toy retailer [[Toys "R" Us]] entered into a 10-year agreement with Amazon, valued at $50&nbsp;million per year plus a cut of sales, under which Toys "R" Us would be the exclusive supplier of toys and baby products on the service, and the chain's website would redirect to Amazon's Toys & Games category. In 2004, Toys "R" Us sued Amazon, claiming that because of a perceived lack of variety in Toys "R" Us stock, Amazon had knowingly allowed third-party sellers to offer items on the service in categories that Toys "R" Us had been granted exclusivity. In 2006, a court ruled in favor of Toys "R" Us, giving it the right to unwind its agreement with Amazon and establish its independent e-commerce website. The company was later awarded $51 million in damages.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 18, 2017 |title=Toys R Us bankruptcy: A dot-com-era deal with Amazon marked the beginning of the end |url=https://qz.com/1080389/a-dot-com-era-deal-with-amazon-marked-the-beginning-of-the-end-for-toys-r-us/ |access-date=November 11, 2018 |website=Quartz |language=en |archive-date=November 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119085215/https://qz.com/1080389/a-dot-com-era-deal-with-amazon-marked-the-beginning-of-the-end-for-toys-r-us/ |url-status=live |first=Alison|last=Griswold}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=March 3, 2006 |title=Toys R Us wins Amazon lawsuit |publisher=[[BBC News]] |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/4769896.stm |access-date=December 1, 2012 |archive-date=January 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090129225117/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/4769896.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Metz |first=Rachel |date=June 12, 2009 |title=Amazon to pay Toys R Us $51M to settle suit |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/tech/news/2009-06-12-amazon-toys_N.htm |access-date=December 1, 2012 |archive-date=January 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210102003413/https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/tech/news/2009-06-12-amazon-toys_N.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2001, Amazon entered into a similar agreement with [[Borders (retailer)|Borders]], under which Amazon would comanage Borders.com as a co-branded service.<ref>{{cite news |date=April 11, 2001 |title=Amazon/Borders form online partnership |url=https://money.cnn.com/2001/04/11/companies/amazon/index.htm |access-date=November 11, 2018 |website=CNN Money |archive-date=October 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181016075708/https://money.cnn.com/2001/04/11/companies/amazon/index.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Borders pulled out of the arrangement in 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 13, 2015 |title=How 'Amazon factor' killed retailers like Borders, Circuit City |work=SFGate |url=https://www.sfgate.com/business/article/How-Amazon-factor-killed-retailers-like-6378619.php |access-date=November 11, 2018 |archive-date=November 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111133859/https://www.sfgate.com/business/article/How-Amazon-factor-killed-retailers-like-6378619.php |url-status=live |first=Benny |last=Evangelista}}</ref>

In 2002, the company launched [[Amazon Web Services]] (AWS), which initially focused on providing APIs for web developers to build [[web application]]s on top of Amazon's [[e-commerce]] platform.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=July 16, 2002 |title=Amazon.com Launches Web Services; Developers Can Now Incorporate Amazon.com Content and Features into Their Own Web Sites; Extends ''Welcome Mat'' for Developers |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazoncom-launches-web-services |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |archive-date= 2022-09-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927192432/https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazoncom-launches-web-services/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release |date=March 19, 2003 |title=Amazon.com Web Services Announces Trio of Milestones - New Tool Kit, Enhanced Web Site and 25,000 Developers in the Program |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazoncom-web-services-announces-trio-milestones-new-tool-kit |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927192430/https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazoncom-web-services-announces-trio-milestones-new-tool-kit |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2004, AWS expanded to provide website popularity statistics and web crawler data from its Alexa Web Information Service.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=October 4, 2004 |title=New Amazon Web Services Offerings Give Developers Unprecedented Access to Amazon Product Data and Technology, and First-Ever Access to Data Compiled by Alexa Internet |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/new-amazon-web-services-offerings-give-developers-unprecedented |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927192431/https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/new-amazon-web-services-offerings-give-developers-unprecedented |url-status=live }}</ref> AWS later shifted toward providing enterprise services with [[Amazon S3|Simple Storage Service]] (S3) in 2006,<ref>{{Cite press release |date=March 14, 2006 |title=Amazon Web Services Launches |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazon-web-services-launches-amazon-s3-simple-storage-service |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |archive-date=December 16, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251216213157/https://press.aboutamazon.com/2006/3/amazon-web-services-launches |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud|Elastic Compute Cloud]] (EC2) in 2008, allowing companies to rent data storage and computing power.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=October 23, 2008 |title=Amazon Web Services Launches Amazon EC2 for Windows |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazon-web-services-launches-amazon-ec2-windows |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |quote=Additionally, AWS today announced that Amazon EC2 is now Generally Available, having successfully exited its beta period and now offers a Service Level Agreement (SLA) |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927192429/https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazon-web-services-launches-amazon-ec2-windows |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2006, Amazon launched the'' Fulfillment by Amazon ''program, which allowed individuals and small companies (called "third-party sellers") to sell products through Amazon's warehouses and fulfillment infrastructure.<ref name=amazon-fulfill-press>{{Cite press release |date=September 19, 2006 |title=Amazon Launches New Services to Help Small and Medium-Sized Businesses Enhance Their Customer Offerings by Accessing Amazon's Order Fulfillment, Customer Service, and Website Functionality |url=https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazon-launches-new-services-help-small-and-medium-sized |access-date=September 27, 2022 |publisher=Amazon.com Press Center |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927192433/https://press.aboutamazon.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amazon-launches-new-services-help-small-and-medium-sized |url-status=live }}</ref>

In March 2008, Amazon bought Audible for about $300&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |author=Sayer, Peter |date=January 31, 2008 |title=Amazon buys Audible for US$300 million |work=PC World |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/01/31/AR2008013101662.html |access-date=August 24, 2017 |archive-date=May 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170530160655/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/01/31/AR2008013101662.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The AmazonBasics brand was introduced in 2009, offering a range of Amazon-branded products.<ref name=":4" />

In June 2010, Amazon Seller Product Suggestions was launched.<ref name=":5" />

=== 2011–2020<!-- should be expanded and talk about Amazon's growth -->===
On October 18, 2011, Amazon.com announced a partnership with [[DC Comics]] for the exclusive digital rights to many popular comics, including ''[[Superman]]'', ''[[Batman]]'', ''[[Green Lantern]]'', ''[[Sandman (comics)|Sandman]]'', and ''[[Watchmen]]''. The partnership caused booksellers such as [[Barnes & Noble]] to remove these titles from its shelves.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Streitfeld |first=David |date=October 18, 2011 |title=Bookstores Drop Comics After Amazon Deal With DC |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/19/technology/bookstores-drop-comics-after-amazon-deal-with-dc.html |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=February 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111018234650/http://www.nytimes.com/2011/10/19/technology/bookstores-drop-comics-after-amazon-deal-with-dc.html |archive-date=October 18, 2011 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Amazon acquired [[Kiva Systems]], a warehouse automation company, in 2012.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

Amazon bought [[Goodreads]] in March 2013.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Leslie |date=March 28, 2013 |title=Amazon to Buy Social Site Dedicated to Sharing Books |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/29/business/media/amazon-to-buy-goodreads.html |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=February 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130329013203/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/29/business/media/amazon-to-buy-goodreads.html |archive-date=March 29, 2013 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

In November 2013, Amazon announced a partnership with the [[United States Postal Service|US Postal Service]] to begin delivering orders on Sundays. The service, included in Amazon's standard shipping rates, initiated in metropolitan areas of [[Greater Los Angeles]] and [[New York metropolitan area|New York]], with plans to expand into [[Dallas]], [[Houston]], [[New Orleans]] and [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] by 2014.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barr |first=Alistair |date=November 11, 2013 |title=Amazon starts Sunday delivery with US Postal Service |work=USA Today |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/2013/11/11/amazon-sunday-delivery-usps/3479055/ |access-date=November 25, 2013 |archive-date=November 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131121075007/http://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/2013/11/11/amazon-sunday-delivery-usps/3479055/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Amazon acquired [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] in August 2014 for $970&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |last=Welch |first=Chris |date=August 25, 2014 |title=Amazon, not Google, is buying Twitch for $970 million |url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/8/25/6066295/amazon-reportedly-buying-twitch-for-over-1-billion |access-date=August 8, 2017 |website=The Verge |archive-date=July 19, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160719225746/http://www.theverge.com/2014/8/25/6066295/amazon-reportedly-buying-twitch-for-over-1-billion |url-status=live }}</ref>

In November 2015, Amazon opened a physical [[Amazon Books]] store in [[University Village, Seattle|University Village]] in [[Seattle]]. The store was 5,500 square feet and prices for all products matched those on its website.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-plans-hundreds-of-brick-and-mortar-bookstores-mall-ceo-says-1454449475|title=Amazon Plans Hundreds of Brick-and-Mortar Bookstores, Mall CEO Says|last=Bensinger|first=Greg|date=February 2, 2016|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|access-date=February 20, 2019|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660|archive-date=February 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212191635/https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-plans-hundreds-of-brick-and-mortar-bookstores-mall-ceo-says-1454449475|url-status=live}}</ref> Amazon opened its tenth physical bookstore in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.recode.net/2017/3/8/14850324/amazon-books-store-bellevue-mall-expansion |title=Amazon just confirmed its tenth bookstore, signaling this is way more than an experiment |first=Jason Del |last=Rey |date=March 8, 2017 |website=Recode |access-date=May 12, 2017 |archive-date=March 23, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170323051235/https://www.recode.net/2017/3/8/14850324/amazon-books-store-bellevue-mall-expansion |url-status=live }}</ref>  All locations were closed in 2022 along with other retail locations under the "Amazon 4-Star" brand.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rosenblatt |first=Lauren |date=March 2, 2022 |title=Turning the page on a bookstore push launched in Seattle, Amazon ditches dozens of brick-and-mortar shops |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/turning-the-page-on-a-bookstore-push-launched-in-seattle-amazon-ditches-dozens-of-brick-and-mortar-shops/ |work=The Seattle Times |access-date=March 21, 2024 |archive-date=March 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322034945/https://www.seattletimes.com/business/amazon/turning-the-page-on-a-bookstore-push-launched-in-seattle-amazon-ditches-dozens-of-brick-and-mortar-shops/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In July 2016, the company announced that it was opening a {{cvt|1,100,000|ft|m|1}} square foot facility in [[Palmer Township, Pennsylvania|Palmer Township]] in the [[Lehigh Valley]] region of eastern [[Pennsylvania]]. {{As of|2024}}, Amazon is the Lehigh Valley region's third-largest employer.<ref>[https://www.lehighvalley.org/amazon-opening-new-lehigh-valley-facility-creating-over-500-new-jobs/ "Amazon opening new Lehigh Valley facility, creating over 500 new jobs"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240217092609/https://www.lehighvalley.org/amazon-opening-new-lehigh-valley-facility-creating-over-500-new-jobs/ |date=February 17, 2024 }}, Lehigh Valley Economic Development</ref><ref>[https://www.lehighvalley.org/about-lehigh-valley/lehigh-valley-s-largest-private-sector-employers/ "Lehigh Valley's Largest Private-Sector Employers"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229142719/https://www.lehighvalley.org/about-lehigh-valley/lehigh-valley-s-largest-private-sector-employers/ |date=December 29, 2023 }}, Lehigh Valley Economic Development</ref>

In June 2017, [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] agreed to sell products through Amazon in exchange for better policing of counterfeit goods.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nike confirms 'pilot' partnership with Amazon Amazon purchased [[Whole Foods Market]] supermarket chain for $13.7 billion in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Amazon.com - History & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Amazoncom |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |archive-date=June 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190608125826/https://www.britannica.com/topic/Amazoncom |url-status=live }}</ref> It had over 300 million active customer accounts as of 2020.<ref>{{Citation |last=Schmidt |first=Gordon B. |title=Amazon |date=2020 |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.4135/9781483375519.n28 |encyclopedia=The SAGE International Encyclopedia of Mass Media and Society |access-date=May 1, 2023 |place=Thousand Oaks, California|publisher=SAGE Publications, Inc. |language=en |doi=10.4135/9781483375519.n28 |isbn=978-1-4833-7551-9|s2cid=240656642 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kelleher |first=Kevin |date=August 28, 2017 |title=Amazon closes Whole Foods acquisition.
