======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Cultural impact of TikTok
======================================================================

{{Short description|Cultural impact of the video sharing app}}{{Multiple issues|{{More citations needed|date=July 2026}}
{{Copy edit|date=July 2026}}{{Update|date=July 2026}}}}[[File:TikTok_logo.svg|thumb|Logo of TikTok|250px]]
The online video platform [[TikTok]] has had worldwide a social, political, and cultural impact since its global launch in September 2016. The platform has rapidly grown its userbase since its launch and surpassed 2 billion downloads in October 2020. It became the world's most popular website, ahead of [[Google]], for the year 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rosenblatt |first1=Kalhan |title=TikTok surpasses Google as most popular website of the year, new data suggests |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/tiktok-surpasses-google-popular-website-year-new-data-suggests-rcna9648 |website=NBC News |access-date=1 October 2023 |language=en |date=23 December 2021 |archive-date=20 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920105331/https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/tiktok-surpasses-google-popular-website-year-new-data-suggests-rcna9648 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Cultural impact==
===Music===
TikTok has been noted by many media outlets as having a major influence in the music industry. American artist [[Lil Nas X]] notably rose to fame after his song "[[Old Town Road]]" went viral on TikTok in 2019. He acknowledged the platform's influence in popularizing the song, saying "[TikTok] really boosted the song ... I credit them a lot".<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Shafer |first=Ellise |date=2019-07-29 |title=Started on TikTok, Now We're Here: A Look Back at the Meme-Tastic Beginning of Lil Nas X's 'Old Town Road' |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-tiktok-beginning-8524319/ |access-date=2023-11-03 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-11-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103131430/https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-tiktok-beginning-8524319/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2019-03-30 |title=Lil Nas X on "Old Town Road" and the Billboard Controversy |url=https://time.com/5561466/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard/ |access-date=2023-11-03 |magazine=Time |language=en |archive-date=2019-10-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011091057/https://time.com/5561466/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Doja Cat]] has also been noted as an artist who achieved mainstream popularity thanks to her success on TikTok. [[Insider Inc.|Insider]] noted in 2020 that "one of the most popular, pervasive dances of all time" from TikTok was set to [[Say So]], which became her first no.1 hit on the [[Billboard Hot 100]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tenbarge |first=Kat |title=Doja Cat harnessed viral moments to reach no. 1 on Billboard, but her online past has also resulted in controversial moments for the 'Say So' singer |url=https://www.insider.com/doja-cat-songs-bio-famous-tiktok-dance-say-so-2020-3 |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=Insider |date=25 May 2020 |language=en-US |archive-date=2020-05-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200527034131/https://www.insider.com/doja-cat-songs-bio-famous-tiktok-dance-say-so-2020-3 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] also noted Doja Cat's "astonishing, unprecedented TikTok reign", saying that before her fame on TikTok, "many people didn't fully register Doja Cat as a star".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-18 |title=The Mystery of Doja Cat's Unimpeachable TikTok Reign |url=https://pitchfork.com/thepitch/the-mystery-of-doja-cats-unimpeachable-tiktok-reign/ |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418161650/https://pitchfork.com/thepitch/the-mystery-of-doja-cats-unimpeachable-tiktok-reign/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

When it was launched, TikTok allowed users to upload videos that ranged from 3 seconds to 1 minute. The short video length limit led to users making [[nightcore|sped-up versions of songs]] to use in their videos. This allowed them to fit more of the song in their video.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Sarah |title=TikTok users are demanding that musicians release sped-up songs |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/viral/tiktok-sped-up-fast-songs-sounds-rcna79256 |quote="Fast songs allow users to fit more of their favorite tunes in their TikTok videos." |website=NBC News |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |date=22 April 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103181053/https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/viral/tiktok-sped-up-fast-songs-sounds-rcna79256 |url-status=live }}</ref> Some artists, including [[SZA]] and [[Steve Lacy]], released official sped-up versions of their songs after unofficial sped-up remixes of their songs went viral on the platform.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Conor |title=Why Sped-Up Music—From SZA, Steve Lacy And Many More—Took Over TikTok And Became A Key Marketing Strategy |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2023/01/18/why-sped-up-music-from-sza-steve-lacy-and-many-more-took-over-tiktok-and-became-a-key-marketing-strategy/?sh=754e87dd77e0 |website=Forbes |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103181053/https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2023/01/18/why-sped-up-music-from-sza-steve-lacy-and-many-more-took-over-tiktok-and-became-a-key-marketing-strategy/?sh=754e87dd77e0 |url-status=live }}</ref>

TikTok has also helped popularize older songs. [[Fleetwood Mac]]'s song ''[[Dreams (Fleetwood Mac song)|Dreams]]'' re-entered the Billboard Hot 100 over 40 years after its release after a video that featured the song went viral on the platform.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Zellner |first1=Xander |title=Fleetwood Mac's 'Dreams' Charts on Hot 100 For First Time since 1977, Thanks to TikTok Revival |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/fleetwood-mac-dreams-returns-hot-100/ |magazine=Billboard |access-date=3 November 2023 |date=13 October 2020 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103232640/https://www.billboard.com/pro/fleetwood-mac-dreams-returns-hot-100/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Dan Whateley from Insider noted that songs could "rise up organically on the app even if they've been outside the mainstream for decades".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whateley |first=Dan |title=How TikTok is changing the music industry and the way we discover new, popular songs |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/how-tiktok-is-changing-music-industry |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109013543/https://www.businessinsider.com/how-tiktok-is-changing-music-industry |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2023, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' and TikTok launched a new chart called the ''[[TikTok Billboard Top 50]]'' to track music that is popular on the platform in the United States.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roth |first1=Emma |title=TikTok is tracking its most popular songs with a Billboard top 50 chart |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/14/23873516/billboard-tiktok-top-50-chart-songs |website=The Verge |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |date=14 September 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103182258/https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/14/23873516/billboard-tiktok-top-50-chart-songs |url-status=live }}</ref>

Some artists have complained of a "burnout" due to TikTok's massive role in the music marketing process.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Venkat |first=Mia |date=May 22, 2022 |title=TikTok has changed music — and the industry is hustling to catch up |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/05/22/1080632810/tiktok-music-industry-gayle-abcdefu-sia-tai-verdes-celine-dion |website=Insider |access-date=November 3, 2023 |archive-date=November 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103131428/https://www.npr.org/2022/05/22/1080632810/tiktok-music-industry-gayle-abcdefu-sia-tai-verdes-celine-dion |url-status=live }}</ref> American singer [[Halsey (singer)|Halsey]] said in 2022 that her label was stopping her from releasing a new song if she didn't agree to "fake a viral moment on TikTok".<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2022-05-23 |title=Halsey Is the Latest Artist Complaining About the Music Industry's Reliance on TikTok |url=https://time.com/6180377/halsey-tiktok-label/ |access-date=2023-11-03 |magazine=Time |language=en |archive-date=2022-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831160223/https://time.com/6180377/halsey-tiktok-label/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Thania |date=2022-05-23 |title=Halsey's Label Responds to Singer's TikTok Claim That They Won't Release New Song |url=https://variety.com/2022/music/news/halsey-tiktok-label-responds-1235275187/ |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-08-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220819053233/https://variety.com/2022/music/news/halsey-tiktok-label-responds-1235275187/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Additionally, in February 2024, TikTok experienced a temporary removal of music from [[Universal Music Group|Universal Music Group (UMG)]] due to a licensing dispute over royalty payments, which UMG argued undervalued their catalog compared to a typical "[[pay-per-view]]" royalty model in streaming services.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2025-03-05 |title=What Happened When TikTok Songs Went Silent for Three Months {{!}} Working Knowledge |url=https://www.library.hbs.edu/working-knowledge/what-happened-when-tiktok-songs-went-silent-for-three-months |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=Harvard Business School |language=en-us}}</ref> Existing videos using UMG tracks were muted, creating a "radio silence" effect. According to [[Harvard Business School]] professor Elie Ofek, "when UMG removed its music, artists with partial catalog presence on TikTok saw a 1–3 percent decrease in streams on other platforms for their songs that weren’t previously available on TikTok."<ref name=":4" /> While major artists were affected, some smaller independent artists gained visibility and traction on the platform without competition from UMG's catalog. After 3 months the two companies reached an agreement, and the music was restored to the platform on May 1, 2024.

===News and information===
TikTok is becoming a growing source of news for Americans. [[Pew Research Center]] found that the percentage of US adults who regularly got their news from TikTok more than tripled from 3% of US adults in 2020, to 10% in 2022, and now 14% in 2023. The percentage of US adult TikTok users who regularly get their news from the platform increased from 22% to 33% in the same time period. This is much lower than the percentage of Facebook and Twitter users who regularly get their news from those platforms. However, unlike with TikTok, the proportion of Facebook and Twitter users who get their news from those platforms declined every year from 2020 to 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Matsa |first1=Katerina Eva |title=More Americans are getting news on TikTok, bucking the trend on other social media sites |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/10/21/more-americans-are-getting-news-on-tiktok-bucking-the-trend-on-other-social-media-sites/ |website=Pew Research Center |access-date=3 November 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103154409/https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/10/21/more-americans-are-getting-news-on-tiktok-bucking-the-trend-on-other-social-media-sites/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

An increasing proportion of [[Generation Z]] internet users have also started using TikTok as their preferred [[search engine]] over [[Google]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carbonaro |first1=Giulia |title=Is TikTok about to replace Google as the top search engine? |url=https://www.euronews.com/next/2023/02/05/gen-z-is-using-tiktok-as-a-search-engine-is-this-the-end-of-google |website=euronews |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |date=5 February 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103155400/https://www.euronews.com/next/2023/02/05/gen-z-is-using-tiktok-as-a-search-engine-is-this-the-end-of-google |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Politics ===
{{Globalise section|1=the United States|date=July 2026}}
As the popularity of TikTok grows, more and more individuals join the platform. Hence, current political ideologies are being spread on the platform. TikTok has turned into a political landscape, where young individuals are consuming far-right related content on a daily basis. TikTok has allowed for far-right supporters to have a platform where radical views are naturalized. Statistics have shown that roughly 14% of adults regularly get their election and political news through the platform.<ref name="Seshagiri">{{Cite news |last1=Seshagiri |first1=Ashwin |last2=Dang |first2=Mike |last3=Hartocollis |first3=Anemona |last4=Hill |first4=Kashmir |last5=Hughes |first5=Becky |last6=Nerkar |first6=Santul |last7=Holman |first7=Jordyn |last8=Grynbaum |first8=Michael M. |last9=Barry |first9=Ellen |date=2024-04-19 |title=Love, Hate or Fear It: TikTok Has Changed America |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/04/18/business/media/tiktok-ban-american-culture.html |access-date=2024-11-30 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> TikTok has addressed multiple times that hateful content, related to far-right ideologies, is being banned and removed from their platform.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Ozduzen |first1=Ozge |last2=Ferenczi |first2=Nelli |last3=Holmes |first3=Isabel |date=2023-10-20 |title='Let us teach our children': Online racism and everyday far-right ideologies on TikTok |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1472586X.2023.2274890 |journal=Visual Studies |language=en |volume=38 |issue=5 |pages=834–850 |doi=10.1080/1472586X.2023.2274890 |issn=1472-586X}}</ref> However, most hateful content (related to religion, identity, race) have gone unnoticed by the system until December 2019. Although user protection has improved, hateful videos still go undetected by the platform. In light of recent political tensions on the app, the usage of violent commentary has been more prevalent on the app, more-so from the left wing commenters. An article that evaluated the level of politically violent comments on the app concluded that leftist content also alienates what is perceived as the "enemy" at larger rates and even are more likely to make violent references as well.<ref>{{Citation |last=Marinos |first=Martin |chapter=Labor, Money, and the “Populist” in Right-Wing Populist Media |date=2023-11-21 |title=Free to Hate |pages=197–228 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.5622/illinois/9780252045509.003.0007 |access-date=2025-10-20 |publisher=University of Illinois Press |isbn=978-0-252-04550-9}}</ref> Additionally, those comments were statistically less inclined to express religious beliefs openly. On the flip side, right wing content relies more heavily on toxicity to spread a message and gain more views.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Biswas |first=Ahana |last2=Javadian Sabet |first2=Alireza |last3=Lin |first3=Yu-Ru |date=2025-08-20 |title=Toxic politics and TikTok engagement in the 2024 U.S. election |url=https://doi.org/10.37016/mr-2020-181 |journal=Harvard Kennedy School Misinformation Review |doi=10.37016/mr-2020-181|doi-access=free }}</ref> Additionally, since TikTok functions on an algorithmic system, individuals can get more exposure to hateful content without intending to do so.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Weimann |first1=Gabriel |last2=Masri |first2=Natalie |date=2023-05-04 |title=Research Note: Spreading Hate on TikTok |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1057610X.2020.1780027 |journal=Studies in Conflict & Terrorism |language=en |volume=46 |issue=5 |pages=752–765 |doi=10.1080/1057610X.2020.1780027 |issn=1057-610X |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

There is also a large aspect of political misinformation that is apparent on the app. Every social media app is susceptible of misinformation as it is a platform for anyone to post any opinion, or recall of events. Tactics such as sensational headlines, hyperbolic language, and emotional triggers all aid in gaining the attention of viewers<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Biswas |first=Ahana |last2=Javadian Sabet |first2=Alireza |last3=Lin |first3=Yu-Ru |date=2025-08-20 |title=Toxic politics and TikTok engagement in the 2024 U.S. election |url=https://doi.org/10.37016/mr-2020-181 |journal=Harvard Kennedy School Misinformation Review |doi=10.37016/mr-2020-181|doi-access=free }}</ref> Moving forward, politicians have been utilizing TikTok as a tactic for spreading messages and persuading younger generations that are very active on the app. For example, in the last presidential race, the top two contenders created TikTok accounts in hopes of capitalizing off of the slang and humor that GenZ is familiar with on the app. Both candidates followed through with this idea as a way to give more visibility of their campaigns and de-influence younger voters from the opposing candidate.<ref>https://www.gmfus.org/news/tiktok-2024-us-presidential-race-trending-campaign-strategy-or-passing-trend</ref> Studies have shown that a heavy presence of politics on the app sways political identities of users on the app on various levels. A study was conducted that concluded that approximately one third of the total participants claimed that their political identity had changed a significant amount after using TikTok on a regular basis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Church |first=Lauren |date=2022 |title=TikTok's Impact on Political Identity Among Young Adults in the United States |url=https://hdl.handle.net/1794/27281 |language=en-US}}</ref> Moving further through identity the focus is aimed at Black Americans and their participation in routines on TikTok to boycott and Buycott markets in attempts to advance politics surrounding race. These routines were done in efforts to claim and build identity and promote equality.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Li |first=Minjie |date=2024-03-11 |title=TikTok and Black political consumerism: Investigating how TikTok use is linked to Black Americans' activism and identity |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/17513057.2024.2320928 |journal=Journal of International and Intercultural Communication |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=145–171 |doi=10.1080/17513057.2024.2320928 |issn=1751-3057|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===Food===
{{See also|TikTok food trends}}
TikTok content is able to influence the food choices of its users. A 2023 study of [[teenagers]] found that TikTok content influences both short-term food decisions, such as trying a new food item or recipe, and long-term food decisions, like dietary adjustments.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Wang |first1=Chun-Han |last2=Sher |first2=Stephen Tsung-Han |last3=Salman |first3=Isabela |last4=Janek |first4=Kelly |last5=Chung |first5=Chia-Fang |title="TikTok Made Me Do It": Teenagers' Perception and Use of Food Content on TikTok |date=27 June 2022 |pages=458–463 |doi=10.1145/3501712.3535290 |isbn=978-1-4503-9197-9 |s2cid=249993417 |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3501712.3535290 |access-date=5 November 2023 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105163835/https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3501712.3535290 |url-status=live }}</ref>

TikTok has also led to an increase in custom orders at restaurants, known on the platform as [[menu hack]]s. In 2021, some [[Starbucks]] baristas complained of an increase in complicated, custom drinks being ordered that were not on its menu after videos of the custom drinks went viral on TikTok.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Castrodale |first1=Jelisa |title=Starbucks Baristas Are Sick of Your Ridiculous Custom Orders |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/your-off-menu-custom-tiktok-starbucks-drinks-are-exhausting-baristas/ |website=Vice |access-date=5 November 2023 |language=en |date=7 May 2021 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105163834/https://www.vice.com/en/article/3aqqyw/your-off-menu-custom-tiktok-starbucks-drinks-are-exhausting-baristas |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Schwab |first1=Kristin |title=TikTok menu hacks bring chaos and cash to fast food |url=https://www.marketplace.org/2023/04/05/tiktok-menu-hacks-fast-food/ |website=Marketplace |access-date=5 November 2023 |date=5 April 2023 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105163836/https://www.marketplace.org/2023/04/05/tiktok-menu-hacks-fast-food/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, [[Chipotle Mexican Grill]] added a viral TikTok custom order created by two influencers as a permanent item to its menu after receiving an influx of orders for the item.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Luna |first1=Nancy |title=Chipotle turns viral TikTok food hack into a new quesadilla menu item |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/chipotle-tiktok-food-hack-new-fajita-quesadilla-menu-2023-2 |website=Business Insider |access-date=5 November 2023 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105163834/https://www.businessinsider.com/chipotle-tiktok-food-hack-new-fajita-quesadilla-menu-2023-2 |url-status=live }}</ref> The same year, several videos of different [[Waffle House]] branches refusing to serve custom orders from TikTok went viral on the platform.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Waffle House sandwich hack went viral on TikTok. Many workers aren't happy about it |url=https://www.today.com/food/trends/waffle-house-sandwich-hack-viral-tiktok-worker-backlash-rcna66160 |website=TODAY.com |access-date=5 November 2023 |language=en |date=18 January 2023 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105163835/https://www.today.com/food/trends/waffle-house-sandwich-hack-viral-tiktok-worker-backlash-rcna66160 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Fashion===
{{See also|Internet aesthetics}}
The wide audience that TikTok videos are able to reach compared to other platforms allows just a small number of viral videos about a similar style of clothing to create a new microtrend. The high quantity of new microtrends produced by TikTok users has increased the popularity of [[fast fashion]] retailers such as [[Shein]], who are able to rapidly reproduce and sell items that are trending on TikTok.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jennings |first1=Rebecca |title=Fashion is just TikTok now |url=https://www.vox.com/the-goods/22911116/tiktok-couture-fashion-trends |website=Vox |access-date=2 November 2023 |language=en |date=1 February 2022 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221232547/https://www.vox.com/the-goods/22911116/tiktok-couture-fashion-trends |url-status=live }}</ref> Fashion trends and fads that have become popular through social media platforms have collectively become known as "internet aesthetics".

[[Haul videos]] are popular amongst TikTok fashion creators.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Jones |first1=C. T. |title=How 'Dupe' Culture Took Over Online Fashion |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/dupe-culture-fast-fashion-tiktok-1234591964/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=1 October 2023 |date=15 September 2022 |archive-date=20 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920044832/https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/dupe-culture-fast-fashion-tiktok-1234591964/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Shein successfully worked with influencers on TikTok and Instagram to grow its business by sending them free clothing and discount codes to share with their followers that earn them a [[affiliate marketing|commission on sales]]. Influencers are also paid to post haul videos for Shein with the free clothing.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Vara |first1=Vauhini |title=Fast, Cheap, and Out of Control: Inside Shein's Sudden Rise |url=https://www.wired.com/story/fast-cheap-out-of-control-inside-rise-of-shein/ |magazine=Wired |access-date=2 November 2023 |archive-date=2 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102091134/https://www.wired.com/story/fast-cheap-out-of-control-inside-rise-of-shein/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The popularity of haul videos on TikTok also results in users advertising Shein for free by making and posting their own Shein haul.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nguyen |first1=Terry |title=Shein is the future of fast fashion. Is that a good thing? |url=https://www.vox.com/the-goods/22573682/shein-future-of-fast-fashion-explained |website=Vox |access-date=2 November 2023 |language=en |date=13 July 2021 |quote=In fact, it has cemented its reputation among regular people, particularly Gen Z shoppers, who promote the brand through unsponsored clothing hauls and outfit posts on social media. |archive-date=2 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220102124820/https://www.vox.com/the-goods/22573682/shein-future-of-fast-fashion-explained |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Cosmetic surgery===
Videos about cosmetic surgery are very popular on TikTok.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Long |first1=Emily A. |last2=Shiah |first2=Eric |last3=Lin |first3=Samuel J. |title=TikTok: Is It Time to Start Trending with #PlasticSurgery? |journal=Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery |date=June 2023 |volume=151 |issue=6 |pages=1043e–1050e |doi=10.1097/PRS.0000000000010121 |pmid=36728791 |s2cid=256501822 |url=https://journals.lww.com/plasreconsurg/abstract/2023/06000/tiktok__is_it_time_to_start_trending_with.42.aspx |access-date=4 November 2023 |quote=Videos about plastic surgery, particularly educational videos by board-certified plastic surgeons, perform exceptionally well on the TikTok platform. |archive-date=4 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104183635/https://journals.lww.com/plasreconsurg/abstract/2023/06000/tiktok__is_it_time_to_start_trending_with.42.aspx |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In January 2022, videos with hashtags related to plastic surgery had over 29 billion views combined on the platform.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rivera |first1=JC |last2=Juan |first2=HY |last3=Long |first3=AS |last4=Hauc |first4=SC |last5=Junn |first5=AH |last6=Persing |first6=JA |last7=Alperovich |first7=M |title=Presence of Cosmetic and Aesthetic Surgery on TikTok. |journal=Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery. Global Open |date=September 2022 |volume=10 |issue=9 |article-number=e4519 |doi=10.1097/GOX.0000000000004519 |pmid=36168605|pmc=9509022 |doi-access=free }}</ref> TikTok and Instagram have led to an increase in the number of cosmetic surgeries performed on young people.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bushak |first1=Lecia |title=Selfies, social media driving up rates of cosmetic surgeries among young people |url=https://www.mmm-online.com/home/channel/selfies-social-media-driving-up-rates-of-cosmetic-surgeries-among-young-people/ |website=MM+M - Medical Marketing and Media |access-date=2 November 2023 |date=25 August 2023 |archive-date=2 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102222522/https://www.mmm-online.com/home/channel/selfies-social-media-driving-up-rates-of-cosmetic-surgeries-among-young-people/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2021, ''[[Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery]]'' published an article that found that [[plastic surgery|plastic surgeons]] were among the earliest adopters of social media and at the time the article was published, it was found that at least five plastic surgeons had surpassed 1 million followers on TikTok. The article noted that some surgeons were influencers on the platform and had the ability to influence public perception.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das |first1=Rishub K. |last2=Drolet |first2=Brian C. |title=Plastic Surgeons in TikTok: Top Influencers, Most Recent Posts, and User Engagement |journal=Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery |date=December 2021 |volume=148 |issue=6 |pages=1094e–1097e |doi=10.1097/PRS.0000000000008566 |pmid=34705755 |issn=0032-1052 |doi-access=free }}</ref> A 2021 study published by the [[University of South Florida]] found that content posted on TikTok by plastic surgeons helped legitimize plastic surgery by educating their viewers and reducing their fear of the surgeries.<ref name=":2" /> Plastic surgery is also legitimized by the TikTok recommendation system which shows users who showed interest in plastic surgery videos even more plastic surgery videos via the For You Page, which makes plastic surgery seem more widespread than it actually is among both celebrities and normal people.<ref name=":2">{{cite journal |last1=Rach |first1=Markus |title=The impact of TikTok's plastic surgery content on adolescents' self-perception and purchase intention |journal=Advances in Global Services and Retail Management |date=2021 |volume=2 |pages=1–13 |doi=10.5038/9781955833035 |url=https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1144&context=m3publishing |access-date=14 October 2023 |publisher=USF M3 Publishing |isbn=978-1-955833-03-5 |doi-access=free |hdl=11590/391779 |hdl-access=free |archive-date=2023-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108013058/https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1144&context=m3publishing |url-status=live }}</ref>

TikTok does not allow direct paid advertisements of cosmetic surgeries on its platform, but cosmetic surgery clinics are able to promote their services using normal unpaid posts, as well as by paying influencers or giving them free surgeries in exchange for the influencer posting a video about their cosmetic surgery experience.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tenbarge |first1=Kat |title=Young influencers are being offered cheap procedures in return for promotion. They say it's coming at a cost. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/internet/followers-cheaper-lips-young-influencers-detail-allure-cosmetic-proced-rcna14463 |website=NBC News |access-date=2 November 2023 |language=en |date=27 April 2022 |archive-date=12 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230912071816/https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/internet/followers-cheaper-lips-young-influencers-detail-allure-cosmetic-proced-rcna14463 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Cosmetic procedures that have trended on TikTok include [[rhinoplasty|rhinoplasties]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zitser |first1=Joshua |title=Insider created a TikTok account and set the age at 14 to test how long before a plastic surgeon's promotional video appeared. It only took 8 minutes. |url=https://www.insider.com/rhinoplasty-is-being-promoted-to-teenagers-nose-job-tiktok-2020-12 |website=Insider |access-date=2 November 2023 |quote=#NoseJobCheck has over one billion views on the social media platform. |archive-date=15 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215065205/https://www.insider.com/rhinoplasty-is-being-promoted-to-teenagers-nose-job-tiktok-2020-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[buccal fat removal]]s,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rosenblatt |first1=Kalhan |title=Buccal fat removal surgery videos have gone viral on TikTok but with pushback |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/buccal-fat-removal-surgery-videos-tiktok-rcna62317 |website=NBC News |access-date=2 November 2023 |language=en |date=20 December 2022 |archive-date=26 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326030949/https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/buccal-fat-removal-surgery-videos-tiktok-rcna62317 |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[botox]] injections.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bushak |first1=Lecia |title='Brotox' takes over TikTok: Why more men are getting cosmetic surgery |url=https://www.mmm-online.com/home/channel/brotox-takes-over-tiktok-why-more-men-are-getting-cosmetic-surgery/ |website=MM+M - Medical Marketing and Media |access-date=2 November 2023 |date=10 April 2023 |archive-date=2 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102220454/https://www.mmm-online.com/home/channel/brotox-takes-over-tiktok-why-more-men-are-getting-cosmetic-surgery/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Cosmetic procedures sometimes trend in the form of an [[internet challenge]] on TikTok. The "#Nosejobcheck" challenge involves users posting videos of their noses before and after their rhinoplasties, with a specific background sound for the challenge used in the videos.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zitser |first1=Joshua |title=Insider created a TikTok account and set the age at 14 to test how long before a plastic surgeon's promotional video appeared. It only took 8 minutes. |url=https://www.insider.com/rhinoplasty-is-being-promoted-to-teenagers-nose-job-tiktok-2020-12 |website=Insider |access-date=4 November 2023 |quote=There's even a unique 'nose job check' sound. Over 120,000 videos using this sound have been published on TikTok... |archive-date=15 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215065205/https://www.insider.com/rhinoplasty-is-being-promoted-to-teenagers-nose-job-tiktok-2020-12 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Literature===
{{Main|BookTok}}

[[File:Booktok section, Barnes & Noble, The Grove, Hollywood, Los Angeles, California, USA.jpg|thumb|The [[BookTok]] section at a [[Barnes & Noble]] store]]
Videos discussing and recommending books has collectively become known as [[BookTok]] by users. Books that become popular on BookTok often experience a large increase in sales.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Barnett |first1=David |title='I can't stress how much BookTok sells': teen literary influencers swaying publishers |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2023/aug/06/i-cant-stress-how-much-booktok-sells-teen-literary-influencers-swaying-publishers |website=The Observer |date=6 August 2023 |access-date=3 November 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103231123/https://www.theguardian.com/books/2023/aug/06/i-cant-stress-how-much-booktok-sells-teen-literary-influencers-swaying-publishers |url-status=live }}</ref> The author [[Colleen Hoover]] who rose to popularity on BookTok saw six of her books reach the top ten of [[The New York Times Best Seller list]] in the [[Paperback#trp|paperback trade]] fiction section in October 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mechling |first1=Lauren |title='Never seen anything like it': how Colleen Hoover's normcore thrillers made her America's bestselling author |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2022/oct/11/colleen-hoover-author-tiktok-it-ends-with-us |website=The Guardian |access-date=5 November 2023 |date=12 October 2022 |archive-date=29 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829015440/https://www.theguardian.com/books/2022/oct/11/colleen-hoover-author-tiktok-it-ends-with-us |url-status=live }}</ref> An analyst from the book sales tracking service [[BookScan]] said that BookTok "remains the industry's most important platform for discovering new writers".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Milliot |first1=Jim |title=BookTok Helped Book Sales Soar. How Long Will That Last? |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/93014-booktok-helped-book-sales-soar-how-long-will-that-last.html |website=PublishersWeekly.com |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103231124/https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/93014-booktok-helped-book-sales-soar-how-long-will-that-last.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Some publishers have paid popular BookTok influencers to recommend books to capitalise off of the phenomenon.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zarroli |first1=Jim |title=TikTok is driving book sales. Here are some titles #BookTok recommends |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/12/26/1068063564/booktok-is-a-new-force-driving-book-sales-and-publishing-deals |website=npr.org |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |date=31 December 2021 |archive-date=15 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215101820/https://www.npr.org/2021/12/26/1068063564/booktok-is-a-new-force-driving-book-sales-and-publishing-deals |url-status=live }}</ref>

The success of BookTok content on the platform lead TikTok's parent company, [[ByteDance]], to launch their own publishing company called 8th Note Press in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hawkinson |first1=Katie |title=Tiktok parent company ByteDance wants to capitalize off the success of BookTok but authors worry it might ruin BookTok in the process |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/bytedance-launches-publishing-company-authors-worry-about-future-of-booktok-2023-7 |website=Business Insider |access-date=5 November 2023 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105153545/https://www.businessinsider.com/bytedance-launches-publishing-company-authors-worry-about-future-of-booktok-2023-7 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=TikTok is venturing into book publishing |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/books/features/tiktok-is-venturing-into-book-publishing/articleshow/101521802.cms?from=mdr |website=The Times of India |access-date=10 November 2023 |date=5 July 2023 |archive-date=10 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110164556/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/books/features/tiktok-is-venturing-into-book-publishing/articleshow/101521802.cms?from=mdr |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Medication shortages===
Trends on TikTok have contributed to the shortages of some medications. [[Denmark|Danish]] pharmaceutical company [[Novo Nordisk]] produces three medications containing the active ingredient [[semaglutide]]. One of the drugs, Wegovy, is certified by the [[Food and Drug Administration]] for the treatment of [[obesity]]. The other two, Ozempic and Rybelsus, are only certified for the treatment of [[diabetes]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Basch |first1=Corey H. |last2=Narayanan |first2=Sandhya |last3=Tang |first3=Hao |last4=Fera |first4=Joseph |last5=Basch |first5=Charles E. |title=Descriptive analysis of TikTok videos posted under the hashtag #Ozempic |journal=Journal of Medicine Surgery and Public Health |date=1 January 2023 |volume=1 |article-number=100013 |doi=10.1016/j.glmedi.2023.100013 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2022, the United States suffered shortages of [[Ozempic]] after it became a trend on the platform to use the medication [[off-label use|off-label]] for its weight loss effects.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Court |first1=Court |title=TikTok trend wipes out Ozempic supply, leaving people with diabetes dizzy, scared |url=https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2022-12-23/tiktok-trend-sold-out-ozempic-diabetes-drug |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |date=23 December 2022 |archive-date=8 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108212617/https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2022-12-23/tiktok-trend-sold-out-ozempic-diabetes-drug |url-status=live }}</ref> Australia's [[Therapeutic Goods Administration]] reported that Ozempic's popularity on TikTok had contributed to a global shortage of the medication. It recommended that doctors not prescribe the medication to new patients and prescribe alternative medications to existing patients where possible.<ref>{{cite web |title=About the Ozempic (semaglutide) shortage 2022 and 2023 |url=https://www.tga.gov.au/safety/shortages/information-about-major-medicine-shortages/about-ozempic-semaglutide-shortage-2022-and-2023 |website=www.tga.gov.au |publisher=[[Therapeutic Goods Administration]] |quote="When videos about achieving rapid weight loss with Ozempic went viral on TikTok, the trend was also reported online and across other media. This triggered a huge demand for the product that the manufacturer was not prepared for, and it quickly developed into a worldwide shortage." |access-date=5 November 2023 |language=en |date=8 December 2022 |archive-date=5 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105154340/https://www.tga.gov.au/safety/shortages/information-about-major-medicine-shortages/about-ozempic-semaglutide-shortage-2022-and-2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kolovos |first1=Benita |title=Shortage of diabetes medication Ozempic after TikTok users promote drug for weight loss |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2022/may/31/shortage-of-diabetes-medication-ozempic-after-tiktok-users-promote-drug-for-weight-loss |website=The Guardian |access-date=8 November 2023 |date=31 May 2022 |archive-date=8 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108191817/https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2022/may/31/shortage-of-diabetes-medication-ozempic-after-tiktok-users-promote-drug-for-weight-loss |url-status=live }}</ref> By March 2023, TikTok videos posted with the [[hashtag]] ''#Ozempic'' had amassed 690 million views.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Han |first1=Sabrina H |last2=Safeek |first2=Rachel |last3=Ockerman |first3=Kyle |last4=Trieu |first4=Nhan |last5=Mars |first5=Patricia |last6=Klenke |first6=Audrey |last7=Furnas |first7=Heather |last8=Sorice-Virk |first8=Sarah |title=Public Interest in the Off-Label Use of Glucagon-like Peptide 1 Agonists (Ozempic) for Cosmetic Weight Loss: A Google Trends Analysis |journal=Aesthetic Surgery Journal |date=4 July 2023 |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=60–67 |doi=10.1093/asj/sjad211 |pmid=37402640 |url=https://academic.oup.com/asj/advance-article/doi/10.1093/asj/sjad211/7218900 |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en |quote=Social media users share similar curiosity of #Ozempic with an impressive 690 million views on TikTok |archive-date=23 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223200539/https://academic.oup.com/asj/article/44/1/60/7218900 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Mental health ===
TikTok has become a hub for [[mental health]] content, where users share personal experiences with [[Depression (mood)|depression]] and [[anxiety]]. While this has helped normalize conversations around mental health, it also raises concerns. Dr. Corey Basch, a public health professor, points out that TikTok's algorithm can create echo chambers.<ref name="Seshagiri"/> Users who engage with posts about anxiety or despair may find themselves bombarded with similar content, which can lead to a harmful cycle.

This surge in mental health discussions has also contributed to more young people self-diagnosing conditions like [[ADHD]] and anxiety before consulting a professional. Researchers are concerned about the influence of profit-driven motives, with the platform promoting mental health apps and influencers sponsored by these companies. These services often advertise quick, quiz-based diagnoses, which may oversimplify complex issues. Additionally, [[misinformation]] is a growing problem; studies have found that some videos about therapies, like [[cognitive behavioral therapy]], include inaccurate or misleading information.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

=== Hustle culture ===
TikTok has played a huge role in shaping [[hustle culture]], especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, blurring the lines between work and personal life. With over 1 billion daily active users and 60% of U.S.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Munro |first=Monique-Monét |date=2022 |title=All Work and No Play Makes TikTok a Dull Platform: The Influence of TikTok's 'Hustle Culture' on Productivity in the Digital Age |url=https://ojs.stanford.edu/ojs/index.php/intersect/article/view/2309 |journal=Intersect: The Stanford Journal of Science, Technology, and Society |language=en |volume=16 |issue=1}}</ref> [[Generation Z|Gen Z]] checking in regularly, the platform has made productivity a key focus for many users. People share their daily routines, promoting the idea that constant work leads to success. However, this pressure to always be "on" has its downsides. A 2022 study showed 77% of employees felt burned out, which is a consequence of hustle culture.<ref name=":3" />

That said, some creators are pushing back, showing that it's okay to slow down. For example, Jonathan Graziano's "Bones Day" trend encourages followers to take rest when they need it. TikTok gives a wide range of content, from productivity hacks to messages about [[self-care]], offering users the chance to define their own balance.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

===Other websites===
TikTok is now the dominant social media platform amongst the newer generation. The popularity of TikTok has led various other web services to adopt similar features in order to compete with TikTok. Instagram launched a short, vertical videos section called [[Instagram Reels]] to its app in 2020. [[YouTube]] followed with the release of [[YouTube Shorts]] in 2021.<ref name="Newsweek">{{cite web |last1=Rouhandeh |first1=Alex J. |title=Senators unconcerned over economic impact as they move toward TikTok ban |url=https://www.newsweek.com/senators-unconcerned-over-economic-impact-they-move-toward-tiktok-ban-1787649 |website=Newsweek |access-date=8 November 2023 |language=en |date=14 March 2023 |archive-date=8 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108190349/https://www.newsweek.com/senators-unconcerned-over-economic-impact-they-move-toward-tiktok-ban-1787649 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2022, [[Facebook]] launched a videos tab on its app that shows users a personalized selection of videos.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fischer |first1=Sara |title=Sweeping changes remake Facebook app in TikTok's image |url=https://www.axios.com/2022/07/21/facebook-tiktok-feed-changes |access-date=2 October 2023 |date=21 July 2022 |archive-date=3 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003154850/https://www.axios.com/2022/07/21/facebook-tiktok-feed-changes |url-status=live }}</ref> The same year, [[Twitter]] announced that it would also be launching a short videos feature and [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] added a scrolling feed with photos and videos of available products to its mobile app.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hart |first=Jordan |title=Amazon is introducing a new TikTok-like feature that allows users to 'shop as you scroll' from a social feed of videos and photos |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/amazon-announces-tiktok-like-social-feed-shoppable-videos-photos-2022-12 |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, [[Spotify]] redesigned its home screen to have a similar scrolling interface to TikTok and [[Reddit]] also added a separate video feed to its mobile app.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pierce |first1=David |title=Spotify's new design is part TikTok, part Instagram, and part YouTube |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/3/8/23630821/spotify-design-home-music-podcasts-audiobooks-app |website=The Verge |access-date=2 October 2023 |date=8 March 2023 |archive-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231006160617/https://www.theverge.com/2023/3/8/23630821/spotify-design-home-music-podcasts-audiobooks-app |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Schneider |first1=Jaron |title=Reddit is Adding TikTok-Like Video Feed |url=https://petapixel.com/2023/03/07/reddit-is-adding-tiktok-like-video-feed/ |website=PetaPixel |access-date=2 October 2023 |language=en |date=7 March 2023 |archive-date=20 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020120643/https://petapixel.com/2023/03/07/reddit-is-adding-tiktok-like-video-feed/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Economic impact==
{{Update|section|date=July 2026}}
A 2023 study by Oxford Economics estimated that [[small and medium-sized enterprises]] in the [[United Kingdom]] who posted on TikTok to advertise their and grow their businesses added £1.6 billion to the UK's [[gross domestic product]] in 2022 as a result of their TikTok activity.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gray |first1=Isabelle |title=The TikTok Effect: The socio-economic impact of TikTok in the UK |url=https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/the-tiktok-effect/ |website=Oxford Economics |access-date=3 November 2023 |date=17 July 2023 |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103225625/https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/the-tiktok-effect/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[United States]], following up on a TikTok ban initiated by a previous administration, President [[Donald Trump]] paused the enforcement of the ban twice, granting a total extension of 180 days.<ref>{{cite news|title=Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay |url=https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/ |access-date=30 April 2025 |work=White House |date=4 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref> The platform is set to be shut down unless it is acquired by a U.S.-based company within that period. As of the end of April, no final acquisition agreements have been announced, although several major firms—including [[Oracle Corporation|Oracle]], [[eBay]], and [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]—have reportedly submitted bids.<ref>{{cite news| first=Samuel | last=O'Brient| title=Shocking company makes last-minute bid to buy TikTok |url=https://www.thestreet.com/technology/shocking-company-makes-last-minute-bid-to-buy-tiktok |work=The Street |date=4 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref> If the ban becomes permanent, California is projected to be the most affected state due to its high concentration of TikTok influencers, potential loss in income tax revenue, and broader implications for employment in the digital creator economy.<ref>{{cite news| first=Jenelle | last=Vannoy| title=TikTok ban looms: Nevada TikTokers among those facing economic uncertainty |url=https://news3lv.com/news/local/tiktok-ban-looms-nevada-tiktokers-among-those-facing-economic-uncertainty |work=News3 LV |date=3 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Consumer behavior===
A 2021 study by [[Adweek]] and [[Morning Consult]] found that 49 percent of TikTok users bought goods or services after seeing them being discussed or promoted on the platform.<ref name="Newsweek"/>

In 2023, the ''European Journal of Business and Management Research'' published a study that found that TikTok users were much more likely to trust products shown in TikTok videos that had high-quality videos, rather than products shown on the platform that were more useful or had lower prices.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hoi |first1=New Kuwi |last2=Yin |first2=Lun Ke |title=Short Videos, Big Decisions: A Preliminary Study of Tik Tok's Role in E-Commerce Consumer Behaviour |journal=European Journal of Business and Management Research |date=15 May 2023 |volume=8 |issue=3 |pages=72–81 |doi=10.24018/ejbmr.2023.8.3.1951 |url=https://www.ejbmr.org/index.php/ejbmr/article/view/1951/1132 |access-date=14 October 2023 |issn=2507-1076 |doi-access=free |archive-date=20 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020115328/https://www.ejbmr.org/index.php/ejbmr/article/view/1951/1132 |url-status=live }}</ref>

When products go viral on TikTok, the impact on sales can be significant. Stanley tumblers saw their revenue jump from $73 million in 2019 to $750 million in 2023 after going viral on the platform. [[Feta cheese]] sales soared by 200% in 2021 after the baked feta pasta recipe took off. [[CeraVe]]'s sales increased by over 60% in 2020 as TikTok users turned to the brand during lockdown. Other items, like Cat Crack catnip and Isle of Paradise tanning spray, sold out within days after viral posts.<ref name="Seshagiri"/>

In 2023, TikTok rolled out a shopping feature called [[TikTok Shop]], making it easy for users to buy products directly from a range of sellers. This feature lets businesses sell products directly on the platform, using tools like shoppable ads, product showcases, and creator partnerships to boost sales and connect with their audience in a more native way.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The rise of TikTok Shop: A game-changer for ecommerce |url=https://www.productsup.com/blog/the-rise-of-tiktok-shop-a-game-changer-for-ecommerce/?utm_term&utm_campaign=NAM-EN-PMax-FeedManagement&utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&hsa_acc=5570419478&hsa_cam=21394756726&hsa_grp&hsa_ad&hsa_src=x&hsa_tgt&hsa_kw&hsa_mt&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAiA6aW6BhBqEiwA6KzDc1YBdNYzgJjfMFW1YcintpCTcT_WeZ8n3vVPPYCtjDBpIW-iewGs2hoCIS8QAvD_BwE |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=productsup.com |language=en}}</ref> Some fashion and beauty brands have even started thinking about how a product could be featured on TikTok before they finish developing it.

'''Digikala''' ({{langx|fa|دیجی‌کالا|translit=Dijikalâ|lit=digi(tal) goods}}) is an [[Iran|Iranian]] [[e-commerce]] company based in [[Tehran]], founded in July 2006 by Hamid Mohammadi and Saeid Mohammadi.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fung |first=Brian |date=14 July 2015 |title=The Washington Post:What the Iran deal means for the country's surprisingly strong tech industry |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-switch/wp/2015/07/14/what-the-iran-deal-means-for-the-countrys-surprisingly-strong-tech-industry/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205123135/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-switch/wp/2015/07/14/what-the-iran-deal-means-for-the-countrys-surprisingly-strong-tech-industry/ |archive-date=5 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Digikala is the Largest Online Marketplace in Iran and the Middle East|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/digikala-largest-online-marketplace-iran-150000109.html |access-date=3 September 2021 |work=finance.yahoo.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903140144if_/https://au.finance.yahoo.com/news/digikala-largest-online-marketplace-iran-150000109.html |archive-date=3 September 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 February 2016 |title=Iranian Startups Come of Age |url=https://iranwire.com/en/society/61636/ |access-date=18 September 2022 |website=Iran Wire |language=en}}</ref> 

Digikala offers a wide range of [[consumer products]], which includes [[Sports equipment|sports and entertainment goods]], [[electronics]], [[groceries]], [[Personal care|personal products]], and [[Software|digital products]] with a return option and express delivery service. The group also has subsidiaries involved in other areas of ecommerce.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 February 2022 |title=Total guide on DigiKala's return services |url=https://www.zoomit.ir/howto/378820-how-report-return-counterfeit-products-digikala/ }}</ref>

== History and growth ==
[[File:Digikala HQ in Tehran by Mardetanha (5) 75.jpg|thumb|Hamid Mohammadi and Saeed Mohammadi, co-founders of Digikala]]
Digikala was founded by the brothers Hamid and Saeid Mohammadi, prompted by an unpleasant experience they had trying to buy a [[digital camera]]. The pair used $10,000 of their own savings to start the company.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Guttman |first1=Amy |title=Meet The Twin Brothers Transforming How Iranians Shop |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/amyguttman/2015/01/26/twin-brothers-transforming-how-iranians-shop/3/#60aa5f533fd5 |website=Forbes |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918054425/https://www.forbes.com/sites/amyguttman/2015/01/26/twin-brothers-transforming-how-iranians-shop/?sh=42eb215c57aa |archive-date=18 September 2022 |language=en |date=26 January 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> The company's valuation was $150 million in 2014 and $500 million in late 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McFarland |first=Matt |date=10 November 2014 |title=Here's what it's like to launch a start-up in Iran |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/innovations/wp/2014/11/10/heres-what-its-like-to-launch-a-start-up-in-iran/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520175652/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/innovations/wp/2014/11/10/heres-what-its-like-to-launch-a-start-up-in-iran/ |archive-date=20 May 2022 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharif |first=Hossein |date=12 October 2015 |title=Iran's digital start-ups signal changing times |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-34458898 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220423232648/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-34458898 |archive-date=23 April 2022 |website=BBC}}</ref> As of 2021, more than 4 million products have been offered for sale by nearly 160,000 sellers.<ref>{{cite news |title=وضعیت دیجی کالا در پیک چهارم کرونا چگونه است؟ |url=https://www.farsnews.ir/news/14000129000579/%D9%88%D8%B6%D8%B9%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D8%AF%DB%8C%D8%AC%DB%8C-%DA%A9%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D9%BE%DB%8C%DA%A9-%DA%86%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%85-%DA%A9%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D8%A7-%DA%86%DA%AF%D9%88%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA |language=Persian}}</ref> In 2021, the platform had 30 million visitors per month<ref name="financialtribune">{{cite news |date=23 August 2021 |title=Iran E-Commerce Trending Higher |agency=financialtribune |url=https://financialtribune.com/articles/sci-tech/109916/iran-e-commerce-trending-higher |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref> and 17.2 million visits per day.<ref>{{cite news |date=22 August 2021 |title=Iran E-Commerce Trending Higher |agency=eghtesadonline |url=https://www.en.eghtesadonline.com/Section-iran-economy-67/35567-iran-commerce-trending-higher |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref> In May 2022 it was ranked as Iran's 2nd most visited website.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexa: Top Sites in Iran |url=http://www.alexa.com/topsites/countries/IR |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501153829/https://www.alexa.com/topsites/countries/IR |archive-date=1 May 2022 |website=Alexa}}</ref>

Digikala has benefited from the Iran's increasing [[Digitization economics|digitization]]. By 2017, 62% of Iran's households were connected to the [[Internet]] and this development has driven demand for Internet services that mirror Western digital platforms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.radiofarda.com/a/iranian-startups-offer-opportunities-in-an-unstable-economy/29710513.html|title=Iranian Startups Offer Opportunities In An Unstable Economy|website=RFE/RL|date=15 January 2019 |language=en|access-date=9 May 2019}}</ref> The company does not publicize its [[revenue]], but has said sales are growing at a rate of 200% a year, and that it is receiving orders from even the most remote villages in Iran.<ref>{{Cite news |title=FT:Iranian e-commerce thrives despite obstacles |newspaper=Financial Times |date=October 2014 |url=https://www.ft.com/content/e44136e6-3cdb-11e4-9733-00144feabdc0 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Iran's economic [[Volatility (finance)|volatility]] forced Digikala to lay off 175 workers in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 September 2018 |title=In Face of Hard Times Iran's Digikala Remains Upbeat |url=https://financialtribune.com/articles/sci-tech/93086/in-face-of-hard-times-irans-digikala-remains-upbeat |url-access=subscription |access-date=9 May 2019 |website=Financial Tribune |language=En}}</ref> To survive, the platform adopted several initiatives such as a [[Pay per sale|pay-per-sale]] strategy which allow users to receive a [[Commission (remuneration)|commission]] if a directed customer purchases a product.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 September 2018 |title=Digikala Enlists Pay-Per-Sale Strategy |url=https://financialtribune.com/articles/sci-tech/93861/digikala-enlists-pay-per-sale-strategy |url-access=subscription |access-date=9 May 2019 |website=Financial Tribune |language=En}}</ref> In March 2019, Digikala also addressed the issue of author authenticity of products in the platform after receiving complaints over the quality of goods being sold. In a statement, the company claimed that only 0.2% of the 2 million products sold were unoriginal and that the company has taken steps to implement stringent [[quality control]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://financialtribune.com/articles/sci-tech/97148/digikala-to-carry-out-stringent-quality-control|title=Digikala to Carry Out Stringent Quality Control|date=12 March 2019|website=Financial Tribune|language=En|access-date=9 May 2019}}</ref>

Accordingly, 33.12% of the company's shares belong to Hamid and Saeed Mohammadi, the co-founders of Digikala, followed by IIIC European Investment Fund with 32.67%, Sarava Pars Company with 25.64%, incentive shares for managers and key employees with 4.46%, and other shareholder companies with 11.4%, including Lilian Mod Tejarat, Bazar Ati Ara, Pomegranate Investment AB, Kia Asa Tejarat Toos, and Pars Gostar Dina.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hoe investeerders uit Nederland en België verstrikt raakten in dictatoriaal Iran |url=https://fd.nl/bedrijfsleven/1466654/hoe-investeerders-uit-nederland-en-belgie-verstrikt-raakten-in-dictatoriaal-iran |access-date=2023-03-01 |website=FD.nl |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=دیجی‌کالا با انتشار ساختار سهام‌داری خود اعلام کرد: سهام‌دار حاکمیتی نداریم |url=https://digiato.com/article/2022/11/06/digikala-shareholders-announced |access-date=2023-03-01 |website=دیجیاتو |language=fa-IR}}</ref>

== Products and services ==
Digikala initially started as an online retail platform focused on [[Digital goods|digital]] and electronic products.<ref>{{Cite web |last=hamsite |title=همکاری آژانس دیجیتال مارکتینگ هم سایت |url=https://hamsite.co |website=آژانس دیجیتال مارکتینگ هم سایت}}</ref> Since 2014, Digikala expanded its strategy to become an [[Online shopping|online marketplace]], offering a wider range of products.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ictstartups.ir//fa/content/57604|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116095932/http://www.ictstartups.ir//fa/content/57604 |archive-date=16 January 2019 |title=دیجی‌کالا تا یک سال دیگر «یونیکورن» می‌شود - ictstartups.ir }}</ref>
