==Criticisms and controversies==
===Fraud===
Fraud committed by sellers includes selling [[counterfeit]] merchandise / [[bootleg recording]]s, [[shill]] bidding (undisclosed vendor bidding that is used to artificially inflate the price of a certain item by either the seller under an alternate account or another person in collusion with the seller), receiving payment and not shipping merchandise, shipping items other than those described, giving a deliberately misleading description or photo, knowingly and deliberately shipping faulty merchandise, denying warranty exchange after pre-agreeing to [[return merchandise authorization]] of [[wikt:Defective on arrival|defective on arrival]] merchandise, knowingly [[Fence (criminal)|fencing]] (selling stolen goods), offering nonexistent goods for sale (including goods that could not exist - e.g. devices with battery capacities far beyond that possible for the form factors of the listed items), misrepresenting the cost of shipping, using bulk shipping prices to knowingly mask much higher costing, individual return shipping, and using pseudo-accounts to make high nonpaying bids on similar items that competitors are selling. eBay has been criticized for not doing enough to combat shill bidding. Users have developed techniques, such as [[auction sniping]], to avoid fraud across the site.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2009/07/10/ebay_and_shill_bidding/ |title=Net sleuth calls eBay on carpet over shill bidding |first=Cade |last=Metz |work=[[The Register]] |date=10 July 2009 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214204235/https://www.theregister.co.uk/2009/07/10/ebay_and_shill_bidding/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.rd.com/list/most-common-ebay-scams-to-look-out-for/ |title=10 Most Common eBay Scams to Look Out For |first=Johanna |last=Neeson |work=[[Reader's Digest]] |date=September 1, 2023 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209001834/https://www.rd.com/list/most-common-ebay-scams-to-look-out-for/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Fraud committed by buyers includes filing a false shipping damage claim with the shipping company, [[friendly fraud]] (receiving merchandise and claiming otherwise), returning items other than those received, removing parts from an item and returning it for a refund, sending a forged payment-service e-mail that states that he or she has made a payment to the seller's account as proof of payment, making a low bid then using pseudo-accounts to make high nonpaying bids in an attempt at gaining a low second chance offer price, damaging a non-refundable item to get a refund by claiming that the seller sent the item already damaged (in cases of [[buyer's remorse]]), and a [[package redirection scam]] in which the return package is filled with garbage and sent to the wrong address.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://nordvpn.com/blog/ebay-scams/ |title=Exposing the top 10 eBay scams and how to detect them |first=Saulius |last=Griškėnas |work=[[NordVPN]] |date=August 16, 2023 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226065038/https://nordvpn.com/blog/ebay-scams/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://us.norton.com/blog/online-scams/ebay-scams |title=17 common eBay scams and how to spot them |first=Clare |last=Stouffer |work=[[Norton AntiVirus]] |date=July 20, 2023 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209015312/https://us.norton.com/blog/online-scams/ebay-scams |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2004, [[Tiffany & Co.]] filed a lawsuit against eBay claiming that over 70% of the Tiffany silver jewelry offered for sale on eBay was fake and that eBay profited from the sales of [[counterfeit]] Tiffany items that infringed on its trademark.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/27/technology/27ebay.html |title=Tiffany and eBay in Fight Over Fakes |last=Hafner |first=Katie |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=November 27, 2007 |url-access=limited |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=January 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125163445/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/27/technology/27ebay.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On July 14, 2008, a [[Federal District Court]] judge ruled that eBay did not have a legal responsibility to monitor users selling counterfeit items.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/15/technology/15ebay.html?hp |title=Court Clears eBay in Sale of Counterfeit Items |last=Stone |first=Brad |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 14, 2008 |url-access=limited |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=April 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230421153742/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/15/technology/15ebay.html?hp |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2010, the Second Circuit affirmed this decision in ''[[Tiffany (NJ) Inc. v. eBay Inc.]]''<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.finnegan.com/en/insights/articles/the-second-circuit-s-decision-in-tiffany-v-ebay.html |title=The Second Circuit's Decision in Tiffany v. eBay |first1=Mark |last1=Sommers |first2=Naresh |last2=Kilaru |work=[[Finnegan, Henderson, Farabow, Garrett & Dunner]] |date=May 2010 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207215242/https://www.finnegan.com/en/insights/articles/the-second-circuit-s-decision-in-tiffany-v-ebay.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In June 2008, a court in Paris awarded damages of €40 million to [[LVMH]] over eBay auctions of counterfeit bags, perfumes, and other items sold by non-authorized retailers and entered a permanent injunction against eBay auctions of LVMH perfumes, whether counterfeit or not. eBay banned said items from its site.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!-- No byline --> |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/7481241.stm |title=Court fines eBay over fake goods |work=[[BBC News]] |date=June 30, 2008 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=April 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425151832/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/7481241.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://fortune.com/2008/07/11/ebay-denied-stay-in-lvmh-case/ |title=eBay denied stay in LVMH case |first=Roger |last=Parloff |work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |date=July 11, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090215021429/http://legalpad.blogs.fortune.cnn.com/2008/07/11/ebay-denied-stay-in-lvmh-case/ |archive-date=February 15, 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref> That same month, a court in Troyes, France, ordered eBay to pay luxury goods maker [[Hermès]] €20,000 due to the sale of two counterfeit bags on eBay in 2006. The court also ordered eBay to post the ruling on the home page of eBay's French website for three months.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theregister.com/2008/06/05/ebay_counterfeit_ruling/ |first=Dan |last=Goodin |title=French court fines eBay for sale of counterfeit handbags |work=[[The Register]] |date=June 5, 2008 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=June 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618050839/https://www.theregister.com/2008/06/05/ebay_counterfeit_ruling/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Dr. Seuss books====
In 2021, eBay complied with a request from the estate of [[Dr. Seuss]] to ban the sale of six Dr. Seuss books due to concerns that some illustrations contained therein were racially insensitive. This led to backlash from followers of [[right-wing politics]] and ignited a surge of interest in the discontinued books.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/dr-seuss-books-deemed-offensive-will-be-delisted-from-ebay-11614884201 |title=Dr. Seuss books deemed offensive will be delisted from eBay |first=Jeffrey |last=Trachtenberg |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=March 4, 2021 |url-access=subscription |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231224082425/https://www.wsj.com/articles/dr-seuss-books-deemed-offensive-will-be-delisted-from-ebay-11614884201 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newsweek.com/ebay-removes-discontinued-dr-seuss-books-1573824 |title=eBay is removing listings for discontinued Dr. Seuss books citing 'offensive materials policy' |first=James |last=Crowley |work=[[Newsweek]] |date=March 4, 2021 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=February 20, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240220213800/https://www.newsweek.com/ebay-removes-discontinued-dr-seuss-books-1573824 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/discontinued-dr-seuss-books-with-racist-imagery-removed-by-ebay-2021-3 |title=eBay is removing listings for the Dr. Seuss books that the author's estate pulled due to their racist imagery |first=Steven |last=Tweedie |work=[[Business Insider]] |date=March 5, 2021 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=April 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425151824/https://www.businessinsider.com/discontinued-dr-seuss-books-with-racist-imagery-removed-by-ebay-2021-3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Sale of illegal items===
In September 2023, the [[United States Department of Justice]] sued eBay, accusing it of violating the [[Clean Air Act (United States)|Clean Air Act]] and other environmental laws by allowing the sale of several illegal products, including devices that defeat automobile pollution controls, restricted-use pesticides, and paint and coating removal products containing [[methylene chloride]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/us-sues-ebay-over-sale-aftermarket-motor-vehicle-products-2023-09-27/ |title=U.S. sues eBay over sale of harmful products |first=Jonathan |last=Stempel |work=[[Reuters]] |date=September 27, 2023 |access-date=February 26, 2024 |archive-date=December 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209015438/https://www.reuters.com/legal/us-sues-ebay-over-sale-aftermarket-motor-vehicle-products-2023-09-27/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The court dismissed the case, ruling that the [[Communications Decency Act]] shielded eBay from liability.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weatherbed |first=Jess |date=2024-10-01 |title=eBay is off the hook for selling harmful products |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/10/1/24259191/ebay-doj-harmful-polluting-products-lawsuit-dismissed |access-date=2026-01-01 |website=The Verge |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Port scanning===
In 2020, developer Dan Nemec discovered that eBay was [[port scanning]] its users using [[LexisNexis]]' ThreatMetrix product to detect remote access. The port scanning was performed using [[Code obfuscation|obfuscated]] client-side JavaScript which attempts to open WebSocket connections to [[localhost]] on ports commonly used by remote access tools like [[VNC]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Anderson |first1=Tim |title=eBay users spot the online auction house port-scanning their PCs. Um... is that OK? |url=https://www.theregister.com/2020/05/26/ebay_port_scans_your_pc/ |access-date=10 July 2025 |work=The Register |date=May 26, 2020}}</ref> Some cybersecurity experts have speculated that this method was employed to combat online fraud, as port scanning would allow the company to detect if a compromised computer was being used to make fraudulent purchases on the site.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Spadafora |first1=Anthony |title=eBay is port scanning users' PCs |url=https://www.techradar.com/news/ebay-is-port-scanning-users-pcs |access-date=10 July 2025 |work=TechRadar |date=May 26, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Winder |first=Davey |title=Did You Know eBay Is Probing Your Computer? Here’s How To Stop It |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/daveywinder/2020/05/25/did-you-know-ebay-is-probing-your-computer-heres-how-to-stop-it-windows-privacy-chrome-firefox-web-browser/ |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

'''Etsy, Inc.''' is an American [[e-commerce]] company focused on handmade or vintage items and craft supplies. Its marketplace includes categories such as jewelry, apparel, home decor, furniture, toys, and art. Items described as vintage must be at least 20 years old.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.etsy.com/legal/policy/vintage-items-on-etsy/242665563649 |title= Vintage Items on Etsy |author= Etsy |publisher= Etsy |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> The platform provides sellers with individual storefronts where they list their goods for a fee of US$0.20 per item.<ref name="NYT-Walker-2007-12-16">{{cite news | first= Rob | last= Walker | author-link= Rob Walker (journalist) | title= Handmade 2.0 | date= 2007-12-16 | url   =https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/16/magazine/16Crafts-t.html?_r=2&oref=slogin&ref=magazine&pagewanted=all | work = The New York Times Magazine | access-date = 2007-12-17 }}</ref> Since 2013, the company has allowed the sale of mass-manufactured items.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Etsy CEO Says IPO, Mass Production Won't Ruin Website's 'Handmade Ethos' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/etsy-ceo-ipo-mass-production-ruin-websites-handmade/story?id=29416433 |access-date=2023-04-13 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref>

{{As of|2024|12|31|df=US}}, Etsy's marketplace contained more than 100 million active listings and connected 8 million sellers with 96&nbsp;million buyers.<ref name=AR /> At the end of 2024, Etsy had 2,400 employees.<ref name=AR /> In 2024, Etsy had [[Gross merchandise volume|gross merchandise sales]] of US$12.6&nbsp;billion, a revenue of $2.81&nbsp;billion, and a net gain of $303&nbsp;million.<ref name=AR /> 

The platform generates revenue from three streams. Marketplace revenue includes a 6.5% transaction fee on the final sale value<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sato |first=Mia |date=2022-02-24 |title=Etsy hits sellers with 30 percent transaction fee increase |url=https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/24/22949707/etsy-sellers-transaction-fee-increase|access-date=2022-02-24 |website=The Verge |language=en}}</ref> and a listing fee of $0.20 per item. Seller Services include fees for services such as "Promoted Listings," payment processing, and the purchase of shipping labels through the platform. Other revenue includes fees received from third-party [[payment processors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://amigobulls.com/stock-analysis-videos/etsy-ipo-all-you-need-to-know|title=Alibaba video, Etsy IPO All You Need To Know|access-date=29 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402171455/http://amigobulls.com/stock-analysis-videos/etsy-ipo-all-you-need-to-know|archive-date=2 April 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== History ==
===2005–2014===
[[File:Etsy Work Space.jpg|thumb|Etsy staff at work, July 2010]]
[[File:Etsy Lamps.jpg|thumb|Art in the Etsy office in [[Brooklyn]]]]
[[File:Etsy Dublin office.jpg|thumb|Etsy office in [[Dublin]]]]
The site was launched in 2005<ref name="Marketing 2014">{{cite book | title=Marketing 2014 | publisher=South Western Educational Publishing | last=Pride|first=Ferrell | year=2014 | pages=486 | isbn=978-1133939252}}</ref> by iospace, a small company composed of Robert Kalin, Chris Maguire, and Haim Schoppik. The initial version had taken two and a half months to build.<ref>{{cite web | first = Kat | last = Orland | title = Web 2.0 Awards (2006) – Interview with Robert Kalin of Etsy | publisher = SEOmoz | url = http://www.seomoz.org/web2.0/interview/etsy/2006 | access-date = 2010-10-06 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100914204643/http://www.seomoz.org/web2.0/interview/etsy/2006 | archive-date = 2010-09-14 | url-status = dead }}</ref> Later, Jared Tarbell joined the team. Former [[National Public Radio|NPR]] executive Maria Thomas joined as COO in 2008; she was then promoted to CEO before departing from Etsy in December 2009.  Robert Kalin resumed his role as CEO from December 2009 until July 2011.<ref name="Etsy-2008-07-22">{{cite web | title=New Roles at Etsy Inc. | publisher=Etsy | date=2008-07-22 | url=https://blog.etsy.com/news/2008/etsy-announcement-new-roles-at-etsy-inc/ | work=Storque | access-date=2020-07-10 }}</ref> Investors included Sean Meenan,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/adrianalopez/2013/08/07/passion-before-profit-following-your-passion-is-the-essential-entrepreneurial-trait/|title=Passion Before Profit: Following Your Passion Is The Essential Entrepreneurial Trait|first=Adriana|last=Lopez|website=Forbes.com|access-date=11 February 2022}}</ref> Albert Wenger, Spencer and Judson Ain, [[Union Square Ventures]], and founders of [[Flickr]] and [[Delicious (website)|Delicious]].<ref name="USV-2006-6-5">{{cite web | first=Fred | last=Wilson | author-link=Fred Wilson (financier) | title=Etsy | publisher=Union Square Ventures | date=2006-06-05 | url=http://www.unionsquareventures.com/2006/06/etsy_1.html | access-date=2007-12-19 | url-status=dead | archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20091005213249/http%3A//www.unionsquareventures.com/2006/06/etsy_1.html | archive-date=2009-10-05 }}</ref>

Kalin explained why he named the site Etsy in a 2010 interview with ''[[Reader's Digest]]'', saying, "I wanted a nonsense word because I wanted to build the brand from scratch. I was watching Fellini's ''[[8 ½]]'' and writing down what I was hearing. In Italian, you say ''etsi'' a lot. It means 'oh, yes'. And in Latin and French, it means 'what if'."<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.cnn.com/2011/LIVING/04/22/website.name.origins.mf/index.html?hpt=C2 | title=How Etsy, eBay, Reddit got their names | first = Rob |last=Lammle | date=2011-04-22 | work= Mental Floss | publisher = CNN }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Dalenberg |first=Alex |date=December 2, 2014 |title=Etsy means whatsy? 35 iconic brand names explained |url=http://upstart.bizjournals.com/multimedia/interactives/2014/12/etsy-means-whatsy-35-iconic-brand-names-explained.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222080218/http://upstart.bizjournals.com/multimedia/interactives/2014/12/etsy-means-whatsy-35-iconic-brand-names-explained.html |archive-date=February 22, 2015 |access-date=January 14, 2015 |website=Upstart Business Journal |publisher=American City Business Journals}}</ref>

In Etsy's first year, it attracted attention for frequently adding new tools and functionality to the site to help sellers gain exposure and traffic, including [[Adobe Flash]]-based visualizations and a [[Taxonomy (general)|taxonomy]] of categories with [[Tag (metadata)|tags]].<ref name="Techrunch-Arrington-2005-11-8">{{cite web | first = Michael | last = Arrington | author-link = Michael Arrington | title = Etsy – P2P Commerce with Tagging | publisher = Techcrunch | date = 2005-11-08 | url = https://techcrunch.com/2005/11/08/etsy-is-ebay-20/ | access-date   =2007-12-19}}</ref> Etsy passed $1.7 million in sales in May 2007.<ref name="NYT-Ryzik-2007-6-24">{{cite news | first= Melena | last= Ryzik | title= Where the Crafts Babes and D.I.Y. Dudes Are | date= 2007-06-24 |work=The New York Times| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2007/06/24/fashion/24renegade.html?_r=2&oref=slogin&ref=style&pagewanted=all&oref=slogin | access-date=2007-12-19 }}</ref>  On July 29, Etsy had its one-millionth sale and anticipated its two-millionth sale would occur mid-December 2007. In November 2007, buyers spent $4.3 million purchasing 300,000 items for sale on Etsy, an increase of 43 percent from October 2007.<ref name="NYT-Walker-2007-12-16"/> In June 2007, it expected to be profitable by the fall,<ref name="BusinessWeek-6-12-07"/> but in December 2007 it was not a profitable company.<ref name="IHT-Walker-12-15-07">{{cite news |first= Rob |last= Walker |author-link= Rob Walker (journalist) |title= Craft capitalism: Just do it yourself |date= 2007-12-15 |publisher= International Herald Tribune |url= http://www.iht.com/articles/2007/12/14/business/wbcraft.php |access-date= 2007-12-19 |archive-date= 2009-03-26 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090326004915/http://www.iht.com/articles/2007/12/14/business/wbcraft.php |url-status= dead }}</ref> In January 2008, Etsy received an additional $27 million in funding from Union Square Ventures, [[Hubert Burda Media]], and [[Jim Breyer]].<ref name="CNET-McCarthy">{{cite web | first = Caroline | last = McCarthy | title = Crafty commerce site Etsy gets $27 million in funding | publisher = CNET News | date = 2008-01-30 | url = http://www.news.com/8301-13577_3-9861216-36.html | work = The Social | access-date = 2008-02-27}}</ref>

In February 2008, trouble at eBay, including a strike by some dissatisfied sellers, brought speculation that Etsy could be an increasing competitor.<ref>{{cite news | title = Ebay, After Meg | publisher = Knowledge@Wharton | date = 2008-02-19 | url = https://www.forbes.com/entrepreneurstechnology/2008/02/19/ebay-google-amazon-ent-tech-cx_kw_0219whartonebay.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080226072919/http://www.forbes.com/entrepreneurstechnology/2008/02/19/ebay-google-amazon-ent-tech-cx_kw_0219whartonebay.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = February 26, 2008 | access-date = 2008-02-27}}</ref> At the same time, however, some Etsy sellers expressed discontentment with how Etsy was handling complaints about stores.<ref>{{cite web | first = Meg | last = Marco | title = Sellers Growing Increasingly Unhappy With Lack Of Professionalism At Etsy | publisher = Consumerist | date = 2008-02-26 | url = http://consumerist.com/360889/sellers-growing-increasingly-unhappy-with-lack-of-professionalism-at-etsy | access-date = 2008-02-27 | archive-date = October 8, 2009 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20091008213253/http://consumerist.com/360889/sellers-growing-increasingly-unhappy-with-lack-of-professionalism-at-etsy | url-status = dead }}</ref> At the time, a comparison of the two websites included complaints that on Etsy, items are difficult to find, the interface "feels slow", and the buying and selling process is United States-centric.<ref name="Guardian-Schofiled-2008-2-18">{{cite news | first= Jack | last= Schofield | author-link = Jack Schofield (journalist) | title= Arts and crafts for the space age | date= 2008-02-18 | publisher= Guardian.co.uk | url= https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2008/feb/18/etsy.crafts | work = Netbytes | access-date=2008-02-27 | location=London}}</ref> Other reviewers enjoyed using Etsy's specialized search options,<ref>{{cite news | first = Micki | last = Takac | title = Etsy's Handmade Goods Inspire the Shopper in All of Us | publisher = Invention and Technology News | date = 2009-02-16 | url = http://news.inventhelp.com/Articles/Internet/Inventions/etsy-shop-12587.aspx | access-date = 2009-05-12 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090422130559/http://news.inventhelp.com/Articles/Internet/Inventions/etsy-shop-12587.aspx | archive-date = 2009-04-22 | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | first = Arlene | last = Lott | title = Do You Etsy? | publisher = CBC.ca | date = 2009-02-24 | url = http://longlivetheinternet.com/do-you-etsy-viable-ecommerce-option/ | work = Steven and Chris | access-date = 2009-05-12 | archive-date = 2019-04-02 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190402230902/http://longlivetheinternet.com/do-you-etsy-viable-ecommerce-option/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> including the "Shop Local" tool.<ref>{{cite news | first = Alexander | last = Baxevanis | title = Etsy brings handmade crafts closer to home | publisher = Marketing Week | date = 2009-02-19 | url = http://www.marketingweek.co.uk/cgi-bin/item.cgi?id=64373&u=pg_dtl_art_news&m=271 | access-date = 2009-05-12}}</ref>

In July 2008, Rob Kalin ceded the position of CEO to Maria Thomas.<ref name="Storque-The-Long-View-2008-7-2">{{cite web | first = Robert | last = Kalin | title = The Long View: Rob & Maria | publisher = Etsy | date = 2008-07-09 | url = https://blog.etsy.com/news/2008/the-long-view-rob-maria/ | work = Storque | access-date = 2020-07-10 }}</ref> Some longtime Etsy employees left the company in August 2008, including founders Haim Schoppik and Chris Maguire.<ref name="Storque-A-Fond-Farewell-2008-12-8">{{cite web | first = Chris | last = Maguire | author-link = Chris Maguire | title = A Fond Farewell | publisher = Etsy | date = 2008-08-28 | url = https://blog.etsy.com/news/2008/a-fond-farewell/ | work = Storque | access-date = 2020-07-10 }}</ref> In September 2008, Etsy hired Chad Dickerson, who formerly worked at [[Yahoo!]], as [[Chief technology officer|Chief Technology Officer]].<ref>{{cite news | first = Ina | last = Steiner | title = Touring Etsy.com's Brooklyn Headquarters | publisher = AuctionBytes.com | date = 2009-04-05 | url = http://www.auctionbytes.com/cab/abu/y209/m04/abu0236/s02 | access-date = 2009-05-12}}</ref> The company acknowledged concerns about vendors selling other people's work as their own.<ref>{{cite news | first = Bobbie | last = Johnson | title = Etsy: eBay for arts and crafts | publisher = Guardian.co.uk | date = 2008-10-15 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2008/oct/15/etsy-arts-and-crafts-online | access-date = 2009-05-12 | location=London}}</ref>

In April 2009, users organized an "etsyday" promotion on [[Twitter]] that brought extra attention to the site.<ref>{{cite news | first = Geoffrey A. | last= Fowler | title = How #etsyday Grew on Twitter |publisher=The Wall Street Journal| date = 2009-04-24 | url = https://blogs.wsj.com/digits/2009/04/24/how-etsyday-grew-on-twitter/ | work = Digits | access-date = 2009-05-12 }}</ref> As of May 2009, it had approximately 60 employees and sales of $10 to 13 million per month,<ref name="emarketer-recession">{{cite web | title = Etsy Crafts a Recession Success | publisher = eMarketer Digital Intelligence | date = 2009-05-01 | url = http://www.emarketer.com/Article.aspx?R=1007066 | access-date = 2009-05-12 | archive-date = April 2, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190402230901/http://www.emarketer.com/Article.aspx?R=1007066 | url-status = dead }}</ref> possibly boosted by consumer interest in cheaper and more personalized goods due to the United States recession.<ref>{{cite news | first = Claire Cain | last = Miller | title = For Craft Sales, the Recession Is a Help |work=The New York Times| date   =2008-12-22 | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2008/12/23/business/23craft.html?_r=2&partner=rss&pagewanted=all | access-date= 2009-05-12}}</ref>

In March 2010, Kalin said that the company is profitable and "plans to go public, though not until at least next year".<ref>{{cite news | first = Teri | last = Evans | title = Creating Etsy's Handmade Marketplace |work=The Wall Street Journal| date = 2010-03-30 | url= https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702304370304575152133860888958 | access-date = 2010-03-30}}</ref> Financial statements required to be filed by Etsy in order to go public show that due to reinvestment of annually increasing gross profits in marketing, [[Web development|product development]], and [[SG&A|management]], the company has not reported a net profit as of 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1370637/000119312515129455/d806992ds1a.htm#toc806992_9|title=Amendment No.2 to Form S-1|website=Sec.gov|access-date=29 July 2015}}</ref>

In December 2010, Etsy said it had seven million registered users, and that it would continue to focus on a personal community feel as it grows larger, as that is part of what distinguishes it from eBay.<ref>{{cite news | first = Jenna | last = Wortham | title = Online Bazaar Builds on Its Base With Sense of Community |work=The New York Times| date = 2010-12-26 | url= https://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/27/technology/27etsy.html | access-date = 2011-01-01}}</ref>

In March 2011, Etsy "introduced a Facebook-style social networking system called People Search...to help buyers and sellers connect with each other and become friends". By doing so, Etsy made any past purchase with feedback easily searchable, which caused many complaints. Etsy then made changes to the site to better guard information regarding users' purchases.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grant |first=Drew |title=Etsy's social media DIY-saster |url=http://proimexers.com/ |publisher=Professional Imexers|access-date=20 March 2011}}</ref>

In July 2011, Chad Dickerson, CTO since September 2008, became CEO, upon the firing of Rob Kalin. Later CTOs were Kellan Elliot-McCrea and John Allspaw.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kitchensoap.com/2012/10/25/on-being-a-senior-engineer/|title=On Being A Senior Engineer|first1=I. like making things go! At the|last1=moment|first2=I. am Etsy's|last2=CTO|first3=I. just recently finished my master's degree in Human|last3=Factors|first4=Systems Safety at Lund|last4=University|date=25 October 2012}}</ref>

In April 2012, a newspaper article about Etsy covered its fraud detection efforts;<ref name="WSJ-Crafts-Cops">{{cite news | first = Sarah | last = Nassauer | title = Busted by the Crafts Cops | date= 2012-04-17 |work=The Wall Street Journal| url = https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702304299304577349731690704306 | access-date = 2012-04-26 }}</ref> Etsy had been criticized in the past for inconsistently applying its rules about items having to be handmade.<ref name="Etsy-Closings-2012-01-27">{{cite news | first = Jeff | last = F. | title = Etsy Closes Azreal's Accomplice. Cites Policy Infringement | date = 2012-01-27 | publisher = Houston Press | url = http://blogs.houstonpress.com/artattack/2012/01/etsy_closes_azreals_accomplice.php | access-date = 2012-01-27 | archive-date = 2012-01-31 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120131071651/http://blogs.houstonpress.com/artattack/2012/01/etsy_closes_azreals_accomplice.php | url-status = dead }}</ref> Later in April 2012, the writer of Regretsy, a popular blog, did independent research into a specific featured vendor, Ecologica Malibu, and found evidence to accuse the vendor of being a [[reseller]], which would be against the Etsy Terms of Service.<ref name="Regretsy-Killer-2012-04-21">{{cite news | first = Helen | last = Killer | title = The Etsy Featured Reseller: Ecologica Malibu | date= 2012-04-21 | publisher= Regretsy | url = http://www.regretsy.com/2012/04/21/the-etsy-featured-reseller-ecologica-malibu/ | access-date = 2012-04-21 }}</ref> The vendor asserted that it was in line with the Terms of Service, stating that the shop had simply failed to identify itself as a "collective" that included the work of several individuals, and many Etsy community members posted on the Etsy forum expressing unhappiness with the action (or lack of action) taken by Etsy.<ref>{{cite news | first = Chris | last = Morran | title = Etsy Features Seller Who May Be Blatantly Violating Etsy Policy | date= 2012-04-23 | publisher= The Consumerist | url = http://consumerist.com/2012/04/etsy-features-seller-who-may-be-blatantly-violating-etsy-policy.html | access-date = 2012-04-26 }}</ref> As of June 2012, the vendor's account is no longer active on Etsy.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://betabeat.com/2012/06/controversial-etsy-seller-disappears-from-etsy/ |title= Controversial Etsy Seller Disappears From Etsy After High-Profile Protest |first= Adrianne |last=Jeffries |date= June 5, 2012 |website= BetaBeat |access-date=June 16, 2012}}</ref>

In May 2012, Etsy raised $40 million in Series F funding, and announced the company had become a [[B Corporation certification|B Corp]].<ref>{{cite news | first = Jessica | last = Roy | title = With New B Corp. Certification, Etsy Raises $40M for International Growth | date= 2012-05-09 | website= Betabeat | url = http://betabeat.com/2012/05/09/with-new-b-corp-certification-etsy-raises-40m-for-international-growth/ | access-date = 2012-05-09 }}</ref> This [[B Lab]] certification lapsed in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://qz.com/work/1146365/etsy-made-mistakes-from-which-other-b-corps-can-learn/|title=Etsy made mistakes, but its commitment to social responsibility wasn't one of them|first=Nikita T.|last=Mitchell|website=Quartz at Work|date=5 December 2017 }}</ref><!-- more info: https://observer.com/2017/09/etsy-b-corp-deadline/ --> Etsy's 2012 funds went towards expanding Etsy in international markets, including France, Germany, and Australia.<ref>{{cite news |title= Etsy Focuses on Growth Down Under |first= Gillian |last=Tan |url= https://blogs.wsj.com/dealjournalaustralia/2012/06/12/etsy-focuses-on-growth-down-under/ |newspaper= The Wall Street Journal |date= June 12, 2012 |access-date=June 14, 2012}}</ref>

On October 1, 2013, Dickerson held an online Town Hall Meeting to announce that Etsy would now permit factory-made goods and [[drop shipping]], provided the seller either designed or hired designers of the items, disclosed to Etsy their factory, disclosed that they used factories and took "ownership" of the process. In that meeting and afterward, Etsy claimed the meaning of the word "handmade" should be redefined to encompass factory made.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/townhall/2013/10/01|title=Town Hall: New Guidelines for Etsy Shops|work=Etsy}}</ref> Dickerson described the website as "a platform that provides meaning to people, and an opportunity to validate their art, their craft".<ref name="Om">{{cite web|title=Meet the man behind New York's other billion dollar internet company. This one makes money|url=http://gigaom.com/2013/08/23/meet-the-man-behind-new-yorks-other-billion-dollar-internet-company-this-one-makes-money/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130823201100/http://gigaom.com/2013/08/23/meet-the-man-behind-new-yorks-other-billion-dollar-internet-company-this-one-makes-money/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 23, 2013|work=GIGAOM|access-date=24 August 2013|first=Om |last=Malik|date=24 August 2013}}</ref>

In June 2014, Etsy purchased A Little Market, a French e-commerce site for handmade goods, foods, and wine, for a mix of cash and stock valued at less than $100 million. At the time the acquisition was the company's largest.<ref name="demos">Telis Demos, [https://blogs.wsj.com/moneybeat/2014/06/23/etsy-acquires-french-market-in-biggest-deal-yet/ "Etsy Acquires French Market in Biggest Deal Yet"], ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', June 23, 2014.</ref>

=== 2015: IPO and investor lawsuit ===
On March 3, 2015, Etsy announced that it had filed for a $100 million [[IPO]].<ref name="ipo_vb">{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/03/04/etsy-files-to-go-public-with-100m-ipo/|title=Etsy files to go public with $100M IPO|date=4 March 2015|publisher=[[The Verge]]|access-date=2015-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.etsy.com/news/2015/etsy-has-filed-a-registration-statement-for-an-ipo/|title=Etsy Has Filed a Registration Statement for an IPO|work=Etsy Blog|publisher=Etsy|access-date=2015-03-04|archive-date=September 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901053752/https://blog.etsy.com/news/2015/etsy-has-filed-a-registration-statement-for-an-ipo/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As of 2015, Etsy generated transactions worth US$1.93 billion on its platform, which has 54 million members.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2015/03/04/etsys-54m-members-drove-1-93b-in-sales-last-year/|title=Etsy now has 54M members. They drove $1.93B in sales last year – VentureBeat – Business – by Harrison Weber|work=VentureBeat|date=4 March 2015|access-date=29 July 2015}}</ref> Etsy went public on the [[Nasdaq]] on April 16, 2015, selling 13.3 million shares, while other stockholders including [[venture capital]] firms such as [[Accel Partners|Accel]] and [[Acton Capital Partners]] were selling the rest.<ref>{{cite news|title=Crafts website company Etsy valued at $4 billion in market debut|date=16 April 2015|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-etsyinc-ipo/crafts-website-company-etsy-valued-at-4-billion-in-market-debut-idUSKBN0N71T420150416|work=Reuters|access-date=24 March 2019|last1=Dimri|first1=Neha}}</ref> The company's valuation was $1.8 billion and raised $237 million in IPO proceeds.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Gurley|first1=Bill|title=Etsy's IPO is a Milestone for New York's Startup Scene|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/venturecapital/2015/04/16/etsys-ipo-is-a-milestone-for-new-yorks-startup-scene/|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=16 April 2015|access-date=17 April 2015}}</ref>  Less than a month later, Etsy stock dropped more than 8%. The stock closed at $30 on its first day of trading on April 16 and dropped down to $20.32 as of May 11.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Long|first1=Heather|title=Etsy stock tanks 8% on fears of counterfeit goods|date=11 May 2015|url=https://money.cnn.com/2015/05/11/investing/etsy-stock-fall-counterfeit-warning/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150514005057/http://money.cnn.com/2015/05/11/investing/etsy-stock-fall-counterfeit-warning|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 14, 2015|publisher=CNN Money|access-date=14 May 2015}}</ref>

Shortly after the IPO in 2015, a group of investors filed a class action lawsuit against Etsy claiming fraud. The suit claimed that Etsy's CEO and officers failed to disclose numerous problems with the site which could affect the stock price, among them that "more than 5 percent of all merchandise for sale on Etsy’s website may be either counterfeit or constitute trademark or copyright infringement" and that "brands are increasingly pursuing sellers on Etsy for trademark or copyright infringement, jeopardizing listing fees and commissions". The suit also claimed that Etsy management knew of the rampant trademark and copyright infringement but did little to stop it, and in fact worked to hide this information from potential investors.<ref name="Conark Law360.com">{{cite web|last1=Conarck |first1=Ben|url=https://www.law360.com/articles/655838/etsy-hid-counterfeiting-problems-from-investors-suit-says|title=Etsy Hid Counterfeiting Problems From Investors, Suit Says|website=Law360.com|date=May 14, 2015}}</ref>

===2016–present===
In November 2016, Etsy disclosed that it paid US$32.5 million to purchase Blackbird Technologies, a startup that developed [[AI]] software used for shopping context/search applications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2016/11/03/etsy-paid-32-5-million-for-ai-startup-blackbird-technologies/|title=Etsy paid $32.5 million for AI startup Blackbird Technologies|website=VentureBeat|date=4 November 2016|access-date=2016-11-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2016/09/19/etsy-buys-blackbird-ai-to-bring-more-machine-learning-into-its-search-platform/|title=Etsy buys Blackbird Technologies to bring AI to its search|last=Lunden|first=Ingrid|website=TechCrunch|date=19 September 2016 |access-date=2016-09-23}}</ref> After experiencing a first-quarter loss in May 2017, Etsy replaced its chief executive and cut 8% of its workforce. In May 2017, Board member [[Josh Silverman]] was appointed CEO over Chad Dickerson,<ref name=wsj-sfadar>{{cite news |last=Safdar |first=Khadeeja |date=May 2, 2017 |title=Etsy Replaces Its CEO After Swinging to a Loss  |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/etsy-replaces-its-ceo-after-swinging-to-a-loss-1493761030 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref> citing pressure from shareholders and poor profits.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/etsy-replaces-ceo-cuts-jobs-amid-shareholder-pressure-47167426|title=ABC News|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|website=ABC News|access-date=2017-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512045447/https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/etsy-replaces-ceo-cuts-jobs-amid-shareholder-pressure-47167426|archive-date=2017-05-12|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2019, Etsy acquired the music based marketplace [[Reverb.com|Reverb]] for $275 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2019/07/22/etsy-acquires-musical-instruments-site-reverb-for-275-million/|title=Etsy acquires musical instruments site Reverb for $275 million|last=Vega|first=Nicolas|date=2019-07-22|website=New York Post|language=en|access-date=2019-10-23}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic in 2020]], shares in Etsy more than quadrupled. Equity analyst at [[Regional Bond Dealers Association#Leadership and Members|D.A. Davidson]] Tom Forte stated the pandemic gave customers incentive to return to the website multiple times, rather than the usual occasional purchase of a unique product.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Burton|first=Amber|date=2020-12-23|title=Etsy and Shopify Buoyed as Covid-19 Boosts Online Sales|language=en-US|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/etsy-and-shopify-buoyed-as-covid-19-boosts-online-sales-11608719401|access-date=2020-12-25|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|Non-medical face masks]] accounted for around 11% of gross-merchandise sales in the third quarter, selling roughly 24 million.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chin |first=Kimberly |date=2020-10-28 |title=Etsy Sales Lifted by Demand for Face Masks |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/etsy-sales-lifted-by-demand-for-face-masks-11603925874 |access-date=2020-12-25 |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 April 2020 |title=Etsy Rallies Its Artisanal Troops: 'Start Making Face Masks' |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/etsy-rallies-artisanal-troops-start-100050427.html |access-date=2020-04-21 |website=Bloomberg |language=en-US |via=Yahoo! Finance}}</ref>

On June 2, 2021, Etsy announced that it had agreed to acquire shopping app [[Depop]], the fashion resell marketplace for $1.63 billion.<ref>{{cite news|date=2 June 2021|title=Etsy to acquire global fashion resale marketplace Depop|work=Etsy Investor Relations|url=https://investors.etsy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2021/Etsy-to-acquire-global-fashion-resale-marketplace-Depop/default.aspx|access-date=22 July 2021}}</ref> Depop was later sold to [[eBay]] for $1.2{{nbsp}}billion in 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx240kme2k8o |title=Etsy sells second-hand fashion app Depop to eBay for $1.2bn |date=19 February 2026 |work=BBC News |first1=Danielle |last1=Kayeand |first2=Osmond |last2=Chia}}</ref>

In most locations where Etsy Payments is not available, new shops are unable to on board to Etsy. As of April 26, 2021, most sellers opening new shops on Etsy are required to on board with Etsy Payments, which brings limitations on creating new shops in some countries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why Can't I Open a Shop in My Country? |url=https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500006519562-Why-Can-t-I-Open-a-Shop-in-My-Country-?segment=selling |website=Etsy}}</ref>

In June 2022, Etsy announced the August launch of a purchase protection program for buyers and sellers. The company stated that an item that arrives damaged, does not arrive or does not match a description, will be refunded in full for the buyer. Etsy also reported it would invest $25 million to cover the refunds for cases where the seller is not at fault for item damage or loss.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Malik |first1=Aisha |title=Etsy is launching a purchase protection program, investing $25M to cover refunds in some cases |url=https://techcrunch.com/2022/06/06/etsy-purchase-protection-program-investing-25m-cover-refunds/ |website=TechCrunch |date=6 June 2022 |access-date=6 June 2022}}</ref>

In December 2023, Etsy laid off approximately 225 employees, or 11% of its workforce.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Sara |author2=Gabrielle Fonrouge|date=2023-12-13 |title=Etsy stock falls after company lays off 11% of its staff, citing 'very challenging' environment |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/13/etsy-laying-off-11percent-of-staff-citing-competitive-environment.html |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2024, Etsy introduced "Gift Mode", powered by [[OpenAI]] [[GPT-4]], which allows users to generate gift guides based on survey questions related to the recipient's demographic and interests.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Forristal |first=Lauren |date=2024-01-24 |title=Etsy launches 'Gift Mode,' a new AI-powered feature that generates 200+ gift guides |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/01/24/etsy-launches-gift-mode-a-new-ai-powered-feature-that-generates-200-gift-guides/ |access-date=2024-02-16 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 29, 2025, Etsy announced that it will switch its stock listing from [[Nasdaq]] to the [[New York Stock Exchange]] on October 10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/etsy-move-stock-listing-nyse-nasdaq-2025-09-29/|title=Etsy to move stock listing to NYSE from Nasdaq|agency=Reuters|date=September 29, 2025}}</ref>

In October 2025, Etsy announced that it will promote Chief Growth Officer Kruti Patel Goyal to become Etsy's CEO starting January 1, 2026, ending Josh Silverman's eight years in the position. Silverman will become executive chair through the end of 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Etsy Names New CEO, Sending Shares Down Despite Profit Beat|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-29/etsy-taps-chief-growth-officer-as-ceo-to-navigate-the-ai-era |first=Caroline |last=Hyde|author2=Paayal Zaveri |website=Bloomberg |date=2025-10-29 |access-date=2025-10-30}}</ref>

In February 2026, Etsy announced that [[eBay]] would acquire its fashion resale marketplace [[Depop]] for approximately $1.2 billion. Etsy said the sale would allow it to focus on its core marketplace. At the end of 2025, Depop had approximately $1 billion in gross merchandise sales, 7 million active buyers and more than 3 million active sellers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-18 |title=eBay to Acquire Depop from Etsy |url=https://investors.etsy.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/217/ebay-to-acquire-depop-from-etsy |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Etsy, Inc. |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2026, Etsy completed the sale of Depop to eBay. Etsy received approximately $1.4 billion in aggregate cash, consisting of the $1,2 billion purchase price plus $200 million in purchase price adjustments and interest.<ref>{{Cite web |title=July 30, 2026 - 8-K: Current report {{!}} Etsy, Inc. (ETSY) |url=https://investors.etsy.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001370637-26-000071/etsy-20260730.htm |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Etsy, Inc. |language=en-US}}</ref> The following month Etsy announced plans to lay off approximately 220 employees, or about 12% of its workforce, as part of an organizational restructuring.<ref name=retaildive>{{cite web|url=https://www.retaildive.com/news/etsy-slashes-workforce-12-percent-laying-off-220-ai-chatgpt/827193/ |title=Etsy slashes workforce by 12%, laying off 220 | first=Daphne|last=Howland|work=RetailDIVE|date=August 6, 2026|access-date=August 24, 2026}}</ref>

== Operations ==
[[File:Offices near Clumber Corner, Brooklyn, New York City.png|thumb|Etsy's headquarters in Brooklyn]]
[[File:Etsy Labs.jpg|thumb|Etsy Labs community workspace area]]
[[File:Etsy, Hudson, NY.jpg|thumb|Office in [[Hudson, New York]]]]
Etsy is used by individuals as a part-time business and as a marketplace for handmade, vintage, or recycled goods, in addition to items that differ from mass-produced products.{{cn|date=December 2025}} Many items on Etsy are handmade, vintage, or craft supplies. Product listings often include multiple photographs, and sellers can add up to 13 tags to their products to improve searchability. Buyers can choose to search for items available locally.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2011-jan-01-la-fi-etsy-20110101-story.html|title=Online crafts marketplace is vast but not impersonal|first=Kelsey |last=Ramos|date=January 1, 2011|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|access-date=December 9, 2012}}</ref> Etsy staffers publish lists of featured items.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.santacruzsentinel.com/localnews/ci_16776130|title=Heavens to Etsy: Online artisan marketplace makes shopping local a cinch|last1=Copeland|first1=Laura|date=December 4, 2010|publisher=Santa Cruz Sentinel|access-date=December 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130613002640/http://www.santacruzsentinel.com/localnews/ci_16776130|archive-date=June 13, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Most sellers are women,<ref name="BusinessWeek-6-12-07">{{cite news|url=http://www.businessweek.com/smallbiz/content/jun2007/sb20070611_488723.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070615044915/http://www.businessweek.com/smallbiz/content/jun2007/sb20070611_488723.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 15, 2007|title=Etsy: A Site for Artisans Takes Off|last=Miller|first=Kerry|date=2007-06-12|access-date=2007-12-19|publisher=BusinessWeek}}</ref> who tend to be college-educated and in their twenties and thirties.<ref name="emarketer-recession2">{{cite web|url=http://www.emarketer.com/Article.aspx?R=1007066|title=Etsy Crafts a Recession Success|date=2009-05-01|publisher=eMarketer Digital Intelligence|access-date=2009-05-12|archive-date=April 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402230901/http://www.emarketer.com/Article.aspx?R=1007066|url-status=dead}}</ref> Individual Etsy sellers decide which payment options to offer buyers; these options may include credit card, cheque, [[money order]], [[PayPal]], [[bank transfer]], and Etsy [[gift card]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-gb/articles/115014503608|title=How to Get Paid on Etsy|author=Etsy|publisher=Etsy|access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref>

Etsy sellers range from hobbyists to professional artists who use the site to make a living.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rogers|first=Kate|date=2021-11-26|title=Etsy sellers and other small businesses are betting on local sourcing to win the holiday|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/11/26/holiday-shopping-2021-etsy-sellers-bet-local-sourcing-will-help-win-holiday.html|access-date=2021-12-16|website=CNBC|language=en}}</ref> According to artists who have developed their Etsy stores into their primary jobs, scaling up production of handmade items can require [[Overtime|more than full-time work]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/12/17/fashion/17etsy.html?_r=1&pagewanted=all|title=That Hobby Looks Like a Lot of Work|first=Alex |last=Williams|date=December 16, 2009|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date=June 14, 2012}}</ref> especially during the [[holiday shopping season]].<ref name="businessweek-nosleep2">{{cite news|url=http://www.businessweek.com/articles/2012-12-05/no-sleep-till-christmas-etsy-sellers-haggard-holidays|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121207014131/http://www.businessweek.com/articles/2012-12-05/no-sleep-till-christmas-etsy-sellers-haggard-holidays|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 7, 2012|title=No Sleep Till Christmas: Etsy Sellers' Haggard Holidays|first=John |last=Tozzi|date=December 5, 2012|work=Small Business|publisher=Businessweek|access-date=December 16, 2012}}</ref>

Etsy's main office is in [[Dumbo, Brooklyn]], and it has hosted open crafting classes in the "Etsy Labs".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ecommercebytes.com/cab/abu/y209/m04/abu0236/s02|title=Touring Etsy.com's Brooklyn Headquarters|first=Ina |last=Steiner|date=April 5, 2009|publisher=EcommerceBytes|access-date=December 16, 2012}}</ref> The site's technology, [[customer support]], marketing, PR, business, and communications teams operate out of this office. Etsy Labs has a workspace that provides equipment and donated materials, where members gather to make items, take and teach workshops, and attend special events.<ref name="NYT-Walker-2007-12-162">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/16/magazine/16Crafts-t.html?_r=2&oref=slogin&ref=magazine&pagewanted=all|title=Handmade 2.0|last=Walker|first=Rob|date=2007-12-16|work=The New York Times Magazine|access-date=2007-12-17|author-link=Rob Walker (journalist)}}</ref> Etsy also has an office in Berlin.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thelocal.de/society/20100401-26269.html#.UM6F4OOe_Kw|title=Etsy gets made in Berlin|last1=Allen|first1=Kristen|date=April 1, 2012|publisher=[[The Local]] Germany|access-date=December 16, 2012|archive-date=January 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130103191108/http://www.thelocal.de/society/20100401-26269.html#.UM6F4OOe_Kw|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2012 Etsy announced that it was taking steps to hire more women engineers to improve the gender balance of its team, as a website with majority women users but few women engineers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/danielnyegriffiths/2012/04/06/etsy-hacker-school/|title=Etsy To Fund "Hacker School" Grants For Women|first=Daniel Nye |last=Griffiths|date=April 6, 2012|work=Tech|publisher=Forbes|access-date=June 16, 2012}}</ref> By 2019, 30 percent of Etsy's engineers identified as "women or non-binary", and more than 30 percent were people of color.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://triplepundit.com/story/2019/etsy-shows-leadership-diversity-tech/81936/|title=Etsy Shows Leadership on Diversity in Tech|last=Mazzoni|first=Mary|date=January 22, 2019|website=TriplePundit|language=en|access-date=2019-02-12|archive-date=2019-02-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190213010148/https://triplepundit.com/story/2019/etsy-shows-leadership-diversity-tech/81936/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Etsy was one of the main members of the Handmade Consortium, a 2007 effort to encourage buying handmade holiday gifts.<ref name="IHT-Walker-12-15-072">{{cite news|url=http://www.iht.com/articles/2007/12/14/business/wbcraft.php|title=Craft capitalism: Just do it yourself|last=Walker|first=Rob|date=2007-12-15|access-date=2007-12-19|publisher=International Herald Tribune|author-link=Rob Walker (journalist)|archive-date=2009-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090326004915/http://www.iht.com/articles/2007/12/14/business/wbcraft.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> Etsy has partnered with the retail chain West Elm to sell some Etsy products in its stores.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://minnesota.publicradio.org/features/npr.php?id=167080018|title=Etsy Crafts A Strategy For Staying Handmade And Profitable|last1=Blair|first1=Elizabeth|date=December 13, 2012|publisher=Minnesota Public Radio News|access-date=December 16, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://life.nationalpost.com/2011/06/03/we-love-etsy-and-so-does-west-elm-%E2%80%94-the-store-will-host-etsy-sellers-june-4/|title=We love Etsy, and so does West Elm — the store will host Etsy sellers June 4|last1=Guthrie|first1=Becky|date=June 3, 2011|work=Homes|publisher=National Post|access-date=December 16, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130129115931/http://life.nationalpost.com/2011/06/03/we-love-etsy-and-so-does-west-elm-—-the-store-will-host-etsy-sellers-june-4/|archive-date=January 29, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2012, Etsy opened a temporary holiday storefront in [[SoHo]], New York City.<ref name="businessweek-nosleep2" /> In 2019 the UK's first Etsy store was opened in [[Didcot]], Oxfordshire. The store features more than 50 local makers & small businesses and an eco refill station, selling packaging free groceries including dry foods, toiletries, and cleaning products.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oxfordetsy.com/pages/didcot-store-1|title=Visit Us|website=Oxfordetsy.com|access-date=11 February 2022}}</ref>

=== Selling ===
Creating a shop on Etsy requires creating and posting at least one listing in the shop, which costs $0.20. Each listing will remain on the shop's page for a maximum of four months, or until someone buys the product. The prices of products are set by the shop owner, but Etsy claims 6.5% of the final sale price of the listing<ref name="etsy.com">{{Cite web|title=Etsy Seller News|url=https://www.etsy.com/seller-news|website=Etsy|access-date=June 14, 2018|archive-date=March 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210307095701/https://www.etsy.com/seller-news|url-status=dead}}</ref> and 6.5% of the postal fee.

Additionally, Etsy has mandatory offsite ad fees of 12% or 15%. If a shop is selling less than $10K per year, they can opt out of offsite ad fees. However, once their sales reach $10K per year, offsite ad fees become mandatory and a shop cannot opt out. When a buyer clicks on an offsite ad and purchases from a shop, the seller is charged that fee on everything that is purchased, as well as any other purchases the same buyer may make within the next 30 days. This fee is in addition to the listing fees, credit card processing fees, and commissions that are charged on all sales. These payment processing fees (handled via Etsy Payments) vary depending on the seller's bank location; for example, sellers in the United States are charged an additional 3% plus a $0.25 flat rate per transaction.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=Etsy Fees Explained (2026): What You Actually Keep Per Sale |url=https://anlyzo.com/blog/etsy-fees-explained-what-you-actually-keep |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=anlyzo.com |language=en}}</ref> Only shops that met the $10K in the last year threshold when this fee was first implemented are charged the lower 12% fee. Currently, all shops that reach $10K in sales for a twelve-month period are charged the higher fee of 15%. Shop owners are sent a bill at the end of every month detailing the fees Etsy has charged them, and they have until the 15th of the following month to pay the fees.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/legal/fees/#fee|title=Etsy – Learn How to Sell on Etsy|work=Etsy}}</ref> Sellers can choose which payment options to offer buyers, including [[credit card]]s, debit cards, and [[PayPal]], among others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/cart?ref=si_cart|title=Etsy – Shopping Cart|work=Etsy}}</ref>

=== Buying ===
On the Etsy homepage, potential buyers can type a "product description" into the search bar,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/|title=Etsy – Your place to buy and sell all things handmade, vintage, and supplies|work=Etsy}}</ref> or they can "browse" through a list of options, which includes Art, Home & Living, Jewelry, Women, Men, Kids, Vintage, Weddings, Craft Supplies, Trending Items, Gift Ideas, Mobile Accessories, and more.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/blog/news/2012/better-ways-to-browse-a-new-look-at-the-marketplace|title=Better Ways to Browse: A New Look at the Marketplace|work=etsy.com}}</ref> Furthermore, buyers may choose from a list of categories by clicking on the "categories" link under "More Ways to Shop". This will bring the user to a page of more than 30 categories, each containing subcategories.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/categories|title=Etsy – Browse Shopping Categories|work=Etsy}}</ref>

When a buyer views a product, they can choose to view the positive feedback of each seller to determine the reliability of the shop. Once a buyer finds a product they would like to buy, they click "Add to Cart", and that product is added to their virtual "Shopping Cart". The buyer may then either continue shopping or purchase the selected item. In order to purchase items, buyers do not have to have an account with Etsy and can instead register with [[Facebook]], [[Google Account]], [[Apple Account]], or email.

Etsy has received criticism for its handling of [[customer data]] and [[Internet privacy|privacy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arstechnica.com/business/2011/03/etsy-users-irked-after-buyers-purchases-exposed-to-the-world/?comments=1|title=Etsy users irked after buyers, purchases exposed to the world|date=14 March 2011}}</ref> {{As of|2016||df=|lc=|since=}}, the "[[Privacy policy|Privacy Policy]]" section on the website reads: "By using Etsy, you authorise Etsy to use your information in the United States, Ireland and any other country where Etsy operates".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etsy.com/legal/privacy/|title=Privacy Policy – Our House Rules – Etsy|website=Etsy}}</ref>

== Environmental impact ==
In 2008, Etsy received a B Corporation certification but later lost it in 2017.<ref name=":0">{{cite thesis |id={{ProQuest|2674829587}} |last1=Anderson |first1=Victoria |year=2022 |title=Crafting and Labor: An Investigation of the E-Commerce Giant, Etsy }}</ref> This certification was a recognition of the company abiding by transparent and accountable practices, which includes environmental practices.<ref name=":0" /> The environmental impact from depends greatly on the individual seller usage of wholesale retailer and large manufacturers.<ref name=":0" /> In Etsy's Supplier Code of Conduct, it states that sellers are obligated to follow environmental laws and regulations and that sellers must conduct business in a sustainable and responsible manner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Supplier Code of Conduct - Our House Rules |url=https://www.etsy.com/legal/contractor-guidelines-limited/ |website=Etsy |language=en-US}}</ref> Etsy's 2020 Climate Change Response outlines the company's annual plan for climate related issues and how it achieves the motto of "keep commerce human".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Etsy, Inc. - ESG - ESG Reporting and Resources |url=https://investors.etsy.com/impact-reporting/ESG-Reporting-and-Resources/default.aspx |access-date=2022-11-11 |website=investors.etsy.com}}</ref> In 2019, the board that oversees climate change at Etsy made a goal of becoming a carbon neutral company in 2020.<ref name=":1" /> To achieve this, Etsy is offering eco-friendly packaging to its sellers through a partnership with EcoEnclose.<ref name=":2">{{cite magazine |id={{ProQuest|2575083199}} |title=Etsy Introduces Eco-Friendly Packaging |magazine=Waste360 |date=22 September 2021 }}</ref> This provides sellers with the option to use certified 100% recycled packaging.<ref name=":2" /> Buyers are also given a carbon offsetting option when selecting shipping.<ref name=":03">{{Cite journal |last=Shebell |first=Merissa |date=2019-04-30 |title=Spotsylvania Solar: A Stakeholder Analysis of Corporate Involvement |url=https://scholarship.richmond.edu/environmentalstudies-seniorseminar/32 |journal=Environmental Studies Senior Seminar Projects}}</ref> Etsy, partnered with multiple companies including Apple, pledged to purchase 165 Megawatts of solar energy through Spotsylvania.<ref name=":03" />  By 2025, Etsy's goal is to reduce energy intensity by 25%.<ref name=":1" />

In 2018, nearly 98% of its carbon impact came from the delivery of goods sold on its platform. Etsy reports that it offsets 100% of its carbon emissions from shipping. These offsets support several verified carbon reduction projects through their partnerships. For example, Etsy helps fund the UPM Blandin Native American Hardwoods Conservation Project, which conserves more than 187,000 acres of forest in Minnesota, absorbing CO<sub>2</sub> and protecting biodiversity. Additionally, they invest in renewable energy initiatives like the Giriraj Wind Power Project in India and the Solar Grouped Project by ACME, which replace fossil fuel-based energy generation with wind and solar power. Etsy has also supported innovative projects such as the {{Proper name|Meridian Magnesium SF6 Reduction}} in the automotive sector, which reduces the use of SF<sub>6</sub>, a greenhouse gas 22,800 times more potent than CO<sub>2</sub>.<ref>{{cite web |title=Meridian SF6 Reduction Project |url=https://3degreesinc.com/insights/meridian-carbon-credit-project/ |website=3Degrees}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Silverman |first=Josh |date=27 February 2019 |title="Etsy Becomes the First Global Ecommerce Company to Completely Offset Carbon Emissions from Shipping." |url=https://medium.com/etsy-impact/etsy-becomes-the-first-global-ecommerce-company-to-completely-offset-carbon-emissions-from-shipping-b8ede4322e44 |access-date=3 October 2024 |website=Medium}}</ref>

In 2013, following pressure by the [[Snow Leopard Trust]] Etsy banned the sale of products made from endangered or threatened animals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nuwer |first=Rachel |title=Etsy Has Banned Sales of Protected Animals’ Fur, Bones, Teeth And Bodies |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/etsy-has-banned-sales-of-protected-animals-fur-bones-teeth-and-bodies-17690856/ |access-date=2026-04-07 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref> Similarly, in April 2026, due to the efforts of the [[Coalition to Abolish the Fur Trade]] (CAFT), Etsy announced that it would be excluding items containing animal fur from its marketplace, beginning on August 11th, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chua |first=Jasmin Malik |date=2026-04-06 |title=Etsy to Ban Fur Sales |url=https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/etsy-fur-ban-animal-rights-1238890619/ |access-date=2026-04-07 |website=WWD |language=en-US}}</ref>
