'''Flipkart Video''' was an India-based [[Over-the-top media service|OTT]] (Over the Top) video streaming platform operated by Flipkart.<ref>{{cite news |last= Abrar|first= Peerzada|title= Flipkart forays into original video content, takes on Amazon and Netflix|url= https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/flipkart-forays-into-original-video-content-takes-on-amazon-and-netflix-119101501471_1.html|access-date=19 January 2020|work= [[Business Standard]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= OTT war heats up: Flipkart takes on Amazon Prime with 'Video Originals'|url= https://brandequity.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/media/ott-war-heats-up-flipkart-takes-on-amazon-prime-with-video-originals/71601175|date=15 October 2019|work= [[The Economic Times]]}}</ref> It was launched in 2019, and formed content partnerships with [[Voot]], [[Arre (brand)|Arre]], [[Viu (streaming service)|Viu]], [[The Viral Fever|TVF]], and Pocket Aces' Dice Media.<ref name="indiatoday">{{cite news |last= Ganjoo|first= Shweta|date= 17 October 2019|title= Flipkart launches Video Originals to take on Amazon Prime video|url= https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/flipkart-launches-video-originals-in-india-1609906-2019-10-16|work= [[India Today]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last= N S|first= Vikas|title= Flipkart forays into original content with mobile-first videos|url= https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/internet/flipkart-forays-into-original-content-with-mobile-first-videos/71596427|access-date=19 January 2020|work= [[The Economic Times]]}}</ref> In October 2019, it announced its first original series ''[[Back Benchers]]'', a [[game show|quiz show]] hosted by [[Hindi cinema|Bollywood]] [[film producer]] and [[film director|director]] [[Farah Khan]],<ref name="livemint" /><ref name="financialexpress" /><ref name="inch42" /> which featured Bollywood actors as students and host Farah as the dean of the figurative school. The show had appearances from Bollywood actors such as [[Anil Kapoor]], [[Shilpa Shetty]],<ref name="Mid-day">{{cite news |title=Farah Khan's quiz show Backbenchers will take you back to school days |url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/farah-khans-quiz-show-backbenchers-will-take-you-back-to-school-days/21916190 |work=[[Mid-Day]] |date=16 October 2019 |language=en|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref> [[Kartik Aaryan]], [[Parineeti Chopra]], [[Ananya Panday]], [[Bhumi Pednekar]], [[Taapsee Pannu]], [[Janhvi Kapoor]], and [[Malaika Arora]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.exchange4media.com/digital-news/farah-khans-quirky-quiz-backbenchers-is-flipkart-video-originals-1st-non-fiction-show-100214.html|title= Farah Khan's quirky quiz Backbenchers is Flipkart Video Originals' 1st non-fiction show|date= 16 October 2019|publisher= Exchange 4 Media|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref>

Flipkart Video is a free video streaming service<ref>{{cite news |last= Bose|first= Mouli|title= How Flipkart's streaming service will be different from Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hotstar, ZEE5|url= https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/technology/how-flipkarts-streaming-service-will-be-different-from-netflix-amazon-prime-video-hotstar-zee5/1667690/|date=7 August 2019|work= [[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]]|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref> that is available within the video section of the Flipkart app.<ref name="livemint">{{cite news |last= Chaudhary|first= Deepti|date= 15 October 2019|title= Flipkart to offer original video content|url= https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/flipkart-to-offer-original-video-content-11571137220758.html|work= [[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref><ref name="financialexpress">{{cite news |title= Flipkart forays into original video content to take on Amazon Prime, Netflix|url= https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/technology/flipkart-forays-into-original-video-content-to-take-on-amazon-prime-netflix/1736837/|work= [[The Financial Express (India)]]|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref> Flipkart has cooperated with various production houses, including Studio Next and Frames, as well as Sikhya Productions, to offer its library of original series in foreign languages and genres to Flipkart users.<ref name="indiatoday"/><ref>{{cite news |title= Flipkart to launch original video content|url= https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/flipkart-to-launch-original-video-content/article29691597.ece|access-date=19 January 2020|work= [[Business Line]]}}</ref>

===Flipkart Video Original programming===
Flipkart Video Originals features programming in several genres, including [[Action film|action]], comedy, romance, drama, horror, adventure, and others.<ref name="inch42">{{cite news |title= Flipkart Video Originals Are Here: Has Flipkart Got The Timing Right?|url= https://inc42.com/buzz/flipkart-video-originals-launched-has-flipkart-got-the-timing-right/|access-date=19 January 2020|work= inc42}}</ref>

== Criticism ==
On 13 September 2014, a Flipkart deliveryman allegedly molested a housemaid in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Flipkart delivery boy molests maid in Hyderabad|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/140916/nation-crime/article/flipkart-delivery-boy-molests-maid-hyderabad|access-date=15 December 2014|work=Deccan Chronicle|date=14 December 2014}}</ref> The housemaid's employer sued Flipkart for this incident, citing the need for regulations to make offline delivery services safer.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sachitanand |first=Rahul |date=14 December 2014 |title=Women's safety: E-commerce companies need to do more to ensure quality of offline workforce |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/retail/womens-safety-e-commerce-companies-need-to-do-more-to-ensure-quality-of-offline-workforce/articleshow/45506321.cms |access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref>

In 2014, competitors such as [[Future Group]] (owner of retail chain [[Smart Bazaar|Big Bazaar]] at that time) filed complaints with India's [[Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India)|Ministry of Commerce and Industry]], alleging that Flipkart's Big Billion Days discounts [[Predatory pricing|undercut prices in a manner predatory to other retailers]]. The ministry stated that it would look into the complaints.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Anand |first1=Shambhavi |last2=Malviya |first2=Sagar |date=8 October 2014 |title=Future Group's Kishore Biyani, vendors accuse Flipkart of undercutting to destroy competition |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/services/retail/future-groups-kishore-biyani-vendors-accuse-flipkart-of-undercutting-to-destroy-competition/articleshow/44637244.cms |access-date=18 February 2015 |work=The Economic Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=8 October 2014 |title=Centre to look into complaints against Flipkart sale |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/features/smartbuy/tech-news/sitharaman-will-look-into-complaints-on-flipkart-discount-sale/article6481305.ece |access-date=18 February 2015 |work=Business Line}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Mookerji |first=Nivedita |date=9 October 2014 |title=Big Billion Day sale cost Flipkart big; govt takes notice |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/billion-day-sale-cost-flipkart-big-govt-sits-up-114100900029_1.html |access-date=18 February 2015 |work=Business Standard}}</ref>

In April 2015, Flipkart faced criticism for being a launch partner in the [[Airtel Zero]] program. Critics alleged that the [[zero-rating]] scheme violated the principles of [[net neutrality]]. Flipkart later pulled out of the project.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Balasubramanian |first=Shyam |date=14 April 2015 |title=Flipkart Pulls Out of Airtel Deal Amid Backlash Over Net Neutrality |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/flipkart-pulls-out-of-airtel-deal-amid-backlash-over-net-neutrality-754829 |access-date=5 February 2019 |website=NDTV}}</ref>

In 2015, around 400 delivery executives working with [[Ekart|eKart]], the logistics arm of Flipkart, went [[Strike action|on strike]] to protest poor working conditions. Complaints included seven-day workweeks, extended hours, and a lack of clean toilets and medical assistance for bike riders involved in accidents.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Singh |first=Dipti |date=2 August 2015 |title=Logistics staff go on strike, Flipkart, Myntra in a fix |language=en-US |work=The Indian Express |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/companies/logistics-staff-go-on-strike-flipkart-myntra-in-a-fix/ |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> In 2016, delivery executive Nanjunda Swamy was allegedly murdered by a customer who did not have enough money to pay for a product.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Khanna |first=Anahita |date=15 December 2016 |title=Flipkart Delivery Man Murdered For ₹12,000 Cellphone In Bengaluru |language=en-IN |work=HuffPost India |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.in/2016/12/15/flipkart-delivery-man-murdered-for-12-000-cellphone-in-bengalur_a_21628355/ |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> In response, Flipkart launched a safety initiative -'Project Nanjunda', named after the deceased executive. This included an SOS button in the mobile app (called the Nanjunda button) that could be used by field executives in case of emergencies.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mashable.com/2017/01/18/flipkart-sos-feature-delivery-boys/#8olxYbb0_gqS|title=A month after delivery boy's murder, Flipkart launches new SOS feature|last=Mitter|first=Sohini|work=Mashable|access-date=9 July 2018|language=en}}</ref>

Vendors on Flipkart have faced several challenges while doing business on the company's marketplace, to the extent that some of them have quit the portal. Some of these challenges include Flipkart's alleged unfair policies towards sellers, the lack of a competent logistics service, and customer returns that are a result of [[consumer fraud]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Menezes |first=Rebecca |date=25 November 2016 |title=Seller Interview – 'We quit Flipkart 3 times due to missing products, order cancellations' Online seller Ravi Chopra shares why quitting Flipkart was needed |url=https://indianonlineseller.com/2016/11/seller-interview-we-quit-flipkart-3-times-due-to-missing-products-order-cancellations-etc-online-seller-ravi-chopra-shares-why-quitting-flipkart-was-needed/ |website=IndianOnlineSeller|access-date=2026-10-20}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
* Flipkart was reported to be at the top in the annual Fairwork India Ratings 2021 - which is a 10-point system that creates a score based on fair pay, conditions, contracts, management, and representation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ola, Uber score poorly in gig-work conditions, Flipkart tops the chart: Fairwork Ratings |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/ola-uber-score-poorly-in-gig-work-conditions-flipkart-tops-the-chart-fairwork-ratings/2393621/ |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=Financialexpress |date=30 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> A total of 11 platforms were evaluated by a consortium of the Centre for IT and Public Policy (CITAPP), International [[International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore|IIIT Bangalore]] and the global Fairwork network. The methodology included qualitative interviews with 19-20 workers in Delhi and Bangalore.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Flipkart tops Fairwork index for gig workers; Ola and Uber come with zero score |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2021/dec/30/flipkart-tops-fairworkindex-for-gig-workers-ola-and-uber-come-with-zero-score-2401216.html |access-date=2022-10-19 |website=The New Indian Express|date=30 December 2021 }}</ref>

'''Hilco Global''' is an American [[financial services]] holding company headquartered in [[Northbrook, Illinois]]. The company has offices throughout the world and provides services to companies, their lenders and professional services advisers across a broad spectrum of business categories including retail, commercial, industrial and financial.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barreto |first=Sergio |date=2025-09-03 |title=ORIX USA acquires majority stake in Hilco Global |url=https://www.alternativeswatch.com/2025/09/03/orix-usa-acquires-hilco-global-majority-stake/ |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=Alternatives Watch |language=en-US}}</ref> It is considered one of the largest [[Distressed securities|distressed investment]] and advisory companies in the world.<ref name=CrainsLiquidGoldf>{{cite news|last1=Strahler|first1=Steven R.|title=Hilco CEO puts on glitz|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20070915/ISSUE01/100028428/hilco-ceo-puts-on-glitz|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Crain's Chicago Business|date=17 September 2007}}</ref>

In 2025, a majority stake in Hilco Global was acquired by ORIX Corporation USA, a subsidiary of Japanese firm [[Orix|ORIX]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORIX USA acquires majority stake in Hilco Global {{!}} Work |url=https://www.torys.com/work/2025/07/cc198179-552e-4c4e-9fde-d1ddb0fe6f9e |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Torys LLP}}</ref> and the company was restructured into two divisions.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |date=2025-09-03 |title=Hilco Global Unveils Operating Structure Following Majority Stake from ORIX - ABF Journal |url=https://www.abfjournal.com/hilco-global-unveils-operating-structure-following-majority-stake-from-orix/ |access-date=2026-05-17 |language=en-US}}</ref> The firm now provides advisory and valuation services on maximizing the value of under-performing and excess retail, consumer products and industrial inventory, real estate, intellectual property, including consumer brands, patents, and accounts receivable. The second division named Hilco Global Capital Solutions is focused on asset-based lending to assist companies with asset monetization.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Brianna |date=2025-09-03 |title=Hilco Global Unveils Operating Structure Following Majority Stake from ORIX |url=https://www.abfjournal.com/hilco-global-unveils-operating-structure-following-majority-stake-from-orix/ |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=ABF Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

==History==
The company was founded in 1987 by Jeff Hecktman as the Hilco Trading Company,<ref name=ABFJournal>{{cite news|title=Hilco Global Unveiled as New Name for Hilco Trading|url=http://www.abfjournal.com/dailynews/hilco-global-unveiled-as-new-name-for-hilco-trading/|accessdate=13 January 2015|publisher=ABF Journal|date=2 July 2013}}</ref> after restructuring his family's industrial supply business and selling off many of the under-performing assets.<ref name=InvestmentNewsOwnLiquid>{{cite news|last1=Strahler|first1=Steven|title=Wall Street firms eye Hilco Trading|url=http://www.investmentnews.com/article/20060911/SUB/609110702/wall-street-firms-eye-hilco-trading|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Investment News|date=11 September 2006}}</ref> The company was renamed Hilco Global in 2013, eliminating the use of the name Hilco Trading Company, as well as introducing a new logo and website for the company.<ref name=ABFJournal/>

In 2006, it was announced that [[Goldman Sachs|Goldman Sachs Group]] and [[Cerberus Capital Management]] were in talks to purchase a significant stake in the company.<ref name=InvestmentNewsOwnLiquid/> Hecktman sold part of the company to both investment firms to help finance other ventures, including [[private equity]] style buyouts of faded consumer brands.<ref name=CrainsLiquidGoldf/>

From 2019 until 2023, a 27% stake in Hilco Global was owned by the [[Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec]] (CDPQ), a Canadian company which manages public pension and insurance funds.<ref name="PhillyInq">{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/business/philadelphia-energy-solutions-refinery-hilco-sale-closes-20200626.html|title=A Chicago company has finalized its purchase of the bankrupt Philly refinery|author=Maykuth|publisher=|accessdate=30 September 2020|first=Andrew|date=2024-03-15|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In May 2019, Hilco subsidiary H19 Capital acquired the assets of 19th Capital Group, an Indianapolis transportation and truck leasing company.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.insideindianabusiness.com/story/42125435/hilco-global-acquires-indy-truck-leasing-company|title=Hilco Global Acquires Indy Truck Leasing Company|author=Mary Willkom|publisher=Inside Indiana Business|accessdate=30 September 2020}}</ref>

===Hilco Merchant Resources / Hilco Consumer - Retail===
In 2000, Hilco Global founded a business division named Hilco Merchant Resources LLC, a subsidiary of the company that specializes in retail inventory valuation, retail store closings, retail inventory disposition, fixture, furniture, and equipment disposition, and asset protection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hilco Launches Wholesale Inventory Disposition Business - Article {{!}} ABL Advisor |url=https://www.abladvisor.com/articles/2551/hilco-launches-wholesale-inventory-disposition-business |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=www.abladvisor.com}}</ref> Michael Keefe and Cory Lipoff, formerly of [[Gordon Brothers Group|Gordon Brothers]], joined HMR the same year with Keefe becoming the CEO.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Baeb|first1=Eddie|title=Science and art of the closeout|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20010120/ISSUE01/100015748/science-and-art-of-the-closeout|accessdate=16 December 2014|publisher=Crain's Business Chicago|date=20 January 2001}}</ref> In 2001, the division became known as one of the top five liquidation firms in the United States, having been involved in the $1.8 billion liquidation of [[Montgomery Ward]] following that company's bankruptcy.<ref name=CrainsCloseout>{{cite news|last1=Baeb|first1=Eddie|title=Science and art of the closeout|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20010120/ISSUE01/100015748/science-and-art-of-the-closeout|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Crain's Chicago Business|date=22 January 2001}}</ref> Some of its most notable disposition and liquidation deals included work for [[Sears]], [[Sears Canada]], [[CompUSA]], [[Sports Authority|Sportmart]], [[Phar-Mor|PharMor Rx]], [[Coldwater Creek (clothing retailer)|Coldwater Creek]], [[Charming Charlie]], and [[Target Canada]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Copeland family selling, Sports Authority / Hilco stalking horse bidder|url=http://www.snewsnet.com/news/copeland-family-selling-sports-authorityhilco-stalking-horse-bidder/|accessdate=24 November 2014|publisher=S News net|date=3 November 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Brohan|first1=Mark|title=Hilco puts two iconic e-commerce brands up for bid|url=https://www.internetretailer.com/2013/07/15/hilco-puts-two-iconic-e-commerce-brands-bid|accessdate=24 November 2014|publisher=Internet Retailer|date=15 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Bathon|first1=Michael|title=Coldwater Creek Liquidation Auction Won by Hilco, Gordon|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2014-05-06/coldwater-creek-liquidation-auction-won-by-hilco-gordon.html|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|date=6 May 2014}}</ref> In 2016, the division helped save [[Aéropostale (clothing)|Aéropostale]] from final liquidation, eventually allowing the retailer to restructure and reopen over 500 stores.<ref name="ChainStoreAge">{{cite news | url=https://www.chainstoreage.com/article/teen-apparel-retailer-reopens-00-plus-stores/ | title=Teen apparel retailer reopens 500-plus stores | work=Chain Store Age | date=January 11, 2017 | accessdate=February 10, 2018 | author=Wilson, Marianne | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180212014946/https://www.chainstoreage.com/article/teen-apparel-retailer-reopens-00-plus-stores/ | archive-date=February 12, 2018 | url-status=dead }}</ref> As [[Toys "R" Us]] stores closed in 2018, Hilco Merchant Resources oversaw the nearly $2 billion liquidation of their inventory and assets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20180518/ISSUE01/180519860/hilco-profits-from-demise-of-retailers-toys-r-us-bon-ton|title=Retail bankruptcies mean big business for this company|author=Alby Gallun|publisher=Crain's Chicago Business|accessdate=30 September 2020}}</ref> Hilco Merchant Resources also expanded its operations by opening an office in Australia, taking on retail inventory liquidations of stores that include [[Fletcher Jones (Australian entrepreneur)|Fletcher Jones]],<ref>{{cite news|last1=Butler|first1=Ben|title=Fletcher Jones stock to be liquidated|url=http://www.smh.com.au/business/fletcher-jones-stock-to-be-liquidated-20120127-1ql59.html|accessdate=19 November 2014|newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=27 January 2012}}</ref> Dubbo Everyday Living<ref>{{cite news|title=Staff hit by store closure|url=http://www.dailyliberal.com.au/story/93800/staff-hit-by-store-closure/|accessdate=19 November 2014|newspaper=The Daily Liberal|date=12 March 2012}}</ref> and [[Dick Smith (retailer)|Dick Smith]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.com.au/dick-smith-is-closing-down-2016-2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226124113/http://www.businessinsider.com.au/dick-smith-is-closing-down-2016-2|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 26, 2016|title=DICK SMITH IS GONE -- 3000 staff lose jobs -- stock sell-off today|last=Tucker|first=Harry|work=Business Insider|date=26 February 2016}}</ref>

ReStore for Retail, a Hilco Global company, introduced a mobile [[visual merchandising]] and operations software to aid the working of the frontline store associates and managers and update the in-store shopping experience.<ref>{{cite news |title=ReStore for Retail Gives Collaborative Power to Store Associates, Managers |url=https://wwd.com/business-news/business-features/restore-for-retail-empowers-store-associates-managers-1235803883/ |work=WWD |date=13 September 2023}}</ref>

===ReStore Capital===
In 2019, Hilco Global launched ReStore Capital which resolves shipping and stocking problems between vendors and retailers. ReStore Capital buys shipments from vendors and then consigns the goods to retailers.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://wwd.com/business-news/financial/restore-capital-hilco-financing-retail-fashion-coronavirus-1203628476/|title=Restore Capital Steps In With Financing Fixes|author=Evan Clark|publisher=WWD|accessdate=30 September 2020}}</ref>

===Hilco Real Estate===
Hilco Global founded its real estate business division in 2000 with the formation of Hilco Real Estate, LLC, to be a national provider of accelerated real estate disposition and advisory services.<ref name=CREDcoFoundLeave>{{cite news|last1=Schroedter|first1=Andrew|title=Co-founder leaves Hilco Real Estate|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/realestate/20081212/CRED03/200032221/co-founder-leaves-hilco-real-estate|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Chicago Real Estate Daily|date=12 December 2008}}</ref> It has acted as agent or principal for numerous real estate acquisitions and sales. It was co-founded by Mitchell Kahn who served as the company's CEO until 2008.<ref name=CREDcoFoundLeave/> Kahn was replaced by Neil Aaronson as CEO and Gregory Apter was promoted to President of the company.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schroedter|first1=Andrew|title=Co-founder leaves Hilco Real Estate|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/realestate/20081212/CRED03/200032221/co-founder-leaves-hilco-real-estate|accessdate=16 December 2014|publisher=Chicago Real Estate Daily|date=12 December 2008}}</ref> Hilco Real Estate was responsible for numerous large transactions in real estate including 1,200 leases for [[MCI Worldcom]] that the company either sold or renegotiated.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Muto|first1=Sheila|title=How Hilco Helps MCI Unload Its Properties|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB105830605753506400|accessdate=19 November 2014|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|date=16 July 2003}}</ref> It also closed hundreds of [[Blockbuster LLC|Blockbuster]] stores following the company's 2010 bankruptcy as well as approximately 200 [[Borders (retailer)|Borders]] following that company's 2011 bankruptcy.<ref name=WSJblockbusterdraws>{{cite news|last1=Spector|first1=Mike|title=Blockbuster Auction Draws Liquidators|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704587004576242993096839556|accessdate=19 November 2014|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|date=5 April 2011}}</ref> Hilco Real Estate was also involved with the selling of over 165 unused properties owned by [[Hostess (snack cakes)|Hostess]] after that company filed for bankruptcy in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Judge OKs Hilco to sell Hostess' real estate, other assets|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/realestate/20130108/CRED03/130109813/judge-oks-hilco-to-sell-hostess-real-estate-other-assets|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Chicago Real Estate Daily|date=8 January 2013}}</ref>

Hilco Global expanded its real estate business in 2012 with the formation of Hilco Real Estate Finance LLC, a lending division of Hilco Real Estate.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Matthews|first1=David Lee|title=Targeting small investors for big profits|url=http://www.chicagobusiness.com/realestate/20131008/CRED0701/131009810/targeting-small-investors-for-big-profit|accessdate=13 January 2015|publisher=Chicago Real Estate Daily|date=8 October 2013}}</ref> Hilco Real Estate Finance operated as a private real estate mortgage lending company and in a year and a half had originated loans in approximately 20 states. Hilco Real Estate Finance was sold to the private equity firm Garrison Investment Group in 2014.<ref name=housingWireSale>{{cite news|last1=Lane|first1=Ben|title=Hilco Real Estate Finance sold, rebrands as Jordan Capital Finance|url=http://www.housingwire.com/articles/31882-hilco-real-estate-finance-sold-rebrands-as-jordan-capital-finance|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Housing Wire|date=29 October 2014}}</ref>

In August 2023, WeWork hired Hilco Global and Hilco Real Estate as an adviser for restructuring advice to avoid a Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing and restructuring the company's debts out of court.<ref>{{cite news |title=WeWork tapping advisers for restructuring help |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/wework-tapping-advisers-restructuring-help-bloomberg-news-2023-08-23/ |work=Reuters |date=23 August 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

===Hilco Capital===
[[File:HMV, Kirkgate, Wakefield (10th March 2013) 002.JPG|thumb|An HMV store in Wakefield closed as part of the group administration, prior to the purchase by [[Hilco Capital]]]]
In 2000, Hilco Global launched [[Hilco Capital]] in the United Kingdom to support retail restructuring and distressed investments.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Neal|first1=Dave|title=Music store HMV breaks ground with MP3 download store|url=http://www.theinquirer.net/inquirer/news/2301172/music-store-hmv-breaks-ground-with-mp3-download-store|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018092138/http://www.theinquirer.net/inquirer/news/2301172/music-store-hmv-breaks-ground-with-mp3-download-store|url-status=unfit|archive-date=October 18, 2013|accessdate=24 November 2014|publisher=The Inquirer|date=17 October 2013}}</ref>   
[[File:Blockbuster Store Closing, Ypsilanti Township, Michigan.JPG|thumb|Blockbuster Store Closing, Ypsilanti Township, Michigan]]

===Hilco Valuation Services===
In 2001 Hilco Global formed a business unit called Hilco Appraisal Services LLC, bundling all of the industrial, retail and real estate appraisal services of the holding company into a single unit. Later renamed Hilco Valuation Services, the company is based in the U.S. and has global offices in the U.K., Canada, Australia, Mexico, South American and Asia. One of this units most notable deals was completed in 2005 with the valuation of 29 locations of over 40 million square feet owned by Delphi Automotive.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hilco Global Opens New Valuation Services Office in Sydney|url=http://www.abladvisor.com/press-releases/5456/hilco-global-opens-new-valuation-services-office-in-sydney|accessdate=20 November 2014|publisher=ABL Advisor|date=18 September 2014}}</ref>

===Hilco Receivables===
2001 was also the year Hilco Global expanded its holdings with the formation of Hilco Receivables LLC, a division that purchases [[bad debt]] and services [[accounts receivable]].<ref name=Debt200>{{cite news|title=Debt Purchaser Hilco Receivables Opens 200-Person Collection Call Center|url=http://www.insidearm.com/uncategorized/debt-purchaser-hilco-receivables-opens-200-person-collection-call-center/|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Inside Arm|date=12 September 2006}}</ref> By 2004, Hilco Receivables had acquired more than $2 billion in receivables and in 2006 it opened a 200-person collection center that operated under the name Apex Financial, LLC.<ref name=Debt200/> The company also provides receivable appraisals to lenders as well as financing to companies who acquire receivables portfolios. One of the most notable transactions involving Hilco Receivables was the purchase of $25 million in account receivables from [[National Envelope Corporation]] after its bankruptcy in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Santo|first1=Jamie|title=Bankrupt National Envelope Brings In $65M With 3-Way Sale|url=http://www.law360.com/articles/466915/bankrupt-national-envelope-brings-in-65m-with-3-way-sale|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Law 360}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Bathon|first1=Michael|title=NE Opco Wins Approval to Sell Assets for $70 Million|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-09-11/ne-opco-wins-approval-to-sell-assets-for-70-million.html|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|date=11 September 2013}}</ref>

===Hilco Retail Consulting===
In 2004, Hilco Global acquired a retail strategic consulting practice from [[Arthur Andersen]] called Senn Delaney – SD Consulting. In 2013, the consulting practice was rebranded as Hilco Retail Consulting or HRC Advisory,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilson|first1=Marianne|title=Survey: Retailers not using consumer data to boost omnichannel shopping efforts|url=http://www.chainstoreage.com/article/survey-retailers-not-using-consumer-data-boost-omnichannel-shopping-efforts|accessdate=20 November 2014|publisher=Chain Store Data|date=29 September 2014}}</ref> and in 2021, it was sold to [[Accenture]] with the team in North America joining Accenture's Retail Strategy group.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Ben |title=Chicago-area retail consultancy HRC Retail Advisory acquired by Accenture |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/chicago/news/2021/07/28/chicago-area-retail-consultancy-hrc-acquired-by-ac.html |work=[[Chicago Business Journal]] |date=July 28, 2021}}</ref>  
[[File:Bankruptcy Shop.jpg|thumb|A Linens 'n Things store notifying customers "Going out of Business"]]

===Hilco Consumer Capital===
Hilco Brands was formed from the initial investment as an extension of Hilco Consumer Capital, another company held by Hilco Global. One of the first brands purchased was [[Halston]], a notable fashion line that became popular in the 1970s. Additional brands purchased by Hilco include the Ram and Tommy Armour golf club lines, both companies that were previously based in Chicago,<ref name=CrainsLiquidGoldf/> as well as [[Le Tigre (clothing brand)|Le Tigre]], Haute Hippie, Portico, Under the Canopy, [[Linens 'n Things]], and [[Polaroid Corporation|Polaroid]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Timberlake|first1=Cotten|title=Linens 'N Things Marks Bought by Hilco, Gordon|url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2009-02-06/linens-n-things-marks-bought-by-hilco-gordon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130203212143/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2009-02-06/linens-n-things-marks-bought-by-hilco-gordon|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 3, 2013|accessdate=19 November 2014|magazine=Bloomberg Businessweek|date=6 February 2009}}</ref> Hilco then sold the Polaroid brand and its related intellectual property in 2017 to the Smolokowski family, a Polish group of investors.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dpreview.com/news/7106292979/polaroid-sold-to-new-owner|title=Polaroid sold to new owner|author=Allison Johnson|publisher=Digital Photography Review|accessdate=30 September 2020}}</ref> In 2017, Hilco Brands invested in the startup company StreetTrend LLC, a luxury sneaker producer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.worldfootwear.com/news/former-stuart-weitzman-ceo-back-in-business/2861.html|title=Former Stuart Weitzman CEO back in business|publisher=World Footwear|accessdate=30 September 2020}}</ref>

===Hilco Streambank===
Hilco Streambank is an additional subsidiary added to the Hilco Global family in 2011. The company was formed to provide services for intellectual property brands such as [[Borders (retailer)|Borders]], Posh, Tots,<ref name=TimesDispatchPost>{{cite news|last1=Gilligan|first1=Gregory J.|title=Firm hired to sell PoshTots business|url=http://www.timesdispatch.com/business/firm-hired-to-sell-poshtots-business/article_e03ff5e4-0d43-5014-8535-a5af4e7726ce.html|accessdate=20 November 2014|newspaper=Times Dispatch|date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Linens N’ Things and Circuit City.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hallman|first1=Randy|title=Circuit City name is for sale, again|url=http://www.newsadvance.com/work_it_lynchburg/news/circuit-city-name-is-for-sale-again/article_8fd9e71c-ebf9-11e2-b2d2-001a4bcf6878.html?mode=jqm|accessdate=20 November 2014|publisher=News Advance|date=13 July 2013}}</ref> Hilco Streambank is also known for its [[IPv4]] auction marketplace used for the purchase and sale of IPv4 assets.<ref>{{cite web |title=IPv4 Global - Experienced IP Brokers |url=https://ipv4.global |website=IPv4 Global |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, Hilco Streambank helped [[Johnson Publishing]] organize an auction for their [[Ebony (magazine)|Ebony]] and [[Jet (magazine)|Jet]] magazine photograph archive after Johnson went bankrupt.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2019/07/23/historic-ebony-and-jet-photo-auction-continue-wednesday/1803859001/|title=Historic Ebony and Jet photo auction to continue Wednesday after 'truly remarkable' participation|author=N'dea Yancey-Bragg|publisher=USA Today|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref> Hilco Streambank also managed the intellectual property sale for [[Charming Charlie]] in 2019 after they went bankrupt including their trademarks, domain names, customer data, and social media assets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/houston/news/2019/09/13/charming-charlie-founder-bids-to-buy-brand-ip.html|title=Charming Charlie founder bids to buy brand, IP assets out of bankruptcy|author=Olivia Pulsinelli|publisher=Houston Business Journal|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref> In 2020, Hilco Streambank managed the marketing and selling of all [[Earth Fare]] stores, leases, and intellectual property after they filed for bankruptcy.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://chainstoreage.com/earth-fare-stores-leases-intellectual-property-even-recipes-sale|title=Earth Fare stores, leases, intellectual property — even recipes — for sale|author=Marianne Wilson|publisher=Chain Store Age|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref>

In 2023, IPv4.Global, a Hilco Global company and an IPv4 marketplace, brokered {{US dollar|1 billion|link=yes}} in IPv4 address sales.<ref>{{cite news|title=IPv4.Global Hits $1 Billion Milestone for IPv4 Sales |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ipv4global-hits-1-billion-milestone-for-ipv4-sales-301894658.html |work=PR Newswire |date=7 August 2023}}</ref>

===Hilco Industrial===
Hilco Global's Industrial unit, Hilco Industrial LLC, made national news in 2014 with its involvement in the disposition of excess municipal transportation assets for the City of Detroit following the city's [[Detroit bankruptcy|bankruptcy]],<ref>{{cite news|last1=Martinez|first1=Shandra|title=Grand Rapids auction company to help sell of Detroit's surplus transportation fleet|url=http://www.mlive.com/business/west-michigan/index.ssf/2014/09/grand_rapids_auction_company_h.html|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=MLive|date=12 September 2014}}</ref> the largest municipal bankruptcy filing in the history of the United States.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Guillen|first1=Joe|last2=Bomey|first2=Nathan|title=Detroit's Future? More cops, firefighters, but fewer people|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2014/07/16/detroit-bankruptcy-future/12749719/|accessdate=19 November 2014|newspaper=USA Today|date=16 July 2014}}</ref> Prior to its involvement with the City of Detroit, Hilco Industrial played a role in the sale of Chrysler and GM plants in 2010.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shea|first1=Bill|title=Double-decker trolley car, trucks, buses part of massive Detroit equipment auction|url=http://www.crainsdetroit.com/article/20141029/NEWS/141029834/double-decker-trolley-car-trucks-buses-part-of-massive-detroit|accessdate=19 November 2014|publisher=Crain's Detroit Business|date=29 October 2014}}</ref> In Australia, Hilco Industrial liquidated the last remaining automotive manufacturing plant on the continent, Toyota Altona.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wardsauto.com/industry/machinery-auction-set-toyota-australia-nears-end-car-production|title=Machinery Auction Set as Toyota Australia Nears End of Car Production|author=Alan Harman|publisher=Wards Auto|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref>

===Hilco Redevelopment Partners===
In 2012, Hilco Redevelopment Partners (HRP) bought the [[Sparrows Point, Maryland|Sparrows Point Steel Mill]] in Maryland to demolish and rebuild as a warehouse distribution hub, renamed Tradepoint Atlantic. The deal has operated in partnership with Baltimore-based investment firm Redwood Capital Partners.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wood|first1=Pamela|title=Sparrows Point owner, government reach cleanup agreement|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/09/18/sparrows-point-owner-government-reach-cleanup-agreement/|access-date=19 November 2014|newspaper=The Baltimore Sun|date=18 September 2014}}</ref><ref name=PhillyInq/> In 2017, HRP bought the Crawford Generating Station in [[Little Village, Chicago]], to transform the space into an updated distribution center called Exchange 55.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-07-30/turning-a-dead-coal-plant-into-a-hip-waterfront-experience|title=Turning a Dead Coal Plant Into a Hip Waterfront Experience|author=Will Wade|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://negociosnow.com/site-of-little-village-power-plant-to-be-transformed-by-minority-run-business/|title=Site of Little Village power plant to be transformed by minority-run business|publisher=Negocios Now|accessdate=1 October 2020}}</ref> After the [[Philadelphia Energy Solutions]] refinery burned down and went bankrupt in 2019, HRP bought the plant for $225.5 million.<ref name=PhillyInq/> Hilco will carry out the dismantling of the plant and an extensive remediation effort before beginning projects on the site.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Saul |first1=Josh |title=How to Tear Down an Oil Refinery in the Middle of Philadelphia |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2021-decommissioned-philadelphia-oil-refinery/?srnd=premium&sref=CIpmV6x8 |access-date=30 September 2021 |work=Bloomberg |date=30 September 2021}}</ref>

In October 2020, Hilco was hired by Shop Vac Corp. for liquidation services.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maykuth |first=Andrew |date=2020-11-09 |title=Shop Vac abruptly went out of business in September and 437 Pa. employees are still looking for answers |url=https://www.inquirer.com/business/shop-vac-closure-covid-layoffs-williamsport-miller-20201109.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, HRP began the construction of the first phase of The Bellwether District's South Philadelphia site to convert the industrial site into an e-commerce and logistics campus.<ref>{{cite news |last1=D'Onofrio |first1=Mike |title=First phase of South Philly's new Bellwether District to soon begin |url=https://www.axios.com/local/philadelphia/2023/01/13/bellwether-district-south-philadelphia-first-phase |work=Axios |date=January 13, 2023}}</ref>

In August 2023, WeWork Inc. partnered with Hilco for real estate restructuring with hundreds of landlords.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Basu |first=Reshmi |date=2023-08-23 |title=WeWork Taps Restructuring Advisers in Effort to Stave Off Bankruptcy |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-08-23/wework-taps-advisers-for-restructuring-help-amid-viability-doubt |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240207022201/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-08-23/wework-taps-advisers-for-restructuring-help-amid-viability-doubt |archive-date=2024-02-07 |access-date=2026-07-28 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2024, Hilco worked with [[Pitney Bowes|Pitney Bowes Global]] to acquire its struggling e-commerce business.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garland |first=Max |date=2024-09-17 |title=Pitney Bowes Global Ecommerce laying off more than 1,200 |url=https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/pitney-bowes-global-ecommerce-layoffs/727215/ |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=[[Supply Chain Dive]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The company oversaw a [[Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] and liquidation of their e-commerce segment and assets.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Church |first=Steven |date=2024-08-09 |title=Pitney Bowes to Liquidate E-commerce Unit in Bankruptcy |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-08-08/pitney-bowes-to-liquidate-ecommerce-unit-in-bankruptcy |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-07-28 |work=[[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In September 2025, Hilco Global finalized the spinoff of Hilco Redevelopment Partners property unit with plans to launch a {{US dollar|250 million|link=yes}} investment fund.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wong |first=Natalie |date=2025-09-08 |title=Hilco Spins Out Property Arm With Plans for $250 Million Fund |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-08/hilco-spins-out-property-arm-with-plans-for-250-million-fund |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-11 |work=[[Bloomberg L.P.]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Acquisition by Orix and restructuring===
In July 2025, Hilco Global announced that [[Orix|ORIX]] Corporation USA would be buying a 70% equity stake, at a valuation near {{US dollar|1 billion|2025|link=yes}}.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Klein |first=Jodi Xu |date=2025-07-03 |title=Exclusive {{!}} Hilco Global to Sell Majority Stake, Launch Direct Lending Unit |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/hilco-global-to-sell-majority-stake-launch-direct-lending-unit-fec71b23 |access-date=2026-05-17 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Hilco Global became a subsidiary of Orix USA with a new structure focused on professional services and asset management, including new funding commitments.<ref name=":02" /><ref name=":1" /> The deal was set to position Hilco's background in asset valuation with global capital management infrastructure by Orix.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cavanagh |first=Cassidy |date=2026-04-10 |title=ORIX-Backed Hilco Global Expands Asset-Based Lending Platform |url=https://www.themiddlemarket.com/latest-news/orix-backed-hilco-global-expands-asset-based-lending-platform |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=www.themiddlemarket.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: History of IBM
======================================================================

{{Short description|none}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=April 2012}}
{{AI-generated|date=December 2025}}

[[IBM|International Business Machines Corporation]] (IBM) is a [[multinational corporation]] specializing in computer technology and information technology consulting. Headquartered in [[Armonk, New York|Armonk]], New York, the company originated from the amalgamation of various enterprises dedicated to automating routine business transactions, notably pioneering [[punched card]]-based [[unit record equipment|data tabulating machines]] and [[time clock]]s. In 1911, these entities were unified under the umbrella of the [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company|Computing-Tabulating-Recording]] Company (CTR).

[[Thomas J. Watson]] (1874–1956) assumed the role of [[general manager]] within the company in 1914 and ascended to the position of President in 1915. By 1924, the company rebranded as "International Business Machines". IBM diversified its offerings to include [[electric typewriter]]s and other office equipment. Watson, a proficient salesman, aimed to cultivate a highly motivated, well-compensated sales force capable of devising solutions for clients unacquainted with the latest technological advancements.

In the 1940s and 1950s, IBM began its initial forays into [[computing]], which constituted incremental improvements to the prevailing card-based system. A pivotal moment arrived in the 1960s with the introduction of the [[IBM System/360|System/360]] family of [[mainframe computer]]s. IBM provided a comprehensive spectrum of [[Hardware random number generator|hardware]], [[software]], and [[Service Agreement|service agreements]], fostering client loyalty and solidifying its moniker "[[Big Blue]]". The customized nature of [[End-user development|end-user software]], tailored by in-house [[programmer]]s for a specific brand of [[computer]]s, deterred brand switching due to its associated costs. Despite challenges posed by clone makers like [[Amdahl Corporation|Amdahl]] and legal confrontations, IBM leveraged its esteemed reputation, assuring clients with both hardware and system software solutions, earning acclaim as one of the esteemed American corporations during the 1970s and 1980s.

However, IBM encountered difficulties in the late 1980s and 1990s, marked by substantial losses surpassing $8 billion in 1993. The mainframe-centric corporation grappled with adapting swiftly to the burgeoning [[Unix]] [[Open systems architecture|open systems]] and personal computer revolutions.<ref>Jim Spohrer, "IBM's service journey: A summary sketch". ''Industrial Marketing Management'' 60 (2017): 167–72.</ref> Desktop machines and [[Unix]] midrange computers emerged as cost-effective and easily manageable alternatives, overshadowing multi-million-dollar [[Mainframe computer|mainframes]]. IBM responded by introducing a [[Unix]] line and a range of personal computers. The competitive edge was gradually lost to clone manufacturers who offered cost-effective alternatives, while [[Integrated circuit|chip]] manufacturers like [[Intel]] and software corporations like [[Microsoft]] reaped significant profits.

Through a series of strategic reorganizations, IBM managed to sustain its status as one of the world's largest computer companies and systems integrators. As of 2014, the company boasted a [[workforce]] exceeding 400,000 employees globally<ref>{{cite web |title=Worldwide IBM Research Locations |date=February 6, 2007 |url=http://www.research.ibm.com/worldwide/ |access-date=2014-09-26 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> and held the distinction of possessing the highest number of patents among U.S.-based technology firms.<ref>{{cite web |title=IBM, Fortune 500, 2015 |url=http://fortune.com/fortune500/ibm-24/ |access-date=2015-09-26 |work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]|date=June 4, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="patents">{{cite web |date=January 10, 2006 |title=IBM maintains patent lead, moves to increase patent quality |url=http://www.ibm.com/news/us/en/2006/01/2006_01_10.html |publisher=[[IBM]]}}</ref> IBM maintained a robust presence with research laboratories dispersed across twelve locations worldwide. Its extensive network comprised [[scientist]]s, [[engineer]]s, consultants, and sales professionals spanning over 175 countries.<ref>{{cite web |title=2014 IBM Annual Report |url=http://www.ibm.com/investor/att/pdf/IBM_Annual_Report_2014.pdf |access-date=2015-09-26 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> IBM employees were recognized for their outstanding contributions with numerous accolades, including five [[Nobel Prize]]s, four [[Turing Award]]s, five [[National Medal of Technology and Innovation|National Medals of Technology]], and five [[National Medal of Science|National Medals of Science]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Awards & Achievements |date=February 6, 2007 |url=http://www.research.ibm.com/resources/awards.shtml |access-date=August 13, 2009 |publisher=IBM}}</ref>{{TOC limit |3}}

==1880s–1924: The origin of IBM==
{{Main|Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company}}

[[IBM]] traces its roots to the 1880s through the consolidation of four predecessor companies:<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bennett |first1=Frank P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BQkhAQAAMAAJ&pg=RA4-PA26 |title=United States Investor |date=1911 |volume=22, Part 2 |page=1298 (26)}}</ref><ref>Belden, Martin; Belden, Marva (1961). ''The Life of Thomas J. Watson'', Little, Brown; p. 92</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company (1911–1924) |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/logo/logo_4.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041221233509/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/logo/logo_4.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 21, 2004}}</ref><ref>Maney, Kevin; Hamm, Steve; O'Brien, Jeffrey M. (2011). ''Making the World Work Better: The Ideas That Shaped a Century and a Company'', IBM Press; p. 19</ref>

# [[Bundy Manufacturing Company]]:
#* Founded in 1889 by [[Harlow E. Bundy House|Harlow Bundy]] in [[Binghamton, New York]], as the first manufacturer of [[time clock]]s.
# [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company#Tabulating Machine Company|Tabulating Machine Company]]:
#* Initiated by [[Herman Hollerith]], who began building [[punch card]]-based [[unit record equipment|data processing machines]] as early as 1884.
#* Founded the [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company|Tabulating Machine Company]] in 1896 in [[Washington, D.C.]]
# [[International Time Recording Company]]:
#* Founded in 1900 by [[George Winthrop Fairchild]] in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]], and reincorporated in 1901 in [[Binghamton, New York|Binghamton]], later relocating to [[Endicott, New York]] in 1906.
# [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company#Computing Scale Company of America|Computing Scale Company of America]]:
#* Established in 1901 in Dayton, Ohio.

[[File:Tabulating Machine Co. plant.jpg|thumb|Hollerith's plant in 1893|276x276px]]

The [[U.S. Census Bureau]] contracted to use [[Herman Hollerith]]'s [[Unit record equipment|punched card tabulating technology]] on the [[1890 United States census]]. That census was completed in 6-years and estimated to have saved the government $5 million.<ref><nowiki>Report of the Commissioner of Labor In Charge of The Eleventh Census to the Secretary of the Interior for the Fiscal Year Ending June 30, 1895. Washington, D.C., July 29, 1895. p. 9: {{You may confidently look for the rapid reduction of the force of this office after the 1st of October, and the entire cessation of clerical work during the present calendar year.</nowiki>&nbsp;<nowiki>... The condition of the work of the Census Division and the condition of the final reports show clearly that the work of the Eleventh Census will be completed at least two years earlier than was the work of the Tenth Census.}} Carroll D. Wright Commissioner of Labor in Charge</nowiki></ref> The total population of 62,947,714, the family, or ''rough'', count, was announced after only six weeks of processing (punched cards were not used for this tabulation).<ref>[[Leon E. Truesdell|Truesdell, Leon E.]] (1965) The Development of Punch Card Tabulation in the Bureau of the Census 1890–1940, US GPO, p. 61</ref><ref>(Austrian, 1982, p. 69)</ref> Hollerith's [[punched card]]s become the tabulating industry standard for input for the next 70 years, and were initially sold as ''The Tabulating Machine Company''.{{Citation needed|date=March 2024}} In 1906, Hollerith made the first tabulator with an automatic card feed and control panel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Computing at Columbia: Timeline – Early |url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/computinghistory/#early |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=Columbia.edu}}</ref> Hollerith later expanded to private businesses in the [[United States]] and abroad. In 1911, due to declining health, Hollerith sold the business to financier [[Charles Ranlett Flint|Charles Flint]] for $2.3 million.<ref>[http://www.officemuseum.com/data_processing_machines.htm Officemuseum.com] – early Hollerith history, with good photographs of period equipment</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IBM Archives: Charles R. Flint |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/builders/builders_flint.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051215184848/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/builders/builders_flint.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 15, 2005}}</ref>

On June 16, 1911, Flint merged the four companies into a new holding company named the [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company]] (CTR), headquartered in [[Endicott, New York|Endicott]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Appendix to Hearings Before the Committee on Patents, House of Representatives, Seventy-Fourth Congress, on H. R. 4523, Part III |date=1935 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_8tFAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA3428 |contribution=Certificate of Incorporation of Computing-Tabulating-Recording-Co |publisher=United States Government Printing Office |orig-year=Incorporation paperwork filed 16 June 1911}}</ref><ref>Martin Campbell-Kelly and William Aspray, ''Computer a History of the Information Machine'' – Second Edition, Westview Press, pp. 37–39 2004</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: Chronological History of IBM 1880s |url=https://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1880.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041211024229/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1880.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 11, 2004 |access-date=September 27, 2015 |publisher=IBM}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Rodgers |first=Williams |title=THINK |publisher=Stein and Day |year=1969 |page=83}}</ref> The consolidation aimed to diversify the company's revenue sources and mitigate risks associated with dependence on a single industry.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}} The consolidated entity initially had 1,300 employees and offices/plants in several locations across the [[United States]] and [[Toronto|Toronto, Ontario]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Flint |first=Charles R. |title=Memories of an Active Life: Men, and Ships, and Sealing Wax |publisher=G.P. Putnam's Sons |year=1923 |page=312}}</ref> The amalgamated companies started manufacturing, and selling or leasing machinery such as commercial scales, industrial time recorders, meat and cheese slicers, tabulators, and punched cards.<ref>Certificate of Incorporation of Computing-Tabulating-Recording-Co, 14th day of June 1911</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Pugh |first=Emerson W. |title=Building IBM: Shaping an Industry and Its Technology |publisher=MIT Press |year=1995 |isbn=978-0-262-16147-3 |pages=24–27}}</ref> The individual companies continued operating under their established names as subsidiaries of CTR until the holding company was [[Dissolution (law)|dissolved]] in 1933.<ref>The last page of this ref shows continued use of established names. The 2nd ref shows the consolidation into IBM in 1933 [http://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/text/Knuth_Don_X4100/PDF_index/k-9-pdf/k-9-u2669-IBM-Inventory-Simplified.pdf The Inventory Simplified] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004230834/http://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/text/Knuth_Don_X4100/PDF_index/k-9-pdf/k-9-u2669-IBM-Inventory-Simplified.pdf|date=October 4, 2013}}, published in 1923, states: "The Tabulating Machine Company – Division of – International Business Machines Corporation".</ref>

To strengthen the management of CTR, Flint recruited [[Thomas J. Watson Sr.]], formerly general sales manager of the [[National Cash Register Company]] (NCR). Watson joined CTR as general manager on May 1, 1914. While at NCR, Watson had been convicted with other company executives in a federal antitrust case; the conviction was subsequently overturned on appeal in 1915.<ref>{{cite book
 |last=Maney
 |first=Kevin
 |title=The Maverick and His Machine: Thomas Watson, Sr. and the Making of IBM
 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons
 |year=2003
 |isbn=978-0471230528
}}</ref> He became president of CTR Monday, March 15, 1915.<ref>Maney (2003) p. 57</ref> Watson's managerial strategies and emphasis on customer service and large-scale tabulating solutions propelled revenue growth and expanded the company's operations globally.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

In 1916, CTR started investing in its subsidiary's employees, creating an education program. Over the next two decades, the program expanded to include management education, volunteer study clubs, and the construction of the IBM Schoolhouse in 1933.<ref>Pugh (1995) p. 57</ref> In 1917, CTR expanded to Brazil, invited by the Brazilian Government to conduct the census.<ref>{{cite web |title = IBM Archives: Frequently Asked Questions |page= 15|publisher= IBM |url= http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/faq.pdf|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20050514230534/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/faq.pdf|url-status= dead|archive-date= May 14, 2005}}</ref> In 1920, the Tabulating Machine Co. made their printing tabulator. With prior tabulators the results were displayed and had to be copied by hand.<ref>{{cite web |title = IBM Archives: 1920 |publisher= IBM |url= http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1920.html|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20050117192831/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1920.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= January 17, 2005|date= January 23, 2003 }}</ref> In 1923, CTR acquired majority ownership of the German tabulating firm Deutsche Hollerith Maschinen Groupe ([[Dehomag]]).{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

Watson had never liked the hyphenated title of Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company and chose the new name of "International Business Machines Corporation" (IBM) both for its aspirations and to escape the confines of "office appliance". The new name was first used for the company's Canadian subsidiary in 1917, and was formally changed on February 14, 1924.<ref name="Belden 1962 p.125">Belden (1962) p. 125</ref> The subsidiaries' names did not change; there would be no IBM labeled products until 1933 (below) when the subsidiaries are merged into IBM. Under Watson's leadership, he established key initiatives that shaped IBM's organizational culture, including hiring disabled workers, promoting employee education, and fostering a culture of thinking ("THINK" was a slogan made in 1915<ref>Rodgers, William; ''THINK: A Biography of the Watsons and IBM'' Stein and Day, New York, p. 52.</ref>). His Open Door Policy and initiatives to support employees and their families became integral aspects of IBM's culture.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

==1925–1929: IBM's early growth==
{{blockquote|Our products are known in every zone. Our reputation sparkles like a gem. We've fought our way through and new fields we're sure to conquer too. For the ever-onward IBM|"Ever Onward", IBM employee songbook{{r|greenwald19830711}}}}

{| class="wikitable" style="float: right;"
|-
! Year || Gross income (in $m) || Employees
|-
| 1925 || 13 || 3,698
|}

[[Thomas J. Watson]], during his tenure at IBM, implemented strict [[guideline]]s for employees, encompassing a dress code stipulating dark suits, white shirts, and striped ties. The consumption of alcohol, whether during working hours or otherwise, was prohibited. Watson actively led singing sessions during meetings, featuring songs such as "Ever Onward" from the official IBM songbook.{{r|greenwald19830711}} Additionally, the company initiated the publication of an employee newspaper named Business Machines, consolidating coverage of all IBM businesses into one publication.<ref name="IBM1924">{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1924 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1924.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050117192736/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1924.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 17, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref>

Several employee recognition programs were introduced, including the Quarter Century Club<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=First quarter Century Club |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2051.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050122185802/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2051.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 22, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> to honor those with 25 years of service and the Hundred Percent Club<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=Hundred Percent Club "main tent" |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2054.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050113162806/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2054.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 13, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> to reward sales personnel meeting annual quotas. In 1928, IBM launched the Suggestion Plan program,<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1988 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1988.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041216110621/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1988.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2004 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> providing cash rewards to employees for valuable ideas aimed at improving IBM products and procedures. Over a span of 70 years, IBM and its predecessor companies specialized in manufacturing clocks and other time recording products,<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: IBM Time Device |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/attic3/attic3_0153.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060821084318/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/attic3/attic3_0153.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 21, 2006 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM's swing era oldies (vol. 1) |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/swingera/swingera_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050116150535/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/swingera/swingera_1.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 16, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> culminating in the 1958 sale of the IBM Time Equipment Division to [[Simplex Time Recorder Company]].<ref name="IBM 1958">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060909005625/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/cc/pdf/cc_2407PR02.pdf IBM Archives: Text of IBM's October 24, 1958 press release] announcing the sale of its time equipment (clocks, et al.) business to Simplex Time Recorder Company.</ref> This division produced a range of equipment, including dial recorders, job recorders, recording door locks, time stamps, and traffic recorders.

IBM expanded its product line through innovative engineering, driven by notable inventors such as [[James W. Bryce]], [[Clair Lake (inventor)|Clair Lake]],<ref>{{cite book |last=Bashe |first=Charles J. |url=https://archive.org/details/ibmsearlycompute00bash/page/8 |title=IBM's Early Computers |author2=Pugh, Emerson W. |author3=Johnson, Lyle R. |author4=Palmer, John H. |publisher=MIT Press |year=1986 |isbn=0-262-02225-7 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/ibmsearlycompute00bash/page/8 8–34]}}</ref> Fred Carroll,<ref>{{cite web |title=IBM Archives/Business Machines: Fred M. Carroll |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/builders/builders_carroll.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060904123900/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/builders/builders_carroll.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 4, 2006 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref> and Royden Pierce.<ref>Bashe (1986) pp. 9–14</ref> Significant product innovations were introduced, including the first complete school time control system<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1920s |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1920.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041216110223/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1920.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2004 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> and the first printing tabulator<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1920 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1920.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050117192831/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1920.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 17, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> in 1920. In 1923, the company pioneered the first electric keypunch.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archive: 1923 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1923.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050117192513/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1923.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 17, 2005 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref> The Carroll Rotary Press introduced in 1924 revolutionized the production of punched cards by achieving record-setting speeds.<ref name="IBM1924" /> In 1928, IBM introduced the 80-column [[punched card]], known as the "[[IBM card|IBM Card]]", effectively doubling its information capacity.<ref name="IBM1928">{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1928 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1928.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050117192707/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/year_1928.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 17, 2005 |access-date=May 29, 2011 |publisher=IBM}}</ref> This format became an industry standard until the 1970s.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

Key events in IBM's history during this period include the first tabulator sold to [[Japan]] in 1925, through a partnership with Morimura-Brothers.<ref name="morimura_history">
{{cite web |title=History |url=http://www.morimura.co.jp/english/history/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204031632/http://www.morimura.co.jp/english/history/ |archive-date=February 4, 2014 |access-date=2014-02-01 |work=morimura.co.jp |publisher=Morimura Brothers, Inc. |df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref name="ibm.com">{{cite web |title=History of Innovation on the 75th anniversary of founding IBM Japan |url=http://www-06.ibm.com/ibm/jp/75th/index2.shtml |access-date=2014-02-01 |work=ibm.com |publisher=IBM}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IBM Highlights, 1885–1969 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/1885-1969.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051215062527/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/1885-1969.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 15, 2005 |access-date=2014-02-01 |work=ibm.com |publisher=IBM}}</ref> IBM established its presence in Italy by opening its first office in Milan in 1927, facilitating operations with national insurance and banks. A significant advancement in tabulator technology occurred in 1928 with the introduction of the Hollerith Type IV tabulator capable of subtraction.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM 301 Accounting Machine (the Type IV) |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/attic2/attic2_122.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060826033153/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/attic2/attic2_122.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 26, 2006 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref> This year also marked the debut of the Hollerith 80-column punched card, a format that became an industry standard, superseding the prior 45-column card and eventually ending vendor compatibility.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

==1930–1938: The Great Depression==
{| class="wikitable" style="float: right;"
|-
! Year || Gross income (in $m) || Employees
|-
| 1930 || 19 || 6,346
|-
| 1935 || 21 || 8,654
|}

The 1930s [[Great Depression]] posed an extraordinary economic test, yet IBM displayed resilience by maintaining investments in personnel, manufacturing, and technological advancements during this challenging period. Rather than downsizing its workforce, Watson opted to hire additional salesmen and engineers in alignment with President Franklin Roosevelt's National Recovery Administration plan.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}
[[File:Social Security, "Keeping Individual Old-Age Insurance Records" - NARA - 195883.tif|left|thumb|204x204px|IBM accounting machines in operation at the U.S. [[Social Security Administration]] {{circa|1936}}]]
During this era, IBM emerged as a pioneering corporation by instituting employee benefits such as group life insurance (1934), survivor benefits (1935), and paid vacations (1936). The company furthered its commitment to education and research by establishing the IBM Schoolhouse in Endicott and constructing a modern research laboratory at the same location. Watson's strategic decisions during this time represented IBM's initial 'Bet the Company' gamble, marked by substantial internal investments to secure the future.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

In an effort to manage the strain on resources caused by factories running at maximum capacity for six years without a market to sell to, IBM opted to sell the struggling Dayton Scale Division (food services equipment business) to Hobart Manufacturing in 1933.<ref>{{cite book |last=Rogers |first=William |title=THINK: A Biography of the Watsons and IBM |publisher=Stein and Day |year=1969 |page=108}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Maney |first=Kevin |url=https://archive.org/details/maverickhismachi00mane |title=The Maverick and His Machine |publisher=Wiley |year=2003 |isbn=0-471-41463-8 |page=[https://archive.org/details/maverickhismachi00mane/page/154 154] |url-access=registration}}</ref> An opportune moment arrived with the enactment of the [[Social Security Act of 1935]], hailed as "the biggest accounting operation of all time",<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: 1930s |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1930.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041216110832/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/history/decade_1930.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2004 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref> wherein IBM secured the exclusive bid by promptly providing the necessary equipment. This landmark government contract involved maintaining employment records for 26 million individuals, propelling IBM's success and paving the way for additional government orders. By the decade's end, IBM had not only navigated through the Depression but had also ascended to a prominent position in the industry.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

Watson's visionary focus on international expansion emerged as a pivotal aspect of IBM's 20th-century growth and triumph. Influenced by the devastating impact of World War I on society and businesses, he advocated for commerce as a deterrent to war, emphasizing the compatibility of business interests and peace. Watson's belief was so strong that he inscribed his slogan "World Peace Through World Trade" on the façade of IBM's new World Headquarters (1938) in New York City.<ref name="world hq">{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archives: World Headquarters, N.Y. City |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2045.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050122185120/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2045.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 22, 2005 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=IBM Archives}}</ref> This phrase became a fundamental IBM business tenet, and Watson actively campaigned for this idea with international business and government leaders. He played a role as an informal government host to visiting world leaders in New York and received numerous awards from foreign governments in recognition of his efforts to enhance international relations through the establishment of business connections.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}

[[File:IBM Homestead Endicott, NY A.jpg|thumb|IBM Homestead in Endicott, NY, circa 1930s]]
[[File:IBM Model A typewriter (1).jpg|thumb|An IBM Model A typewriter]]
In 1936, following a loss at the US Supreme Court, IBM agreed to a [[#1936Decree|consent decree]] which created a separate market for the punched cards and in effect for subsequent computer supplies such as magnetic tapes and disk packs.

===Key events===

==== 1931 ====
* The first Hollerith punched card machine capable of multiplication is introduced, known as the Hollerith 600 Multiplying Punch.<ref>{{cite book |last=Bashe |first=Charles J. |url=https://archive.org/details/ibmsearlycompute00bash/page/14 |title=IBM's Early Computers |author2=Johnson, Lyle R |author3=Palmer, John H. |author4=Pugh, Emerson W. |publisher=MIT |year=1986 |isbn=0-262-02225-7 |page=[https://archive.org/details/ibmsearlycompute00bash/page/14 14]}}</ref>
* The first Hollerith alphabetical accounting machine, the Alphabetic Tabulator Model B, was swiftly followed by the full alphabet ATC.<ref name="Pugh 1995 p.50">Pugh (1995) p. 50</ref>
* The ''[[New York World]]'' newspaper coins the term "Super Computing Machine" to describe the Columbia Difference Tabulator, a specialized tabulator-based machine created for the Columbia Statistical Bureau. It was exceptionally massive and earned the nickname "Packard". Institutions such as the Carnegie Foundation, [[Yale University]], [[Harvard University]], and others became users.<ref>{{cite book |last=Eames |first=Charles |title=A Computer Perspective |author2=Eames, Ray |publisher=Harvard University Press |year=1973 |location=Cambridge, Mass |page=95}} The date given, 1920, should be 1931 (see the Columbia Difference Tabulator web site)</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=March 1, 1920 |title=Columbia Difference Tabulator |url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/computinghistory/packard.html |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=Columbia.edu}}</ref><ref>''Columbia Alumni News'', Vol. XXIII, No. 11, December 11, 1931, p. 1</ref>

==== 1933 ====
* Subsidiary companies merge into IBM, leading to the disappearance of names like the [[Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company|Tabulating Machine Company]].<ref>''The New York Times'', July 15, 1933, All subsidiaries of the International Business Machines Corporation in this county have been merged with the parent company to obtain efficient operation.</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=William |last=Rodgers |url=https://archive.org/details/thinkbiographyof00rodg |title=THINK: A Biography of the Watsons and IBM |publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson |year=1969 |isbn=9780297000235 |page=[https://archive.org/details/thinkbiographyof00rodg/page/83 83] |url-access=registration}}</ref>
* IBM introduces removable control panels.<ref name="jeanbellec">{{cite web |title=Date |url=https://jeanbellec.pagesperso-orange.fr/information_technology_1.htm |website=jeanbellec.pagesperso-orange.fr}}</ref>
* IBM implements a standard [[40-hour work week]] for both manufacturing and office locations.{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}
* IBM purchases the [[IBM Electromatic typewriter|Electromatic Typewriter Co.]], primarily to secure essential patents. [[Typewriter|Electric typewriters]] later become one of IBM's prominent products.<ref>Rogers (1969) p. 108</ref><ref>[[Typewriter#Early electric models]]</ref>

==== 1934 ====
* IBM establishes a group [[life insurance]] plan for all employees with at least one year of service.<ref>{{cite web |title=IBM highlights 1885–1996 |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/1885-1969.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051215062527/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/documents/pdf/1885-1969.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 15, 2005 |access-date=July 11, 2023}}</ref>
* Watson Sr. transitions IBM's factory employees to a salary-based payment system, eliminating [[piece work]] and enhancing economic stability for employees and their families.<ref>{{cite book |last=Watson |first=Thomas J. Jr. |url=https://archive.org/details/fathersoncomylif00wats_0/page/73 |title=Father, Son & Co.: my life at IBM and beyond |author2=Petre, Peter |publisher=Bantam |year=1990 |isbn=0-553-07011-8 |page=[https://archive.org/details/fathersoncomylif00wats_0/page/73 73]}}</ref>
* IBM introduces the IBM 801 Bank Proof machine, a new type of proof machine that improved the efficiency of the check clearing process.<ref>{{cite web |title=Industry Player Business Simulation Game |url=http://www.industryplayer.com/licenceinfo.php?li |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220115407/http://www.industryplayer.com/licenceinfo.php?licid=014000 |archive-date=February 20, 2012 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=Industryplayer.com |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

==== 1935 ====
* During the [[Great Depression]], IBM maintains production of new machines, positioning the company to win a significant [[government]] contract related to the [[Social Security Act]], termed "the biggest accounting operation of all time".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ssa.gov/history/ibm.html|title=Social Security History|website=www.ssa.gov}}</ref>

==== 1936 ====
* IBM agreed to [[#1936Decree|1936 consent decree]].

==== 1937 ====
* IBM establishes a tabulating machine data center at [[Columbia University]], known as the [[Thomas J. Watson]] Astronomical Computing Bureau, dedicated to scientific research.<ref>Pugh (1995) p. 72</ref>
* IBM introduces the first [[collator]], the IBM 077 Collator.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 27, 1957 |title=IBM 077 Collator |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV4004.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060909184555/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV4004.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 9, 2006 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref>
* IBM produces five to ten million punched cards every day, employing 32 presses in [[Endicott, New York|Endicott, N.Y]]., for this purpose.<ref name="Endicott">{{cite web |date=January 23, 2003 |title=IBM Archive: Endicott card manufacturing |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2159.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050122192348/http://www-03.ibm.com/ibm/history/exhibits/vintage/vintage_4506VV2159.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 22, 2005 |access-date=April 24, 2012 |publisher=03.ibm.com}}</ref>
* [[Rey Johnson]] of IBM designs the [[IBM 805 Test Scoring Machine]], revolutionizing the test scoring process with innovative [[Mark sense|pencil-mark sensing]] technology and the phrase, "Please completely fill in the oval."<ref>Pugh (1995) pp. 70–71</ref>
* Watson Sr., as president of the [[International Chamber of Commerce]], presides over the [[International Chamber of Commerce|ICC]]'s 9th Congress in Berlin and received a [[Order of the German Eagle|Merit Cross of the German Eagle with Star]] medal from the [[Government of Nazi Germany|Nazi government]], later returned.<ref>{{cite book |last=Maney |first=Kevin |url=https://archive.org/details/maverickhismachi00mane |title=The Maverick and His Machine: Thomas Watson Sr., and the Making of IBM |publisher=Wiley |year=2003 |isbn=978-0-471-41463-6 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/maverickhismachi00mane/page/207 207–10] |url-access=registration}}</ref><ref>[[IBM and the Holocaust]], [[Edwin Black]], 2001 Crown / Random House. see index.</ref>
* IBM announces a policy of paying employees for six annual holidays, marking one of the first instances of holiday pay in U.S. companies.
