'''JD.com, Inc.''', also known as '''Jingdong Group''' ({{zh|p=Jīngdōng Jítuán|s=京东集团}}), formerly called '''360buy''',<ref name=":0">[http://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/chinas-b2c-e-commmerce-giant-141116445.html China's B2C E-commerce Giant 360buy Rebrands] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215211629/https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/chinas-b2c-e-commmerce-giant-141116445.html |date=15 December 2017 }}, Retrieved 3 December 2013</ref> is a Chinese [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[technology company]] specializing in [[E-commerce in China|e-commerce]], retail, Internet, and technology. The company headquartered in [[Beijing]]. With revenues more than US194 billion in 2025,<ref name="JD2025Filing" /> JD.com is China's largest retailer by revenue, and ranks 47 on [[Fortune Global 500]]. It is one of the two massive [[B2C]] online retailers in China by transaction volume and revenue, and is a major competitor to [[Alibaba Group|Alibaba]]-run [[Tmall]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sampi.co/selling-on-jd-com-in-china-infographic/ |title=Selling on JD.com in China |website=Sampi |date=14 October 2015 |access-date=20 March 2016 |archive-date=6 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506043752/http://sampi.co/selling-on-jd-com-in-china-infographic/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Qu |first=Tracy |date=2024-06-11 |title=Alibaba’s New E-Commerce Strategy Faces Tough Competition |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/alibabas-new-e-commerce-strategy-faces-tough-competition-243356a6 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250916074036/https://www.wsj.com/tech/alibabas-new-e-commerce-strategy-faces-tough-competition-243356a6 |archive-date=September 16, 2025 |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> JD.com's portfolio spans across retail, technology, logistics, health care, industrials, property management, private label, insurance, and international business.<ref name=SEC>{{cite web|url=https://fortune.com/company/jd-com/|title=JD.com|website=Fortune|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ir.jd.com/static-files/8d40e85a-72ec-4796-8bbc-eb5edd09c78a|title=FORM 20-F|website=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> 

The company was founded by [[Liu Qiangdong]] on 18 June 1998, and its [[retail]] platform went online in 2004. It originally sold [[magneto-optical]] products, but soon diversified, selling a wide range of electronics, including mobile phones, computers, and similar items among others. The company changed its domain name to 360buy.com in June 2007 and then to JD.com in 2013.<ref name=Domain>{{cite web|url=https://domaininvesting.com/jd-com-acquired-5-million-usd/|title=JD.com: Was it Acquired for $5 Million USD? - DomainInvesting.com|date=17 February 2014|access-date=19 June 2018|archive-date=27 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327095609/https://domaininvesting.com/jd-com-acquired-5-million-usd/|url-status=live}}</ref> At the same time, JD.com announced its new logo and mascot.

== History ==
===Early years===
The company was founded in 1998 as Jingdong, which was named after Liu Qiangdong's then girlfriend Gong Xiaojing and himself.<ref>{{Cite web |title=企业(品牌)详情 |url=http://gp.chinadevelopment.com.cn/portal/enterprise/detail/id/33.html |access-date=10 October 2023 |website=gp.chinadevelopment.com.cn |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109205219/http://gp.chinadevelopment.com.cn/portal/enterprise/detail/id/33.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2004, the company's B2C site went online as jdlaser.com.<ref name=AFM>{{cite web|url=https://asiafundmanagers.com/jd-com-inc/|title=JD.com Inc, the ‘Amazon of China’|website=Asia Fund Managers|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> The company began using the domain name 360buy.com,<ref name=AFM/> and the name was changed to Jingdong Mall in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://agfundernews.com/chinas-jd-leads-70m-round-in-online-fresh-produce-retailer-fruitday|title=China’s JD Leads $70M Round in Online Fresh Produce Retailer FruitDay|website=AFN|date=May 26, 2015|author=Lauren Manning|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> 

In 2007, JD.com established an in-house logistics department in order to provide more reliable and timely delivery service to consumers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.investorinsights.asia/post/jd-logistics-part-1-introducing-jd-logistics|title=JD Logistics (Part 1): Introducing JD Logistics|website=Investor Insights Asia|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/joecornell/2021/04/05/jdcom-to-carve-out-its-logistics-business-via-ipo/|title=JD.com To Carve-Out Its Logistics Business Via IPO|website=Forbes|date=April 5, 2021|author=Joe Cornell|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

Since 2009, JD.com has set up a customer service center in [[Suqian]], cumulatively investing over 30 billion [[Renminbi|RMB]] to build its self-operated customer service center. As a result, the company now operates the industry's largest customer service team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1549802/000110465917028187/a17-4445_120f.htm|title=JD.com, Inc.|website=SEC.gov|access-date=September 7, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1789772519778374813&wfr=spider&for=pc|title=Liu Qiangdong's "Human Touch"|website=Baijiahao|date=February 2, 2024|access-date=September 7, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://finance.sina.com.cn/tech/digi/2024-11-20/doc-incwteuk5321219.shtml|title=JD.com: Over the past 15 years, it has invested more than 30 billion yuan in customer service and has gradually built the industry's largest and highest-quality self-operated customer service team.|website=Finance Sina|date=November 20, 2024|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

On 10 December 2010, JD's founder [[Liu Qiangdong]] announced through his [[Weibo]] account that every book sold on JD.com would be priced at 20 percent cheaper than its competitors.<ref>{{cite web|title=国美苏宁触网 低价合围京东|url=http://tech.ifeng.com/internet/detail_2010_12/13/3474340_0.shtml|url-status=dead|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319084731/http://tech.ifeng.com/internet/detail_2010_12/13/3474340_0.shtml}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=京东被当当激怒 砸8000万促销图书|url=http://tech.ifeng.com/internet/special/360buypkdangdang/content-1/detail_2010_12/16/3543225_0.shtml|url-status=dead|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319004309/http://tech.ifeng.com/internet/special/360buypkdangdang/content-1/detail_2010_12/16/3543225_0.shtml}}</ref> On December 14, 2010, [[Dangdang]] also began to offer discounts to customers and stated that the company would invest 40 million Chinese yuan to give discounts to customers. As a result, JD.com launched the second promotion to sell books at a lower price than Dangdang<ref>{{cite web|title=京东当当图书大战告停 京东准备停止直接降价|url=http://business.sohu.com/20101216/n278333901.shtml|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319004211/http://business.sohu.com/20101216/n278333901.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> and announced that it would give coupons instead of reducing prices to protect the benefits of publishers.<ref>{{cite web|title=京东商城当当网降价大战升级|url=http://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/20101216/02533551165.shtml|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319214515/http://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/20101216/02533551165.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2011, JD.com provided its customers with a 10 percent discount on books, while Dangdang sent promotional messages to its users.<ref>{{cite web|title=价格大战，京东当当快疯了|url=http://finance.people.com.cn/GB/16208755.html|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=22 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222022823/http://finance.people.com.cn/GB/16208755.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The sudden increase of orders not only caused network errors but also postponed transits of books.<ref>{{cite web|title=京东当当展开价格大战 亏损严重仍"争当败家子"|url=http://news.sdchina.com/show/2104460.html|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=2 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802002959/http://news.sdchina.com/show/2104460.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

JD.com started the e-book selling business online on 20 February 2012, and provided customers with more than 80,000 electronic books.<ref>{{cite web|title=电子书之战打响：出版社不满价格低|url=http://book.sina.com.cn/news/v/2012-02-23/0957295472.shtml|url-status=dead|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319003930/http://book.sina.com.cn/news/v/2012-02-23/0957295472.shtml}}</ref> On 17 April 2013, most of the e-books on Dangdang's website were free for users to download.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Liu|first1=Zhenyou|title=互联网+ 助传统行业旁道超车|publisher=中国财政经济出版社}}</ref> Consequently, Dangdang launched its flagship store on JD.com in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/chinese-online-book-retailer-dangdang-to-open-store-on-jdcom|title=Chinese Online Bookseller Dangdang to Open Store on JD.Com|website=YiCai|date=January 10, 2023|author=Lu Hanzhi|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> 

In 2013, the company's domain name was changed to JD.com.<ref name=":0"/><ref name=Domain/>

===Listing===
In 2014, JD.com's [[Nasdaq]] [[Initial public offering|IPO]] raised $1.8 billion USD, valuing the company at approximately $26 billion and making it the largest Chinese company to be listed only in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/94339c88-e138-11e3-b59f-00144feabdc0|title=JD.com raises $1.8bn in Nasdaq IPO|website=Financial Times|date=May 21, 2014|author=Nicole Bullock|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> 

In 2015, JD.com launched its Russian site aimed to expand its business globally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Khrennikov |first=Ilya |date=June 16, 2015 |title=JD.com to Start Russian Shopping Site in Expansion Beyond China |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-06-16/jd-com-starts-russian-e-commerce-website-to-expand-beyond-china |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630225513/http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-06-16/jd-com-starts-russian-e-commerce-website-to-expand-beyond-china |archive-date=30 June 2016 |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Bloomberg |url-status=live }}</ref> 

In November 2017, JD.com achieved a sales record of US$19.1&nbsp;billion.<ref>{{cite news|title=JD.com Ensures Alibaba Doesn't Have Singles Day to Itself|url=http://fortune.com/2017/11/13/its-not-just-alibaba-jd-com-generated-19-billion-in-sales-at-its-rival-event/|work=Fortune|language=en|access-date=3 December 2017|archive-date=4 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171204114511/http://fortune.com/2017/11/13/its-not-just-alibaba-jd-com-generated-19-billion-in-sales-at-its-rival-event/|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2018, it released its spin-off ''JD Finance'', raising $2.1&nbsp;billion in a capital raise.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-03-02/jd-com-to-gain-2-1-billion-from-sale-and-spinoff-of-finance-arm|title=Alibaba-Rival JD to Get $2.1 Billion in Finance Arm Spinoff|website=[[Bloomberg News]]|date=2 March 2017|access-date=19 June 2018|archive-date=27 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127034120/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-03-02/jd-com-to-gain-2-1-billion-from-sale-and-spinoff-of-finance-arm|url-status=live}}</ref> 

In April 2020, the company confidentially filed for a second listing in Hong Kong<ref>{{Cite web|title=Homecoming: E-commerce giant JD.com secretly files for Hong Kong second listing|url=https://www.independent.ie/business/world/homecoming-e-commerce-giant-jdcom-secretly-files-for-hong-kong-second-listing-39169005.html|website=independent|language=en|access-date=30 April 2020|archive-date=15 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815130952/https://www.independent.ie/business/world/homecoming-e-commerce-giant-jdcom-secretly-files-for-hong-kong-second-listing-39169005.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and began trading on the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]] for [[Hong Kong dollar|HK]]$239 in June 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://today.line.me/hk/v2/article/X5B93l|title=JD.com starts trading in Hong Kong|website=XINHUA|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

In 2020, JD.com announced that would be investing $830 million in its JD Health unit, provided by private equity firm [[Hillhouse Investment|Hillhouse Capital]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/fe1d9bc7-bbf0-4e8d-a0e5-7857afa83d0c|title=China's JD.com reports rising profitability and sales growth|work=[[Financial Times]]|last=McMorrow|first=Ryan|date=17 August 2020|access-date=20 August 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024044415/https://www.ft.com/content/fe1d9bc7-bbf0-4e8d-a0e5-7857afa83d0c|url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2020, JD Health's $3.5 billion IPO was Hong Kong's largest initial public offering of the year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-12-08/jd-health-s-debut-is-the-best-by-a-mega-hong-kong-ipo-ecm-watc|title=JD Health’s IPO is the Best by a Mega Hong Kong Debut|website=Bloomberg|date=December 8, 2020 |access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

In 2021, [[JD Logistics]], the [[supply chain management]] and [[logistics]] delivery arm of JD.com, raised HK$24.6 billion ($3.2 billion USD) for its initial public offering, which was the second-largest IPO in 2021. Shares rose by 18% on its first day of trading.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-05-28/jd-logistics-gains-on-debut-after-3-2-billion-hong-kong-ipo?embedded-checkout=true|title=JD Logistics Gains on Debut After $3.2 Billion Hong Kong IPO|website=Bloomberg|date=May 27, 2021|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>

===Recent years===
In May 2023, [[Sandy Xu|Sandy Ran Xu]], who had served as JD.com’s chief financial officer since 2020, became the company’s chief executive officer and an executive director, succeeding Lei Xu. She was the third CEO in JD.com’s history and the first woman to hold the position.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Datta |first=Tiyashi |date=2023-05-11 |title=China's JD.com promotes finance chief to CEO role as Xu Lei resigns |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-jdcom-beats-estimates-quarterly-revenue-2023-05-11/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2023, JD.com began a 4-hour delivery service in Hong Kong.<ref>{{cite web|url=[https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3238265/chinese-online-shopping-giant-jdcom-launches-four-hour-delivery-hong-kong-battle-against-alibabas](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3238265/chinese-online-shopping-giant-jdcom-launches-four-hour-delivery-hong-kong-battle-against-alibabas)|title=Chinese online shopping giant JD.com launches 4-hour delivery in Hong Kong in battle against Alibaba’s Cainiao|website=SCMP|date=October 17, 2023|author=Ben Jiang|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

In September 2024, JD.com launched its global sales business in the United States, Japan, Singapore, and Malaysia.<ref>{{cite web|url=[https://pandaily.com/jd-com-initiates-global-expansion-launches-global-sales-in-four-countries/](https://pandaily.com/jd-com-initiates-global-expansion-launches-global-sales-in-four-countries/)|title=JD.com Initiates Global Expansion, Launches "Global Sales" in Four Countries|website=Pandaily|date=September 2, 2024|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref>

In July 2025, JD.com agreed to acquire German electronics retailer [[Ceconomy]], parent of [[MediaMarkt]] and [[Saturn (store)|Saturn]], for US$2.5&nbsp;billion ({{Euro}}2.2&nbsp;billion).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Inverardi |first=Matthias |last2=Williams |first2=Matthias |date=2025-07-31 |title=China's JD.com to buy Germany's Ceconomy in deal valuing it at $2.5 billion |url=[https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/chinas-jdcom-buy-germanys-ceconomy-deal-valuing-it-25-billion-2025-07-30/](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/chinas-jdcom-buy-germanys-ceconomy-deal-valuing-it-25-billion-2025-07-30/) |access-date=2025-07-31 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> By November 2025, JD.com had successfully secured a majority stake of over 70% in the company.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-11-14 |title=Ceconomy: JD.com sichert sich Mehrheit an MediaMarkt-Saturn-Mutter |url=[https://www.manager-magazin.de/unternehmen/handel/ceconomy-jd-com-sichert-sich-mehrheit-an-mediamarkt-saturn-mutter-a-cf854a4f-2ba8-456d-a505-aa12b5f45c0d](https://www.manager-magazin.de/unternehmen/handel/ceconomy-jd-com-sichert-sich-mehrheit-an-mediamarkt-saturn-mutter-a-cf854a4f-2ba8-456d-a505-aa12b5f45c0d) |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=Manager Magazin |language=de}}</ref>

On September 13, 2025, JD.com was in advanced talks to acquire British catalogue retailer [[Argos (retailer)|Argos]] from [[Sainsbury's]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Access Restricted |url=[https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/09/13/chinese-retail-giant-plots-swoop-for-argos/](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/09/13/chinese-retail-giant-plots-swoop-for-argos/) |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=www.telegraph.co.uk}}</ref> but discussions ended a day later with Sainsbury's keeping Argos after JD.com communicated it would only engage on materially revised terms.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=[https://corporate.sainsburys.co.uk/news/press-releases/termination-of-discussions-with-jdcom-2/](https://corporate.sainsburys.co.uk/news/press-releases/termination-of-discussions-with-jdcom-2/)|title=Termination of discussions with JD.com|date=14 September 2025|access-date=14 September 2025|website=[[Sainsbury's]]}}</ref>

In early 2026, JD.com's aggressive European retail expansion faced mixed regulatory responses. While the German government allowed the Ceconomy takeover to proceed without intervention, France formally blocked JD.com's attempted acquisition of the French electronics chain [[Fnac Darty]] in January 2026 to prevent it from becoming a direct sales channel for Chinese goods.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-30 |title=JD.com: Frankreich blockiert Übernahme |url=[https://elektrobranche.at/artikel/jd-com-frankreich-blockiert-uebernahme/](https://elektrobranche.at/artikel/jd-com-frankreich-blockiert-uebernahme/) |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=ELEKTRObranche.at |language=de}}</ref> Furthermore, in March 2026, the Ceconomy acquisition encountered serious regulatory resistance in Austria under national investment control laws, prompting JD.com to resubmit its application with enhanced legal commitments regarding data protection and the preservation of local jobs.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-03-31 |title=JD.com will in Österreich nach Widerständen den Antrag für die Übernahme von Ceconomy erneut stellen |url=[https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-03/68086110-jd-com-will-in-oesterreich-nach-widerstaenden-den-antrag-fuer-die-uebernahme-von-ceconomy-erneut-stellen-665.htm](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-03/68086110-jd-com-will-in-oesterreich-nach-widerstaenden-den-antrag-fuer-die-uebernahme-von-ceconomy-erneut-stellen-665.htm) |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=FinanzNachrichten |language=de}}</ref>

==Subsidiaries==
===JD Retail===
JD Retail, the company's retail infrastructure provider, offers products and services in five major sectors: home appliances & furnishings, digital products, supermarket, life services, automotive products and services,  fashion & luxury goods – along with independent divisions, such as local retailing and enterprise services.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pandaily.com/jd-retail-initiates-major-organizational-transformation/|title=JD Retail Initiates Major Organizational Transformation|website=Pan Daily|date=April 11, 2023|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

JD Worldwide, its cross-border e-commerce platform, enables and supports international brands and merchants to sell directly to Chinese consumers without requiring an established presence in China.

JD.com opened its first chain of omnichannel supermarkets ''7Fresh''<ref>{{Cite web |title=京东新零售超市7FRESH：将推出4种业态，门店1000家 新官上任三把火5月30日， 京东 7FRESH业务负责人王敬首次对外宣布7FRESH超市业态升级MSSM（Meal So... - 雪球 |url=https://xueqiu.com/7883471364/127561548 |access-date=10 October 2023 |website=xueqiu.com |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109205218/https://xueqiu.com/7883471364/127561548 |url-status=live }}</ref> in January 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Online Retailer JD Follows Alibaba Into the Supermarket Game|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-01-04/online-retailer-jd-follows-alibaba-into-the-supermarket-game|work=Bloomberg|language=en|access-date=20 January 2018|archive-date=7 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407202659/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-01-04/online-retailer-jd-follows-alibaba-into-the-supermarket-game|url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2024, JD NOW announced an on-demand rapid delivery time as fast as nine minutes for products from over 500,000 stores across 2,300 locations in China.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://retailasia.com/e-commerce/news/jdcom-launches-enhanced-jd-now-demand-retail-service|title=JD.com launches enhanced JD NOW on-demand retail service|website=Retail Asia|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

In August 2024, JD.com expanded its apparel branch, JD Fashion, with an investment of RMB 1 billion ($141 million USD).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://moodiedavittreport.com/jd-com-makes-rmb1-billion-us141-million-plunge-into-online-fashion-expansion/|title=JD.com makes RMB1 billion (US$141 million) plunge into online fashion expansion|website=Moodie Davitt Report|date=August 30, 2024|author=Martin Moodie|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>  JD Fashion has partnered with [[Louis Vuitton]], [[Dior]], [[Bulgari]], and [[Givenchy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voguebusiness.com/consumers/jd-louis-vuitton-partnership|title=Louis Vuitton joins China’s JD.com amid online luxury battle|website=Vogue|date=April 14, 2021|author=Annachiara Biondi|access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref>

=== Joybuy ===

In March 2026, JD.com launched '''Joybuy''', its European online retail business, in the [[United Kingdom]], [[Germany]], [[France]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Belgium]] and [[Luxembourg]].<ref>{{cite news |title=JD.com launches Joybuy in Europe, targeting Amazon |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/jdcom-launches-joybuy-europe-targeting-amazon-2026-03-16/ |work=[[Reuters]] |date=16 March 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

The launch formed part of JD.com’s expansion outside China and was described by news organisations as an attempt to compete with [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] and other established ecommerce companies in Europe.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kharpal |first=Arjun |title=JD.com takes on Amazon in Europe as China’s e-commerce titans expand globally |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/16/jd-launches-joybuy-in-europe-amazon-rival.html |work=[[CNBC]] |date=16 March 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

Joybuy started operating as a first-party retailer, purchasing and holding much of the inventory it sells. At launch, it sold products across categories including technology, appliances, beauty, homeware and groceries, including products from international brands.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nott |first=George |title=Joybuy launches in the UK: ‘Our competition is everybody’ |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/joybuy-launches-in-the-uk-our-competition-is-everybody/716475.article |work=[[The Grocer]] |date=16 March 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

In June 2026, it was reported that Joybuy was testing a marketplace service to sell products third-party products as stock, from both European and international brands.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nott |first=George |title=JD.com’s Joybuy to open up to third-party sellers in marketplace model move |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/jdcoms-joybuy-to-open-up-to-third-party-sellers-in-marketplace-model-move/719884.article |work=[[The Grocer]] |date=9 June 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

JD.com developed its own European warehousing and last-mile delivery infrastructure to support Joybuy. At the time of its launch, its logistics network comprised more than 60 warehouses and depots across Europe,<ref>{{cite news |last=STAT Times |title=JD.com launches JoyExpress in Europe to support Joybuy logistics push |url=https://www.stattimes.com/logistics/jdcom-launches-joyexpress-in-europe-to-support-joybuy-logistics-push-1358132 |newspaper=STAT Times |date=11 February 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref> including a 90,000-square-metre fulfillment center in [[Oberhausen]], Germany.<ref>{{cite news |title=Onlinehandel: JD.com will im E-Commerce in Deutschland kräftig expandieren |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/dienstleister/onlinehandel-jd.com-will-im-e-commerce-in-deutschland-kraeftig-expandieren/100207895.html |work=[[Handelsblatt]] |date=16 March 2026 |language=de |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

In the United Kingdom, its logistics infrastructure included warehouses in [[Milton Keynes]] and [[Luton]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Nott |first=George |title=Joybuy launches in the UK: ‘Our competition is everybody’ |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/joybuy-launches-in-the-uk-our-competition-is-everybody/716475.article |work=[[The Grocer]] |date=16 March 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref> 

In eligible metropolitan areas across its active markets, Joybuy offered same-day delivery for orders placed before 11 a.m. and next-day delivery for orders placed before 11 p.m.<ref>{{cite news |last=Woolfson |first=Daniel |title=Inside the $187bn Chinese mega retailer targeting Britain |url=https://www.thetimes.com/business/companies-markets/article/jdcom-187bn-china-retailer-amazon-w3xgrmrwv |work=[[The Sunday Times]] |date=27 June 2026 |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

In France, ''[[Les Echos (France)|Les Échos]]'' reported that Joybuy’s French website received approximately 1.8 million visitors in March 2026 and 1.2 million in April, citing data from [[Médiamétrie]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lemarchand |first=Julia |title=E-commerce : le chinois Joybuy lance son « Black Friday » festival pour exister en Europe face à Amazon |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/conso-distribution/e-commerce-le-chinois-joybuy-lance-son-black-friday-estival-pour-exister-en-europe-face-a-amazon-2236241 |work=[[Les Echos (France)|Les Échos]] |date=11 June 2026 |language=fr |access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

JD.com established JD Logistics (also known as JINGDONG Logistics) to provide smart supply chain and logistics services.<ref>{{cite JD Logistics plans to double its overseas warehouse space by 2025. It currently operates nearly 100 bonded, direct mail, and overseas warehouses spanning 10 million square feet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dcvelocity.com/jd-logistics-to-double-its-overseas-warehouse-space-by-2025|title=JD Logistics to double its overseas warehouse space by 2025|website=DC Velocity|date=October 17, 2024|author=Ben Ames|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

===JD Health===
[[JD Health]] provides [[digital health]] services and resources. It is the [[healthcare]] unit of JD.com.

In May 2019, JD.com announced the establishment of JD Health as a subsidiary for independent operations in the healthcare business.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1633144572261764249&wfr=spider&for=pc|title=JD.com announced that its health business will be operated independently and JD Health will be established as a subsidiary group|website=Baijiahao|date=May 10, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

===JD Technology===
In 2021, the company announced that it had sold JD Cloud, its [[cloud computing]] services, to its [[financial technology]] unit, JD Digits, for a combined valuation of 15.7 billion yuan ($2.4 billion USD).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-jd-com-divestiture/chinas-jd-spins-off-cloud-and-ai-businesses-to-fintech-unit-idUSKBN2BN1KM/|title=China's JD spins off cloud and AI businesses to fintech unit|website=Reuters|date=March 31, 2021|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> 

In July 2023, JD.com unveiled its ChatRhino (or Yanxi, 言犀 in Chinese) [[large language model]] (LLM), tailored to serve various industries. By combining 70% generalized data with 30% native intelligent supply chain data, it offers targeted solutions for real industry challenges across sectors such as retail, logistics, finance, health, and city.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-07-13/jd-com-joins-china-s-ai-race-with-a-model-for-enterprise-use?embedded-checkout=true|title=JD.com Joins China's AI Race With a Model for Enterprise Use|website=Bloomberg|date=July 12, 2023|author=Jane Zhang|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Ochama===
In January 2022, JD.com launched its Europe-based omnichannel retail brand, Ochama in the Netherlands. It operates automated warehouses in the Netherlands, Poland, and France.  Ochama allows shoppers to either collect online orders from any of its designated pick-up points or have them delivered directly to their homes. Its delivery service has expanded to 24 countries across the continent, and it has also introduced 1-hour express delivery in Amsterdam.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/10/chinas-jdcom-opens-first-robotic-shops-in-europe.html|title=Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com sets challenge to Amazon with first ‘robotic shops’ in Europe|website=CNBC|date=January 10, 2022|author=Arjun Kharpal|access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.parcelandpostaltechnologyinternational.com/news/logistics/ochama-opens-polish-warehouse-to-boost-operational-efficiency.html|title=Ochama opens Polish warehouse to boost operational efficiency|website=Parcel and Postage|date=November 1, 2024|author=Hazel King|access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://jingdaily.com/intels/2024-07/18/jd-com-s-ochama-launches-1-hour-delivery-in-amsterdam|title=JD.com’s Ochama launches 1-hour delivery in Amsterdam|website=Jing Daily|access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, Ochama in the Netherlands was officially rebranded as '''Joybuy''', as part of JD.com's broader European repositioning strategy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joybuy Nederland: de nieuwe naam van Ochama (2025) |url=https://chinesewebwinkel.nl/joybuy/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |language=nl-NL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lelieveld |first=Bart |date=2025-08-04 |title=Chinese webwinkel Ochama verandert in Joybuy |url=https://www.distrifood.nl/191246/chinese-webwinkel-ochama-verandert-in-joybuy |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=www.distrifood.nl |language=nl}}</ref>

===JINGDONG Industrials===
JINGDONG Industrials is an industrial supply chain technology and service provider under JD.com. The company initially filed for an initial public offering in Hong Kong in March 2023 and refiled its second IPO application in October 2024 after its first attempt failed due to lackluster market conditions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3280645/jd-industrials-refiles-hong-kong-ipo-plan-ride-china-stocks-wave|title=JD Industrials refiles Hong Kong IPO to ride the big wave of China’s stock market revival|website=SCMP|access-date=April 28, 2025}}</ref>

===JINGDONG Property===
JINGDONG Property is the real estate development, leasing, management, and fund management subsidiary of JD.com.

[[Tencent]] acquired a 15% stake in JD.com in 2014 by paying cash and handing over its e-commerce businesses Paipai & QQ Wanggou plus a stake in Yixun to JD.com, to build a stronger competitor to [[Alibaba Group]] Holding Ltd.<ref>[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2014-03-10/tencent-agrees-to-buy-15-stake-in-jd-com-for-214-7-million Tencent to Buy 15% Stake in JD.com to Boost E-Commerce] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114202009/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2014-03-10/tencent-agrees-to-buy-15-stake-in-jd-com-for-214-7-million |date=14 November 2017 }} // Bloomberg, 10 March 2014</ref> After it opened in 2015 and offered competition to Alibaba's e-commerce sites, it jumped into foreign sales.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wong |first=Gillian |date=2015-04-15 |title=China JD.com Jumps Into Foreign Sales Business as Rival to Alibaba |access-date=2026-03-17 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Their competition was often touted as a 'cat and dog war', with Alibaba at 59% and JD at 23% B2C share.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chu |first=Kathy |last2=Wong |first2=Gillian |date=2015-08-17 |title=Alibaba vs. JD.com: Executives Weigh In In January 2022, JD.com partnered with [[Shopify]] to begin selling Shopify's brands via its cross-border e-commerce site in China.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/18/shopify-and-jd-tie-up-to-let-us-merchants-sell-in-china.html|title=Shopify steps up China expansion through tie-up with e-commerce giant JD.com|website=CNBC|date=18 January 2022|author=Arjun Kharpal|access-date=21 January 2022|archive-date=20 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120183355/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/18/shopify-and-jd-tie-up-to-let-us-merchants-sell-in-china.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In March 2024, JD.com partnered with [[Geopost]] to develop "comprehensive shipping solutions" between China and Europe. Additionally, its partnership with [[Hermes Europe|Evri]] allows European businesses to access JD.com's marketplace, connecting them with Chinese consumers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.parcelandpostaltechnologyinternational.com/news/logistics/jd-logistics-expands-international-express-delivery-service.html|title=JD Logistics expands international express delivery service|website=Parcel and Postal Technology International|date=March 19, 2024|author=Hazel King|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref>

==ESG==
In 2017, JD.com established an anti-corruption coalition with other Chinese internet companies which aims to blacklist individuals engaged in illicit behavior from seeking employment elsewhere in the internet sector.<ref name=":024">{{Cite book |last=Jin |first=Keyu |title=The New China Playbook: Beyond Socialism and Capitalism |date=2023 |publisher=Viking |isbn=978-1-9848-7828-1 |location=New York |pages=114 |author-link=Keyu Jin}}</ref>

In 2017, JD Logistics launched the "Green Stream Initiative," which aims at exploring carbon reduction in its supply chain. In 2020, the initiative partnered with over 200,000 merchants. It has reduced plastic waste by 50,000 tons and paper waste by 1.3 million tons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://daoinsights.com/works/jd-logistics-drive-for-sustainable-deliveries/|title=JD Logistics’ drive for sustainable deliveries|website=Dao|date=July 23, 2020|access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref> 

In September 2017, JD.com committed to further develop China's parcel delivery efficiency, investing US$101&nbsp;million to subsidize merchants on JD.com for warehousing and distribution costs, for the upcoming 2017 [[Singles' Day]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Alibaba, JD.com commit nearly US$330m to beef up parcel delivery efficiency|url=https://www.scmp.com/business/china-business/article/2112072/alibaba-and-jdcom-commit-nearly-us330m-beefing-parcel|work=South China Morning Post|language=en|access-date=21 September 2017|archive-date=21 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921195709/http://www.scmp.com/business/china-business/article/2112072/alibaba-and-jdcom-commit-nearly-us330m-beefing-parcel|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2022,  JD Logistics launched the "Delivered with Original Package" (DWOP) certification, the industry's first standard for original direct packaging on the same day. JD Logistics partnered with brands to ensure that over 80% of packages sold via e-commerce channels are DWOP compliant by 2030.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://finance.sina.com.cn/tech/2022-06-06/doc-imizirau6821792.shtml|title=Release of the Industry's First Original Packaging Certification Standard|website=Sina|date=Jun 6, 2022|access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref> 

JD.com launched its Green Impact Initiative in May 2022, a program which labels eco-friendly products and allows customers to collect "green credits" to use for redeeming products on JD's app.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1733457551993289778&wfr=spider&for=pc|title=JD.com launches the "Green Plan" during the 618 shopping festival, labeling nearly one million products as "green"|website=Baijiahao|date=May 22, 2022|access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref> 

In late 2022, JD upgraded its "Housing Guarantee Fund" for employees with an investment of RMB 10 billion. Since 2023, 77% of the fund's applicants have been frontline workers; JD.com provides support to frontline employees, including social insurance, education, and housing funds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/jd-com-announces-salary-increase-for-over-20-000-customer-service-employees-1033039924|title=JD.com Announces Salary Increase for Over 20,000 Customer Service Employees|website=Business Insider|date=February 7, 2024|access-date=September 7, 2024}}</ref>

'''Kavak''' is a Mexican company that operates a platform for buying, selling, financing, and managing new and used cars and commercial vehicles, for both individuals and businesses.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|title=Used Car Startup Kavak Valued at $8.7 Billion in Funding Round|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-22/used-car-startup-kavak-valued-at-8-7-billion-in-funding-round|access-date=2022-02-04|newspaper=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]|date=22 September 2021 }}</ref><ref name=infobae>{{Cite news |title=Nuevas tecnologías transforman la compraventa de modelos usados en la Argentina |url=https://www.infobae.com/inhouse/2025/06/27/nuevas-tecnologias-transforman-la-compraventa-de-modelos-usados-en-la-argentina/ |work=[[Infobae]] |date=2025-06-27 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref>

It was founded in 2016<ref>{{Cite news |title=Mexico Car Dealer Kavak's Valuation Slashed by $6.5 Billion as Market Sours |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-04-15/mexico-car-dealer-kavak-s-valuation-slashed-by-6-5-billion-as-market-sours |work=Bloomberg|date=2025-04-15 |access-date=2026-02-11}}</ref><ref name=lanacion>{{Cite news |title=Innovación: la planta de reacondicionamiento que marca un antes y un después en la compra y venta de autos usados |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/autos/innovacion-la-planta-de-reacondicionamiento-que-marca-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-la-compra-y-venta-de-nid06052022/ |work=[[La Nación]] |date=2022-05-06 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Dos ex empleados de Linio van por el mercado de autos usados en México |url=https://expansion.mx/emprendedores/2016/10/02/dos-ex-empleados-de-linio-van-por-el-mercado-de-autos-usados-en-mexico |work=[[Expansión (Mexico)|Expansión]] |date=2016-10-02 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref> and is headquartered in [[Mexico City]]. Its founder and CEO is [[Carlos García Ottati]].<ref name="detras">{{Cite news |title=Kavak: la historia detrás del unicornio |url=https://forbes.com.mx/nuestra-revista-kavak-la-historia-detras-del-unicornio/ |work=[[Forbes México]] |date=2025-02-14 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name=quien>{{Cite news |title=Quién es dueño de Kavak |url=https://expansion.mx/empresas/2025/03/11/quien-es-dueno-de-kavak |work=Expansión |date=2025-03-11 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="baja">{{Cite news |title=Valoración de Kavak baja en US$6 500 millones en última ronda de financiamiento |url=https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/mexico/valoracion-de-kavak-baja-en-us6500-millones-en-ultima-ronda-de-financiamiento/ |work=Bloomberg Línea |date=2025-04-15 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Cómo un vendedor de autos usados logró la empresa emergente más valiosa de América Latina |url=https://www.forbesargentina.com/innovacion/como-vendedor-autos-usados-logro-empresa-emergente-mas-valiosa-america-latina-n19448 |work=Forbes Argentina |date=2025-05-26 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Mexico's Kavak drives away with $700M in new funding, doubling its valuation to $8.7B|url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/09/21/mexicos-kavak-raises-700m-for-its-used-car-marketplace-doubling-its-valuation-to-8-7b/|access-date=2022-02-04|website=TechCrunch|language=en-US}}</ref>

== History ==
Initial fundraising began in 2016,<ref name=":0" /> and was conducted through the Mountain Nazca fund. This investment vehicle provided the support needed to hold a first round for [[Mexican peso|MXN$]]3 million, at that time the biggest seed-stage investment ever completed.<ref name="detras"/> The team raised nearly MXN$400 million in three funding rounds between 2016 and 2020, with Kaszek Venture, Mountain Nazca, and [[SoftBank Group|SoftBank]] taking point. Those investments pushed Kavak to a [[United States dollar|US$]]1 billion valuation by the end of 2020, making it [[Mexico]]'s first [[Unicorn (finance)|unicorn]] company.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2020-10-01 |title=SoftBank-backed used-car startup Kavak becomes first Mexican unicorn |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-mexico-kavak-idUKKBN26M6XB |access-date=2022-02-04 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Women and Latin America's Digital Revolution |url=https://www.wilsoncenter.org/blog-post/women-and-latin-americas-digital-revolution |publisher=[[Wilson Center]] |access-date=2026-02-11}}</ref>

Kavak expanded to [[Argentina]] in 2020 after it merged with local startup Checkars.<ref>{{Cite news |title=“Dólar Kavak”: los planes del unicornio que busca revolucionar la venta de autos usados y paga en moneda extranjera|url=https://www.infobae.com/economia/2021/09/22/dolar-kavak-los-planes-del-unicornio-que-busca-revolucionar-la-venta-de-autos-usados-y-paga-en-moneda-extranjera/|work=Infobae |last=Casas|first=Ximena|date=2021-09-22 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Cómo funciona la plataforma que eligen cada vez más argentinos para la compra y venta de autos usados |url=https://www.infobae.com/inhouse/2024/12/31/como-funciona-la-plataforma-que-eligen-cada-vez-mas-argentinos-para-la-compra-y-venta-de-autos-usados/ |work=Infobae |date=2024-12-31 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref>

The company later expanded to [[Brazil]] at the start of 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-27|title=Kavak Boosts its Global Expansion by Investing US$500 Million in Brazil|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210727005845/en/Kavak-Boosts-its-Global-Expansion-by-Investing-US500-Million-in-Brazil|access-date=2022-02-04|website=www.businesswire.com|language=en}}</ref> It achieved a unicorn ranking as the second-most valuable business in [[Latin America]] after raising US$700 million in a Series E round that valued the company at $8.7 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Expande operación unicornio mexicano |url=https://www.mural.com.mx/expande-operacion-unicornio-mexicano/ar2064647 |work=Mural |date=2020-11-05 |last=de la Cruz |first=Estephany |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="baja"/><ref name=reforma>{{Cite news |title=De la adversidad al éxito: resurge con fuerza Kavak |url=https://www.reforma.com/de-la-adversidad-al-exito-resurge-con-fuerza-kavak/gr/ar2640571?md5=a1c3f2140f0d4a2d1bbb80975f4e32bf&ta=0dfdbac11765226904c16cb9ad1b2efe |work=[[Reforma (newspaper)|Reforma]] |date=2023-07-20 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=2021-04-07|title=Mexican used-car startup Kavak hits $4 billion valuation|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-kavak-idUSKBN2BU0FH|access-date=2022-02-04}}</ref> 

In July 2022, the company announced plans to enter [[Chile]], [[Colombia]], and [[Peru]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak, la startup mexicana de autos, se expande fuera de América Latina |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/sectorfinanciero/Kavak-la-startup-mexicana-de-autos-se-expande-fuera-de-America-Latina-20220706-0024.html |work=[[El Economista (Mexico)|El Economista]] |date=2022-07-06 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref>

Kavak began operating in [[Turkey]] in May 2022 under the Carvak brand.<ref name="carvak">{{Cite news |title=Latin Amerikalı start up Türkiye'ye geldi |url=https://www.ekonomist.com.tr/makale/latin-amerikali-start-up-turkiyeye-geldi-33926 |work=Ekonomist |date= |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=tr}}</ref> In 2025, it sold Carvak to Borusan Next, the used-car business of [[Borusan|Borusan Otomotiv]]. Turkey's Competition Authority approved the transaction on 18 September 2025.<ref name="borusan">{{Cite news |title=Borusan Next, Carvak'ı satın aldı |url=https://www.haberturk.com/borusan-next-carvaki-satin-aldi-3833690-ekonomi |work=[[Habertürk]] |date= |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=tr}}</ref> In October 2022, Kavak announced its launch in the [[United Arab Emirates]], [[Oman]] and [[Saudi Arabia]]. In Saudi Arabia, it planned its own operation, with two operational centres in [[Riyadh]].<ref name="bl-gcc">{{Cite news |last=Guarino |first=Lorena |title=Kavak Steers into Dubai, Oman and Saudi Arabia as Mexican Unicorn Chases Growth |url=https://www.bloomberglinea.com/english/kavak-steers-into-dubai-oman-and-saudi-arabia-as-mexican-unicorn-chases-growth/ |work=Bloomberg Línea |date=12 October 2022 |access-date=14 October 2026}}</ref> Its operations in the United Arab Emirates and Oman began after a merger with Carzaty, an Omani used-car platform.<ref name="national-gcc">{{Cite news |title=Generation Start-up: Kavak seeks to own GCC's used-car space after merging with Carzaty |url=https://www.thenational.ae/business/start-ups/2022/12/19/generation-start-up-kavak-seeks-to-own-gccs-used-car-space-after-merging-with-carzaty/ |work=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]] |date=19 December 2022 |access-date=14 October 2026}}</ref>

In November 2023, Kavak announced it would indefinitely suspend its operations in Colombia and Peru starting January 1, 2024, citing the global and local macroeconomic context.<ref name="bl-salida">{{Cite news |title=Kavak anuncia cierre de operaciones en Colombia y Perú: estas son las razones |url=https://www.bloomberglinea.com/2023/11/03/kavak-anuncia-cierre-de-operaciones-en-colombia-y-peru-estas-son-las-razones/ |work=Bloomberg Línea |date=3 November 2023 |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="colombia">{{Cite news |title=Kavak anuncia suspensión de operaciones en Colombia |url=https://es-us.finanzas.yahoo.com/noticias/kavak-anuncia-suspensi%C3%B3n-operaciones-colombia-100000876.html |work=[[Yahoo Finance|Yahoo Finanzas]] |date=2025-01-15 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="peru">{{Cite news |title=Kavak Perú: qué provocó la salida de la plataforma de autos |url=https://www.ecommercenews.pe/comercio-electronico/2024/kavak-peru-que-provoco-la-salida-de-la-plataforma-de-autos.html/ |work=Ecommerce News Perú |date=2024 |access-date=2026-02-11 |language=es}}</ref>

In January 2025, Kavak reported a share of about 1.2% of the used-car market in Mexico, which it estimated at around US$5 million transactions a year.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak planea abrir hasta cinco puntos de venta en México este primer trimestre del año |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/cartera/kavak-planea-abrir-hasta-cinco-puntos-de-venta-en-mexico-este-primer-trimestre-del-ano/ |work=[[El Universal (Mexico City)|El Universal]] |date=7 January 2025 |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=es}}</ref> In November 2025, Kavak launched Kavak Crédito, a credit platform in Mexico.<ref name="credito">{{Cite news |title=Kavak entra al sector fintech con una plataforma de crédito para cerrar la brecha de financiamiento en América Latina |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/cartera/kavak-entra-al-sector-fintech-con-una-plataforma-de-credito-para-cerrar-la-brecha-de-financiamiento-en-america-latina/ |work=[[El Universal (Mexico City)|El Universal]] |date=6 November 2025 |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

In February 2026, Kavak raised US$300 million in a Series F round led by [[Andreessen Horowitz]], which contributed US$200 million. WCM Investment Management co-led the round.<ref name="seriesf">{{Cite news |title=Kavak capta inversiones por 300 millones de dólares para crecer en Latinoamérica |url=https://expansion.mx/empresas/2026/02/17/kavak-capta-inversiones-por-300-millones-de-dolares-para-crecer-en-latinoamerica |work=[[Expansión (Mexico)|Expansión]] |date=17 February 2026 |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak levanta Serie F de 300 millones de dólares liderada por a16z |url=https://dplnews.com/?p=305960 |work=DPL News |date=17 February 2026 |access-date=14 October 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

== Services ==
[[File:Kavak_Lerma.jpg | thumb | right | Kavak main headquarters.]]
Kavak offers [[Used car|new]] and [[Used car|used cars]], [[Service (motor vehicle)|car maintenance]], and personal credit intermediary services.<ref name="baja"/> The company continued to grow its financial segment, initially from Kavak Capital, and then from two new brands: Kuna and Kavak Crédito.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak lanza créditos para comprar auto y obtener liquidez |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2025/11/05/economia/kavak-lanza-creditos-para-comprar-auto-y-obtener-liquidez |work=[[La Jornada]] |date=2025-11-05 |access-date=2026-02-27|language=es}}</ref>

It uses data and [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] to create an algorithm that collects public auto-industry information and internal data to calculate the prices that will be fair for car buyers and sellers.<ref name=reforma/> Through thousands of runs, the algorithm learned to project market trends and assess users' ability to pay, which allowed the company to provide personalized financing options and offers of vehicles.<ref>{{Cite news |title=De unicornio vuela a Pegaso; mexicana Kavak alcanza valor de 8,700 mdd |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/bloomberg-businessweek/2021/09/22/de-unicornio-vuela-a-pegaso-mexicana-kavak-alcanza-valor-de-8700-mdd/ |work=[[El Financiero]] |date=2021-09-22 |access-date=2026-02-27|language=es}}</ref><ref name=infobae/>

In the [[State of Mexico]], Kavak has a vehicle reconditioning facility, which can recondition over 3,500 vehicles per month.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Profeco reconoce a Kavak por sus procesos de conciliación |url=https://www.telediario.mx/economia/profeco-reconoce-a-kavak-por-sus-procesos-de-conciliacion |work=Telediario.mx |date=2025 |access-date=2026-02-27}}</ref> It involves technical check-ups, repair, and quality certification to ensure that the vehicles are up to the standards.<ref name=lanacion/>

== Investors and alliances ==
Kavak has received investments from some major organizations, such as [[Sea Ltd|Sea]],<ref name=aristegui>{{cite web |title=La plataforma mexicana Kavak asegura ser la segunda startup más valiosa de Latinoamérica |url=https://aristeguinoticias.com/2209/dinero-y-economia/la-plataforma-mexicana-kavak-asegura-ser-la-segunda-startup-mas-valiosa-de-latinoamerica/ |website=Aristegui Noticias |date=22 September 2021 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref> [[SoftBank Group|Softbank]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Startup mexicana Kavak se expande en Medio Oriente |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2022/10/12/startup-mexicana-kavak-se-expande-en-medio-oriente/ |website=Infobae |date=12 October 2022 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref> [[Founders Fund]], [[Tiger Global Management|Tiger Global]], [[General Catalyst]], Spruce House, [[Ribbit Capital]], and the D1 hedge fund.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sea, SoftBank join round valuing Mexico's Kavak at $8.7b|url=https://www.techinasia.com/sea-group-invests-mexicobased-kavak-87b-valuation|access-date=2022-02-04|website=[[Tech in Asia]]|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=aristegui/> 

Among the individual investors, the [[Argentines|Argentine]] athlete [[Manu Ginóbili]] stands out.<ref>{{cite web |last=Della Vecchia |first=Franco |title=Emanuel Ginóbili invierte en Kavak: de qué otras empresas ya es accionista |url=https://www.forbesargentina.com/negocios/emanuel-ginobili-invierte-kavak-otras-empresas-ya-accionista-n17043 |website=Forbes Argentina |date=9 June 2022 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref> 

Kavak has entered into various business deals, such as the partnership with the [[Mexican Football Federation]] (FMF) and the [[Argentine Football Association]] (AFA), <ref>{{cite web |title=Una alianza mundial: Kavak y la Selección Argentina |url=https://www.kavak.com/ar/blog/una-alianza-mundial-kavak-y-la-seleccion-argentina |website=Kavak Blog |date=25 February 2022 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref> as well as the partnership with [[Uber]] to provide self-financing services.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kavak y Uber forman alianza para ofrecer autos seminuevos a conductores |url=https://forbes.com.mx/negocios-kavak-uber-alianza-autos-seminuevos-conductores/ |website=Forbes México |date=23 November 2020 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref> In February 2024, Kavak took over the sponsorship of the [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]] (CCC).<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak concreta alianza con la Copa de Campeones Concacaf |url=https://expansion.mx/empresas/2024/02/22/kavak-concreta-alianza-con-la-copa-de-campeones-concacaf |work=[[Expansión (Mexico)|Expansión]] |date=2024-02-22 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref> In December 2025, Kavak was announced as an official commercial partner of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite news |title=NFL anuncia gran acuerdo comercial en México |url=https://www.foxsports.com.mx/2025/12/08/nfl-anuncia-gran-acuerdo-comercial-en-mexico/ |work=[[Fox Sports (Mexico)]] |date=2025-12-08 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref>

== Social impact ==
The company has put in place a program known as "Talentos únicos", an initiative to recruit and train older people in conjunction with the [[Instituto Nacional de las Personas Adultas Mayores|National Institute for Older Persons]] (INAPAM).<ref>{{Cite news|title=Kavak ofrece empleo a adultos mayores en la segunda fase de Talentos Únicos |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/tendencias/kavak-ofrece-empleo-a-adultos-mayores-en-la-segunda-fase-de-talentos-unicos/ |work=[[El Universal (Mexico City)|El Universal]] |date=2024-10-09 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref>

Kavak has established three committees focused on the rights of its employees: one for women, one for [[racial minorities]], and one for the [[LGBTQ community]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak busca ser agente de cambio en favor de la diversidad y la inclusión |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2022/06/29/kavak-busca-ser-agente-de-cambio-en-favor-de-la-diversidad-y-la-inclusion/ |work=Infobae |date=2022-06-29 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref>

== Recognition ==

*In 2018, Kavak was named Entrepreneur of the Year by [[Expansión (Mexico)|Expansión]] magazine.<ref name=quien/>
*In 2023, Kavak advanced the most out of all the listed companies in Expansión magazine's "The 500 Most Important Companies of Mexico" list, jumping 93 places to 322 from 415.<ref>{{cite web |title=Estas son las empresas que más avanzaron entre "Las 500" |url=https://expansion.mx/empresas/2023/07/20/empresas-que-mas-crecieron-entre-las-500 |website=Expansión |date=20 July 2023 |language=es |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref>
*Kavak has been recognized by the [[PROFECO|Federal Consumer Protection Agency]] (PROFECO) for its conciliation processes.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Profeco reconoce a Kavak por sus procesos de conciliación |url=https://www.telediario.mx/economia/profeco-reconoce-a-kavak-por-sus-procesos-de-conciliacion |work=Telediario |date=2023-07-18 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Kavak mantiene certificación de Profeco pese a aumento de quejas en su contra |url=https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/empresas/Kavak-mantiene-certificacion-de-Profeco-pese-a-aumento-de-quejas-en-su-contra-20220503-0072.html |work=[[El Economista (Mexico)|El Economista]] |date=2022-05-03 |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Profeco orienta para evitar estafas en la compra de autos seminuevos |url=https://www.gob.mx/profeco/prensa/profeco-orienta-para-evitar-estafas-en-la-compra-de-autos-seminuevos?idiom=es |website=Gobierno de México |access-date=2026-04-07 |language=es}}</ref>
