|work=[[Bloomberg News]]|access-date=2026-06-01}}</ref>

In April 2025, President Trump announced that he would end the tariff loophole for low-cost packages, or what is also known as the de minimis exemption. The exemption allowed packages valued under $800 to enter the US without being subject to taxes.  The president signed an executive order that ended the decades-old exemption for any package coming into the US from China or Hong Kong. This resulted in Shein and other companies like Alibaba and Temu announcing that they would have to raise prices for US customers starting April 25. Shein said it would seek to limit prices for customers. In addition to increased prices, the move will also make it longer for shipments of packages.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-23 |title=Trump is ending this tariff loophole for low-cost packages. Here's what that could mean for consumers |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/what-the-end-of-the-de-minimis-exemption-could-mean-for-your-online-orders |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815145554/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/what-the-end-of-the-de-minimis-exemption-could-mean-for-your-online-orders |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=PBS News |language=en-us}}</ref> In response, retailers like Alibaba, Shein, and Temu shifted more inventory to US warehouses, bulked shipments, and reduced advertising expenses while delivery times became longer and more complicated. Short-term negotiations did find a decrease in tariffs, but these were also temporary due to legal challenges. Many issues still remain unsettled, like pricing, sourcing, and fulfillment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=China low-value package exemption ends with questions over US tariff collections, logistics |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/china-low-value-package-tariff-exemption-ends-questions-remain-over-us-2025-05-02/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260210030831/https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/china-low-value-package-tariff-exemption-ends-questions-remain-over-us-2025-05-02/ |archive-date=February 10, 2026 |website=Reuters}}</ref>  The policy affected supply chains, pushing cross-border sellers to localize inventory, use US-based fulfillment centers, and rethink low-margin product lines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lahiri |first=Anusuya |date=2025-07-31 |title=Alibaba, Amazon, Shein Brace For Impact As Trump Nixes Duty-Free Threshold - Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN), Al |url=https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/25/07/46753634/alibaba-amazon-shein-brace-for-impact-as-trump-nixes-duty-free-threshold |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250823134758/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/25/07/46753634/alibaba-amazon-shein-brace-for-impact-as-trump-nixes-duty-free-threshold |archive-date=August 23, 2025 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Benzinga |language=English}}</ref>

In May 2026, Shein agreed to acquire US clothing brand [[Everlane]].<ref name=":16">{{Cite news |last=Press |first=Associated |date=2026-05-22 |title=Chinese fast-fashion company Shein to buy eco-friendly retailer Everlane |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/may/22/shein-everlane-sale |access-date=2026-05-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> The value of the deal was not disclosed by Shein or Everlane but reportedly valued the company at $100 million.<ref name=":16" />

In August 2026, Shein filed to raise up to HK$13.86 billion (US$1.77 billion) through an initial public offering on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company offered approximately 280 million Class B shares at HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 per share.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Sawdah Bhaimiya,Justina |date=2026-08-24 |title=Shein targets $27 billion Hong Kong IPO — a fraction of its 2022 valuation |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/shein-ipo-valuation-hong-kong.html |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

The offering went ahead at the end of August 2026 in a flotation which valued the company at $26.2 billion.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shein shares fall in long-awaited stock market debut |publisher= BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3v0qrz7z25o?app-referrer=deep-link|date=31 August 2026|access-date =7 September 2026}}</ref>

=== Lawsuits with Temu ===
In December 2022, Shein sued [[Temu]] alleging that Temu had enlisted online influencers "to make false and deceptive statements" about Shein to promote its own goods.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Toh |first=Michelle |date=2023-07-19 |title=Analysis: Shein and Temu's battle for US bargain shoppers is getting nasty |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/19/tech/temu-shein-lawsuits-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=2024-11-07 |publisher=CNN |language=en |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108215035/https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/19/tech/temu-shein-lawsuits-intl-hnk/index.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

In August 2023, Shein sought an injunction against Temu, filed in London's High Court, alleging the company had "identified thousands of instances" where Temu's sellers copied its listing photos.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-11 |title=Shein's 'War' Against Temu Reaches London High Court |url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/shein-war-against-temu-reaches-224439348.html |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Yahoo Life |language=en-US}}</ref> Shein requested all violating posts be taken down and at least £100,000 in damages.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Field |first=Matthew |date=2023-09-10 |title=Shein sues Chinese rival in High Court copycat row |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2023/09/10/shein-sues-chinese-rival-temu-high-court-copycat-row/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235 |archive-date=13 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230913104512/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2023/09/10/shein-sues-chinese-rival-temu-high-court-copycat-row/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2024, Temu hit back with a counterclaim in February, accusing Shein of breaking British competition law by tying suppliers of fast-fashion products to exclusive agreements, a claim it values at 4.2 million pounds ($5.5 million) and which Shein denies.<ref name="Jones">{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Callum |date=2023-12-14 |title=Online retailer Temu sues rival Shein, alleging 'mafia-style intimidation' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/dec/14/temu-sues-shein-lawsuit |access-date=2024-11-07 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=18 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240118212037/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/dec/14/temu-sues-shein-lawsuit |url-status=live}}</ref> Temu also alleged that Shein "bullied, intimidated, and even detained" suppliers in China as part of a campaign of "mafia-style intimidation".<ref name="Jones" /> Their cases at London's High Court are expected to come to trial towards the end of 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 5, 2024 |title=Shein, Temu gear up for 2026 UK trial over copyright and competition claims |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/shein-temu-gear-up-2026-uk-trial-over-copyright-competition-claims-2024-11-05/ |work=Reuters |access-date=2026-06-01}}</ref>

== Marketing ==
Shein is available through its website, and through dedicated mobile apps;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ducklin |first=Paul |date=2023-03-10 |title=SHEIN shopping app goes rogue, grabs price and URL data from your clipboard |url=https://news.sophos.com/en-us/2023/03/10/shein-shopping-app-goes-rogue-grabs-price-and-url-data-from-your-clipboard/ |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=Sophos News |language=en-US |archive-date=22 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022104953/https://news.sophos.com/en-us/2023/03/10/shein-shopping-app-goes-rogue-grabs-price-and-url-data-from-your-clipboard/ |url-status=live }}</ref> it is distributed on the [[Google Play|Google Play Store]], [[App Store (Apple)|App Store]], [[Galaxy Store]], and [[Huawei AppGallery]]. According to [[CNN]], TikTok plays a large role in driving customers to the company website due to a TikTok trend of bulk buying clothes from Shein and presenting Shein clothes to their audience like a standard [[haul video]].<ref name=":1" /> On May 17, 2021, the number of Shein's app downloads surpassed those of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|last1=Xiao|first1=Eva|last2=Moss|first2=Trefor|date=2021-08-02|title=How Shein Became the Chinese Apparel Maker American Teens Love|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/how-shein-became-the-chinese-apparel-maker-american-teens-love-11627896600|access-date=2021-11-06|issn=0099-9660|archive-date=27 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027053108/https://www.wsj.com/articles/how-shein-became-the-chinese-apparel-maker-american-teens-love-11627896600|url-status=live}}</ref> Shein was the second most popular shopping app globally in 2021, and the most-downloaded app in May 2022.<ref name=backlash/>

Shein says it uses the psychology of the new generation and implements marketing strategies accordingly to achieve growth.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|date=2021-06-16|title=How US-China trade war turbocharged shopping app Shein's growth|url=https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/fashion-beauty/article/3137319/how-trumps-trade-war-helped-china-shopping-app-shein|access-date=2021-11-06|website=South China Morning Post|archive-date=25 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221125222600/https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/fashion-beauty/article/3137319/how-trumps-trade-war-helped-china-shopping-app-shein|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2020, Shein was the most talked-about brand on TikTok and [[YouTube]], and the 4th most talked-about brand on [[Instagram]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Analysis Shows 'Most Talked About' Brands Across TikTok, YouTube and Instagram|date=19 April 2021|url=https://www.digitalinformationworld.com/2021/04/analysis-shows-most-talked-about-brands.html|access-date=2021-10-04|archive-date=5 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211105191842/https://www.digitalinformationworld.com/2021/04/analysis-shows-most-talked-about-brands.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Its low prices attract teenage internet shoppers with small budgets to post what they bought on social media.<ref name=":3" />

For user growth, the company offers relatively low prices to stimulate demand.<ref name=":3" /> With more spending, customers can be rewarded with more discounts, which are encouraged to be applied to their next shopping trip.<ref name=":3" /> Shein not only makes use of its algorithm-driven recommendation system but also attracts customers to visit the platform frequently to do tasks, like adding items to their cart, watching live streams, conducting reviews of already purchased items and joining its contest show, to win points which can be redeemed later.<ref name=":1" />

== Manufacturing ==
Originally, Shein did not design its clothes.<ref name=":0" /> The company mainly sourced its clothing from China's wholesale clothing market in [[Guangzhou]].<ref name=":0" /> However, Shein became a fully integrated retailer in 2014 when it secured its supply chain system. Now, the company utilizes a network of manufacturing partners and suppliers to make and deliver its products.<ref name=":0" />

Shein makes predictions on trends and produces items as quickly as three days after the identification of a trend.<ref name=":0" /> Shein also limits its orders to small batches of about 100 items to gauge customer interest. Order sizes are increased only if the small batches do well with consumers.<ref name=PRS /> In contrast, its competitors such as [[Zara (retailer)|Zara]] order larger quantities (about 500), increasing their chances of losing profit if orders are not purchased in full.<ref name=":0" /> ''Bloomberg''  reported that Shein's small-batch ordering underpinned its growth, and that suppliers businesses expanded as Shein's scale increased.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 6, 2022 |title=Fast-Fashion Upstarts Are Using Shein’s Own Strategies Against It |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-11-06/fashion-retailer-shein-s-competitors-are-copying-its-super-fast-business-model |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260810225202/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-11-06/fashion-retailer-shein-s-competitors-are-copying-its-super-fast-business-model |archive-date=2026-08-10 |access-date=2026-08-24 |work=Bloomberg |language=en}}</ref>

== Lobbying ==
In 2022, Shein hired [[Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld]] and [[Ben Quayle]] as lobbyists, according to U.S. federal lobbyist disclosures.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oprysko |first=Caitlin |date=2022-10-11 |title=Chinese fast fashion retailer lobbies up |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/politico-influence/2022/10/11/chinese-fast-fashion-retailer-lobbies-up-00061286 |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en |archive-date=16 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716212607/https://www.politico.com/newsletters/politico-influence/2022/10/11/chinese-fast-fashion-retailer-lobbies-up-00061286 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chua |first=Jasmin Malik |date=2022-10-23 |title=Shein Brings in Power-Broker Big Guns |url=https://sourcingjournal.com/topics/business-news/shein-lobbyists-dc-hobart-hallaway-quayle-ventures-akin-gump-strauss-hauer-feld-382876/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=Sourcing Journal |language=en-US |archive-date=16 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716213043/https://sourcingjournal.com/topics/business-news/shein-lobbyists-dc-hobart-hallaway-quayle-ventures-akin-gump-strauss-hauer-feld-382876/ |url-status=live }}</ref> According to ''[[Politico]]'', Shein's lobbying campaign is geared toward rehabilitating its image in Washington.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bade |first=Gavin |date=June 4, 2023 |title=Fast fashion giant with ties to China tries to shake forced labor claims |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2023/06/shein-china-forced-labor-claims-lobbying-fast-fashion-00100065 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en |archive-date=16 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716212608/https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2023/06/shein-china-forced-labor-claims-lobbying-fast-fashion-00100065 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Tax treatment ==
Shein can avoid paying export and import taxes, contributing to larger margins.<ref name=":02" /><ref name=":0" /> The U.S. legislative bill Section 321 in the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015 (also referred to as "''de minimis''") states that any import up to $800 per person is duty-free.<ref>{{Cite web|title=De Minimis Value Increases to $800|url=https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/national-media-release/de-minimis-value-increases-800|access-date=2021-11-06|website=U.S. Customs and Border Protection|archive-date=26 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226124832/https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/national-media-release/de-minimis-value-increases-800|url-status=live}}</ref> This bill has allowed Shein to deliver to the United States without paying taxes, allowing Shein to have a competitive advantage over domestic companies in the United States.<ref name=":02" /> In September 2024, the Biden administration announced that it would propose a new rule closing the $800 ''de minimis'' exception for Chinese e-commerce retailers such as Shein.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lawder |first=David |date=September 13, 2024 |title=China's online retailers Shein, Temu in focus as US aims to plug trade "loophole" |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/us-take-steps-curb-low-value-chinese-shipments-under-800-de-minimis-exemption-2024-09-13/ |access-date=September 13, 2024 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

In April 2023, Brazilian officials stated that Shein used a loophole in Brazilian law to practice tax evasion and "smuggling" to consumers in the country.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Por que varejistas criticam Shein, Shopee e AliExpress por 'contrabando digital' no Brasil |url=https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/2023/03/28/por-que-varejistas-criticam-shein-shopee-e-aliexpress-por-contrabando-digital-no-brasil.ghtml |access-date=2023-04-21 |website=G1 |language=pt-br |archive-date=25 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525015544/https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/2023/03/28/por-que-varejistas-criticam-shein-shopee-e-aliexpress-por-contrabando-digital-no-brasil.ghtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Tax avoidance and evasion accusations===
The [[United Kingdom]] requires foreign sellers shipping low-value consignments (under £135) to register for UK VAT, collect VAT from buyers on such shipments, and remit it to [[HM Revenue and Customs|His Majesty's Revenue and Customs]].<ref>{{cite web |author=UK Government |title=VAT and overseas goods sold directly to customers in the UK |url=https://www.gov.uk/guidance/vat-and-overseas-goods-sold-directly-to-customers-in-the-uk |access-date=2022-04-27 |publisher=Gov.UK |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606081630/https://www.gov.uk/guidance/vat-and-overseas-goods-sold-directly-to-customers-in-the-uk |url-status=live }}</ref> It has been suggested that Shein failed to do so for at least 9 months after the requirement took effect, and its website does not display its UK corporate registration number or itemize VAT, as UK rules require.<ref>{{cite news |last=Chambers |first=Sam |date=2022-04-23 |title=How Chinese clothing giant Shein conquered the UK — and undercut rivals on tax |work=[[The Sunday Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/money/article/how-chinese-clothing-giant-shein-conquered-the-uk-and-undercut-rivals-on-tax-rpn720s3s |url-access=subscription |access-date=2022-04-27 |archive-date=31 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531160333/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/how-chinese-clothing-giant-shein-conquered-the-uk-and-undercut-rivals-on-tax-rpn720s3s |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2025, ''The Guardian'' reported that the company had been accused of UK corporate tax avoidance by shifting profits to Singapore.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Butler |first=Sarah |date=2025-09-06 |title=Shein UK accused of moving 'vast bulk of income' to Singapore to cut British tax |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2025/sep/06/shein-uk-singapore-tax-fashion |access-date=2025-10-03 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==Environmental impact==
In 2023, Shein contributed 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide emitted into the air.<ref name="Grist-2024">{{Cite web |last=Grist |first=Sachi Kitajima Mulkey |date=2024-09-19 |title=Shein is officially the biggest polluter in fast fashion » Yale Climate Connections |url=https://yaleclimateconnections.org/2024/09/shein-is-officially-the-biggest-polluter-in-fast-fashion-ai-is-making-things-worse/ |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=Yale Climate Connections |language=en-US}}</ref> The manufacturers’ rapid use of virgin polyester and large consumption of oil churns out the same amount of CO<sub>2</sub> as approximately 180 coal-fired power plants.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last1=Rajvanshi |first1=Astha |last2=Caldwell |first2=Video by Jenna |last3=Johnson |first3=Andrew D. |date=2023-01-17 |title=Shein's Massive Popularity Comes at a Huge Cost to Us All |url=https://time.com/6247732/shein-climate-change-labor-fashion/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |magazine=Time |language=en |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108214930/https://time.com/6247732/shein-climate-change-labor-fashion/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 76% of Shein's products use polyester, a fabric that easily sheds microplastics, and only 6% of those clothing items are recycled.<ref name="Grist-2024" /> 

[[Deutsche Welle]] released a video in late 2021 detailing the ultra-fast-fashion system Shein is built on, criticizing the company's marketing to adolescents and young adults, as well as the caused [[Environmental impact of fashion|environmental impact]].<ref>{{Citation |title=If you think fast fashion is bad, check out SHEIN |date=10 December 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4km0Cslcpg |access-date=2022-05-04 |archive-date=16 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516082122/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4km0Cslcpg |url-status=live }}</ref> Other media outlets have pointed at the [[Problematic social media use|addictive]] nature of the app, noting how its low prices encourage users to make [[impulse purchase]]s.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mahmood |first=Zainab |date=2022-04-18 |title=Ultra-fast fashion is taking over – and using every trick in the book to get us addicted |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/apr/18/ultra-fast-fashion-retail-sites-shein |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=[[The Guardian]] |archive-date=20 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520153225/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/apr/18/ultra-fast-fashion-retail-sites-shein |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, ''Time'' magazine reported that the company was producing more than 6.3 million tons of carbon dioxide every year.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2023-07-16 |title=What to Know About the Shein Lawsuit |url=https://time.com/6295035/shein-lawsuit-copyright-infringement/ |access-date=2023-08-10 |magazine=Time |language=en |archive-date=10 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810231606/https://time.com/6295035/shein-lawsuit-copyright-infringement/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

In response to criticism, Shein launched a resale service on its US app that enables the buying and selling of [[Used good|secondhand]] Shein fashion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roshitsh |first=Kaley |date=2022-10-17 |title=Shein Launches 'Shein Exchange' Resale Program |url=https://wwd.com/sustainability/business/shein-resale-shein-exchange-fast-fashion-online-shopping-social-1235391629/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=WWD |language=en-US}}</ref> Shein prices are highly affordable hence customers may choose to buy a new item rather than purchase a resale piece.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Minter |first=Adam |date=3 November 2022 |title=Shein's Fast-Fashion Waste Problem Won't Be Fixed by Resale |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2022-11-03/shein-exchange-fast-fashion-resale-won-t-solve-its-waste-problem |access-date=6 December 2022 |archive-date=3 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221203052506/https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2022-11-03/shein-exchange-fast-fashion-resale-won-t-solve-its-waste-problem |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Legal and regulatory issues==
=== Unsafe chemical exposure ===
Shein was also cited in a [[Marketplace (Canadian TV program)|''Marketplace'']] investigation overseen by professor [[Miriam Diamond]] at the [[University of Toronto]] for selling toddlers' jackets that contained almost 20 times the amount of [[Lead poisoning|lead]] permitted under [[Health Canada]]'s safety regulations.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news | first1=Jenny | last1=Cowley | first2=Stephanie | last2=Matteis | first3=Charlsie | last3=Agro |title=Experts warn of high levels of chemicals in clothes by some fast-fashion retailers |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/marketplace-fast-fashion-chemicals-1.6193385 |access-date=5 November 2021 |archive-date=17 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230617051650/https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/marketplace-fast-fashion-chemicals-1.6193385 |url-status=live }}</ref> The company also sold a red purse that contained five times the permitted amount of lead.<ref name=":6" /> Shein notified Marketplace that they would stop selling the two items and would stop getting supplies from the corresponding suppliers until the problem was addressed.<ref name=":6" /> In May 2024, South Korean authorities found that some of Shein products contained unsafe level of [[phthalates]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-05-28 |title=South Korea finds high levels of toxic chemicals in Shein products |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/south-korea-finds-high-levels-of-toxic-chemicals-in-shein-products |access-date=2024-06-28 |work=[[The Straits Times]] |language=en |issn=0585-3923 |archive-date=14 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614104244/https://www.straitstimes.com/business/south-korea-finds-high-levels-of-toxic-chemicals-in-shein-products |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Labor law violations ===
Shein produces its clothing in [[Guangzhou]]. Often going overtime and lasting more than 10 hours, an employee's working hours are unpredictable, and some workers are paid as little as US$5/hour. Employees rent small rooms above the cloth and sewing machine-filled garment factories. They sleep on bunk beds and pay US$130 per month.<ref name="Bradsher-2025">{{Cite news |last=Bradsher |first=Keith |date=2025-02-14 |title=Where China's Exports Begin: Inside the Vast Markets of Guangzhou |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/14/business/economy/china-exports-trump-tariffs.html?searchResultPosition=3 |access-date=2025-03-04 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Because Shein produces 10,000 garments a day to maintain pace with fast-changing clothing trends,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bennett |first=Catherine | date=2024-03-31 |title=Jeremy Hunt and Gen Z are clearly of a mind on Shein. They'd rather skirt the issues | url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/mar/31/jeremy-hunt-and-gen-z-are-clearly-of-a-mind-on-shein-they-would-rather-skirt-the-issues |access-date=2025-03-04 |work=The Observer |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref> they do not stock up on inventory. Because about 60 percent of 18-year-olds are going to college,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-03-01 |title=China has over 47 mln higher-education students in 2023 |url=http://www.china.org.cn/china/2024-03/01/content_117031119.htm |work=China.org.cn |agency=Xinhua |access-date=2025-04-08}}</ref> the amount of Chinese young people willing to work in clothing workshops has decreased, and there are fewer employees working in the Guangzhou workshops. There have been complaints from employees that their work is too taxing.<ref name="Bradsher-2025" /> During an investigation by ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'', Shein workers revealed that they often have to work 75-hour weeks in factories that lack sufficient windows or exits.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Vara |first=Vauhini |title=Fast, Cheap, and Out of Control: Inside Shein's Sudden Rise |url=https://www.wired.com/story/fast-cheap-out-of-control-inside-rise-of-shein/ |access-date=2025-05-02 |magazine=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

In 2021, a [[Public Eye (organization)|Public Eye]] investigation reported that employees of six Shein suppliers in [[Guangzhou]] were working 75 hours per week in breach of [[labour law#China|Chinese labor laws]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-11-12 |title=Shein suppliers' workers doing 75-hour week, finds probe |work=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-59245708 |access-date=2021-11-17 |archive-date=26 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211126095529/https://www.bbc.com/news/business-59245708 |url-status=live }}</ref> Public Eye also discovered workshops with blocked corridors and stairways.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Testa |first=Jessica |date=September 1, 2022 |title=The People's Republic of Shein |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/01/style/shein-clothing.html |access-date=November 12, 2022 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612135818/http://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/01/style/shein-clothing.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Channel 4's documentary, ''Inside The Shein Machine'', sent undercover cameras to film factory workers who were forced to pull 17-hour shifts to make hundreds of garments a day.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last1=Rajvanshi |first1=Astha |last2=Caldwell |first2=Video by Jenna |last3=Johnson |first3=Andrew D. |date=2023-01-17 |title=Shein's Massive Popularity Comes at a Huge Cost to Us All |url=https://time.com/6247732/shein-climate-change-labor-fashion/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |magazine=Time |language=en}}</ref> In one factory, they made a daily base salary of $20, which would then be docked by $14 if any garments had mistakes.<ref>{{Cite news |date=17 October 2022 |title=Inside the Shein Machine: Untold |url=https://www.channel4.com/programmes/inside-the-shein-machine-untold |access-date=7 November 2024 |work=Channel 4 |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108220921/https://www.channel4.com/programmes/inside-the-shein-machine-untold |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2024, Shein said it found two cases of child labour in its supply chain the prior year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-23 |title=Fast fashion giant Shein finds child labour cases in supply chain |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4glzzdd88lo |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108215710/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4glzzdd88lo |url-status=live }}</ref> Shein's general counsel for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Yinan Zhu, disclosed the cases in a letter to MPs in the United Kingdom in 2025. One of the incidents involved a child aged 11 years and eight months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Amber |date=2025-02-27 |title=Child labour cases once again found in Shein's supply chain |url=https://www.cityam.com/child-labour-cases-once-again-found-in-sheins-supply-chain/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=City AM |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Shein said it has built an in-house team to monitor supply-chain partners and engages with independent agencies such as [[Intertek]] to conduct regular and unannounced audits.<ref name="WSJZhai">{{Cite news |last=Zhai |first=Keith |date=12 Dec 2022 |title=Fast-Fashion Giant Shein Explores Becoming Online Marketplace |work=The Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/fast-fashion-giant-shein-explores-becoming-online-marketplace-11670827480 |access-date=13 December 2022 |archive-date=7 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230507043147/https://www.wsj.com/articles/fast-fashion-giant-shein-explores-becoming-online-marketplace-11670827480 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2025, Texas Attorney General [[Ken Paxton]] announced an investigation of Shein, citing unethical labor practices and the sale of unsafe consumer products.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stempel |first=Jonathan |date=1 December 2025 |title=Shein probed by Texas attorney general over labor practices, product safety |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/shein-probed-by-texas-attorney-general-over-labor-practices-product-safety-2025-12-01/ |access-date=3 December 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

=== ISO certification claim ===
In August 2021, Shein claimed on its website that its factories were certified by the [[International Organization for Standardization]] (ISO) and complied with standards set by "organizations like [[SA8000]]".<ref name=":10">{{Cite news |last=Waldersee |first=Victoria |date=2021-08-06 |title=Chinese retailer Shein lacks disclosures, made false statements about factories |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/exclusive-chinese-retailer-shein-lacks-disclosures-made-false-statements-about-2021-08-06/ |access-date=2021-11-06 |archive-date=24 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224102138/https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/exclusive-chinese-retailer-shein-lacks-disclosures-made-false-statements-about-2021-08-06/ |url-status=live }}</ref> While the ISO sets standards, it does not directly certify any company. SA8000 is not an organisation but a standard administered by Social Accountability International, which said Shein had received no such certification.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shein: the false statements about the factories of the ultra-fast-fashion brand |url=https://dress-ecode.com/en/shein-the-false-statements-about-the-factories-of-the-ultra-fast-fashion-brand/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Dress Ecode |language=en-US}}</ref> The claim was removed after [[Reuters]] inquired the company about it.<ref name=":10" />

=== Anti-modern slavery reporting ===
The United Kingdom's [[Modern Slavery Act 2015|2015 Modern Slavery Act]] requires companies over a certain size to make statements about how they are combatting modern slavery. A similar law has been passed in Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Modern slavery laws in the UK and Australia are failing and need urgent reform |url=https://www.walkfree.org/news/2025/modern-slavery-laws-in-the-uk-and-australia-are-failing-and-need-urgent-reform/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250602100249/https://www.walkfree.org/news/2025/modern-slavery-laws-in-the-uk-and-australia-are-failing-and-need-urgent-reform/ |archive-date=2025-06-02 |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Walk Free |language=en-AU}}</ref> Shein declined to disclose its revenue to Reuters in 2021 but said it was in the process of preparing such statements.<ref name=thefashionlaw>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-06 |title=Shein is Falling Short of Modern Slavery Reporting Rules, According to New Report |url=https://www.thefashionlaw.com/shein-is-falling-short-of-modern-slavery-reporting-rules-according-to-new-report/ |access-date=2021-11-06 |website=The Fashion Law |archive-date=4 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104230839/https://www.thefashionlaw.com/shein-is-falling-short-of-modern-slavery-reporting-rules-according-to-new-report/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In June 2023, Shein was included in a report by the [[United States House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party]] titled "Fast Fashion and the Uyghur Genocide".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gallagher |first1=Mike |author-link=Mike Gallagher (American politician) |last2=Krishnamorthi |first2=Raja |author-link2=Raja Krishnamoorthi |date=June 22, 2023 |title=Fast Fashion and the Uyghur Genocide: Interim Findings |url=https://selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/fast-fashion-and-the-uyghur-genocide-interim-findings.pdf |access-date=Feb 20, 2024}}</ref>

=== European Commission investigation ===
In February 2025, the [[European Commission]] requested internal documents from Shein regarding risks linked to the presence of illegal goods on the marketplace as part of an existing investigation under the [[Digital Services Act]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=De Clercq |first1=Geert |last2=Reid |first2=Helen |date=6 February 2025 |title=European Commission asks Shein for information on illegal goods |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/european-commission-asks-chinas-shein-information-illegal-content-goods-2025-02-06/ |access-date=8 February 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> In May 2025, the European Commission alleged that Shein breached EU law.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Labiak |first=Mitchell |date=2025-05-26 |title=Fake discounts on Shein 'breach law', EU says |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c62vq1mnndno |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Investigations by France ===
In November 2023, the French [[Ministry of Economics and Finance (France)|Ministry of Economics and Finance]] initiated an investigation into Shein to assess its compliance with international guidelines and French laws after the [[Socialist Party (France)|Socialist Party]] accused the company of not respecting human rights, the environment, and consumer interest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=WW |first=FashionNetwork com |date=2023-11-15 |title=OECD investigates Shein in France |url=https://ww.fashionnetwork.com/news/Oecd-investigates-shein-in-france,1576794.html |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=FashionNetwork.com |language=en-WW}}</ref> Shein said it would cooperate with the investigation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garel |first=Julia |date=2023-11-16 |title=French watchdog opens investigation into Shein |url=https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/french-watchdog-opens-investigation-into-shein/2023111672594 |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=[[FashionUnited]] |language=en |archive-date=16 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116120801/https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/french-watchdog-opens-investigation-into-shein/2023111672594 |url-status=live }}</ref> In November 2025, the French government moved to suspend the online platform of Shein until Shein could prove to authorities that it complies with local laws and regulations.<ref name=":15" />

==== Childlike sex dolls ====
In November 2025, France's consumer watchdog reported that the company was selling sex dolls with a childlike appearance. They claimed there was "little doubt as to the child pornography nature of the content".<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |date=2025-11-04 |title=Shein bans all sex dolls after outrage over childlike products |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cddrg70pj1mo |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Following media reports and protests in Paris, Shein banned the sale of [[sex doll]]s after French authorities threatened to shut down the site over its sale of sex dolls with child-like features.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 November 2025 |title=Shein bans sex dolls from marketplace after France threatens to shut it down |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/france-could-ban-sheins-access-french-market-if-it-resumed-sale-child-like-sex-2025-11-03/ |access-date=3 November 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-03 |title=Shein bans sex dolls after France outrage over 'childlike' ones |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/shein-bans-sex-dolls-france-194454577.html |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=AFP via Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-02 |title=Shein accused of selling childlike sex dolls in France |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4gjjyvg1nqo |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> France announced it began proceedings to suspend the company's online website. This came an hour after Shein opened its first physical shop in the world on the sixth floor of Paris department store BHV.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-05 |title=France moves to suspend Shein website as it opens first store in Paris |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2lppx2jm7o |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> In February 2026, the European Commission opened a formal investigation into Shein over the issue.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chee |first=Foo Yun |date=February 17, 2026 |title=EU probes Shein over sale of illegal products, addictive design |url=https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/eu-probes-shein-over-sale-illegal-products-addictive-design-2026-02-17/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

=== Xinjiang cotton ===
{{Further|Xinjiang cotton industry}}

In November 2022, [[Bloomberg News]] reported that Shein's apparel was made with [[Xinjiang cotton industry|cotton sourced from Xinjiang]] amid the [[persecution of Uyghurs in China]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Prasso |first=Sheridan |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Shein's Cotton Tied to Chinese Region Accused of Forced Labor |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-11-21/shein-s-cotton-clothes-tied-to-xinjiang-china-region-accused-of-forced-labor |access-date=November 21, 2022 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611003014/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-11-21/shein-s-cotton-clothes-tied-to-xinjiang-china-region-accused-of-forced-labor |url-status=live }}</ref> Following the report, a coalition of [[List of current United States senators|U.S. senators]] wrote to Shein to demand information about the potential use of forced labor in Xinjiang for cotton products.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Prasso |first1=Sheridan |last2=Poh |first2=Olivia |date=2023-02-09 |title=Does Shein Use Banned Xinjiang Cotton? US Senators Want to Know |work=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-02-09/us-senators-ask-shein-about-forced-labor-concerns-for-its-cotton |access-date=2023-03-04}}</ref>

Legal experts have noted that Shein may be able to avoid the repercussions of the [[Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act]] because most Shein parcels shipped to the U.S. are worth less than $800 (''[[de minimis]]'' shipments), which means that inspection by [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection|customs]] may be waived.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lau |first1=Yvonne |last2=Barrett |first2=Eamon |date=June 20, 2022 |title=A Tax Loophole Shein Exploited to Become the U.S.'s Largest Fast Fashion Retailer Might Help It Skirt a New Ban on Forced Labor Too |url=https://fortune.com/2022/06/20/shein-tax-exempt-loophole-de-minimis-uyghur-forced-labor-prevention-act-fast-fashion/ |access-date=March 4, 2023 |website=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |archive-date=8 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608033716/https://fortune.com/2022/06/20/shein-tax-exempt-loophole-de-minimis-uyghur-forced-labor-prevention-act-fast-fashion/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2023, a group of U.S. lawmakers called on the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] to halt Shein's [[initial public offering]] until the company could verify that it does not use forced labor for its products.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McLymore |first=Arriana |date=2023-05-01 |title=US lawmakers push SEC to order audit of Shein IPO over Uyghur forced labor fears |language=en |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/sustainable-business/us-lawmakers-push-sec-order-audit-shein-ipo-over-uyghur-forced-labor-fears-2023-05-01/ |access-date=2023-05-02 |archive-date=24 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230524144033/https://www.reuters.com/business/sustainable-business/us-lawmakers-push-sec-order-audit-shein-ipo-over-uyghur-forced-labor-fears-2023-05-01/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In August 2023, 16 U.S. states requested the Securities and Exchange Commission to audit Shein's supply chain for forced labor before its initial public offering.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McLymore |first=Arriana |date=August 29, 2023 |title=US states ask SEC to check if Shein complies with forced labor rules |url=https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/us-states-ask-sec-check-if-shein-complies-with-forced-labor-rules-2023-08-28/ |access-date=December 20, 2023 |website=Reuters |archive-date=18 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231118155715/https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/us-states-ask-sec-check-if-shein-complies-with-forced-labor-rules-2023-08-28/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 2025, Shein's general counsel in London, Yinan Zhu, refused to answer repeated questions in a parliamentary hearing about whether Shein sources cotton from Xinjiang.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hui |first=Sylvia |date=2025-01-07 |title=UK lawmakers slam Shein for refusing to answer questions on its cotton supply |url=https://apnews.com/article/uk-parliament-shein-temu-a24fa3a6511cde7fe6b4763d693b986b |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en |archive-date=8 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108164315/https://apnews.com/article/uk-parliament-shein-temu-a24fa3a6511cde7fe6b4763d693b986b |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Race |first=Michael |date=January 7, 2025 |title=Shein lawyer refuses to say if Chinese cotton used in clothing |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyg7n1d85go |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB |archive-date=8 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108100700/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyg7n1d85go |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Intellectual property infringement ===
{{Further|Intellectual property in China}}

Shein has been sued by independent creators and by companies such as [[Deckers Brands|Deckers Outdoor Corporation]] and [[Levi Strauss & Co.]] for copyright and trademark infringement. Most of these cases were settled out of court.<ref name=thefashionlaw /><ref name=":2" />

In a 2021 lawsuit, AirWair International Limited accused Shein and its sister company, Romwe, of selling copies of their designs (and calling them "Martins") at a cheaper price while using photos of authentic Dr. Marten shoes to "entice customers," to which Shein responded with a blanket denial of AirWair International's claims.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Lee |first=Dave |date=2021-06-14 |title=Chinese ecommerce site Shein hit with trademark disputes |work=[[Financial Times]] |url=https://www.ft.com/content/b87df56a-cb71-4b6a-8c36-6e2db9a52c7c |url-access=subscription |access-date=2021-10-04 |archive-date=24 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624060519/https://www.ft.com/content/b87df56a-cb71-4b6a-8c36-6e2db9a52c7c |url-status=live }}</ref>

In March 2021, [[Ralph Lauren Corporation|Ralph Lauren]] filed a trademark infringement and [[Anti-competitive practices|unfair competition]] lawsuit against Shein's parent company.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|date=2021-06-15|title=From Dr Martens to Ralph Lauren, Lawsuits Are Starting to Build for $15 Billion Ultra-Fast Fashion Brand Shein|url=https://www.thefashionlaw.com/from-dr-martens-to-ralph-lauren-lawsuits-are-starting-to-build-up-against-15-billion-ultra-fast-fashion-brand-shein/|access-date=2021-09-27|website=The Fashion Law|archive-date=11 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611162148/https://www.thefashionlaw.com/from-dr-martens-to-ralph-lauren-lawsuits-are-starting-to-build-up-against-15-billion-ultra-fast-fashion-brand-shein/|url-status=live}}</ref> In the complaint, Ralph Lauren said that Zoetop Business Co. selling clothing with a "confusingly similar" mark was an exploitation of their "goodwill and reputation of genuine Ralph Lauren products."<ref name=":12" />

In 2022, Mexico's [[Secretariat of Culture]] questioned Shein's use of Mayan cultural elements in the design of one of its garments. The elements represented the "collective creativity" passed down through generations of [[Maya peoples|Mayan people]]. Shein subsequently removed the item from its website.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Diaz |first=Lizbeth |date=2022-07-21 |title=Mexico concerned by Chinese retailer Shein's use of a Mayan design |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/mexico-concerned-by-chinese-retailer-sheins-use-mayan-design-2022-07-21/ |access-date=2022-07-24 |archive-date=10 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410053434/https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/mexico-concerned-by-chinese-retailer-sheins-use-mayan-design-2022-07-21/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Design theft accusations ====
Shein has been accused by dozens of artists, small fashion retailers, and brands such as Reclamare PH and Sincerely RIA, of copying their designs, including enamel pins.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Strumpf |first=Dan |date=2022-07-03 |title=China's Fast-Fashion Giant Shein Faces Dozens of Lawsuits Alleging Design Theft |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/chinas-fast-fashion-giant-shein-faces-dozens-of-lawsuits-alleging-design-theft-11656840601 |access-date=2022-07-04 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606201935/https://www.wsj.com/articles/chinas-fast-fashion-giant-shein-faces-dozens-of-lawsuits-alleging-design-theft-11656840601 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-03-06 |title='They took my world': fashion giant Shein accused of art theft |url=https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2022/mar/06/they-took-my-world-fashion-giant-shein-accused-of-art-theft |access-date=2022-03-06 |website=[[The Guardian]] |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606203040/https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2022/mar/06/they-took-my-world-fashion-giant-shein-accused-of-art-theft |url-status=live }}</ref> There is "little protection for creators", however, because items with basic, useful functions are not broadly covered by copyright laws, and any unique or creative element must be separated out when making claims. According to a lawyer interviewed by [[NPR]], fast-fashion brands can walk a fine line by copying "just enough" without affecting anything that is "legally protected".<ref name=NPR>{{Cite news |last=Pruitt-Young |first=Sharon |date=2021-07-20 |title=Why Indie Brands Are At War With Shein And Other Fast-Fashion Companies |work=[[NPR]] |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/07/20/1018381462/why-indie-brands-are-at-war-with-shein-and-other-fast-fashion-companies |access-date=2021-09-27 |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603170746/https://www.npr.org/2021/07/20/1018381462/why-indie-brands-are-at-war-with-shein-and-other-fast-fashion-companies |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2018, Ilse Valfre, who owns the LA-based brand Valfré, was notified by her customers that Shein was selling "identical copies" of her products.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Chronicling SHEIN's Problematic History|url=https://www.34st.com/article/2020/07/shein-swastika-necklace-controversy-boycott-shein-fast-fashion-upenn-ivy-league|access-date=2021-10-04|website=www.34st.com|date=9 July 2020|archive-date=6 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206071934/https://www.34st.com/article/2020/07/shein-swastika-necklace-controversy-boycott-shein-fast-fashion-upenn-ivy-league|url-status=live}}</ref> Quinn Jones, who is the co-founder of the US company Kikay, said that he found earring designs on Shein that were very similar to Kikay's earrings. In response to the controversy, Shein removed the products and pledged to drop the supplier that produced the copied item.<ref name=":2" />

To bring awareness to Shein's actions and to help support independent brands and artists, the [[hashtag]] "boycottShein" became popular on TikTok and [[Twitter]] in 2020.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=NPR /> In 2021, Mariama Diallo, founder of and designer for Sincerely Ria, accused Shein of stealing her designs in a tweet that included comparative images to demonstrate her point.<ref name="Michie 2021">{{cite web |last=Michie |first=Natalie |title=Shein Stolen Designs: Fast Fashion Retailer Accused of Copying...Again |website=FASHION Magazine |date=2021-06-16 |url=https://fashionmagazine.com/style/shein-stolen-designs/ |access-date=2021-12-06 |archive-date=1 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601185506/https://fashionmagazine.com/style/shein-stolen-designs/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In July 2023, a civil lawsuit was filed against Shein in the US alleging that its aggressive copyright infringement amounts to racketeering under the [[Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act]] (RICO). The lawsuit, filed by three fashion designers, claims that Shein produced, distributed, and sold exact copies of their creative work without permission.<ref>{{Cite Pacer |title= Shein.pdf |access-date=03-19-2024 |case-district=C.D. Cal.|case-division=2 |case-sequence=05551 |case-state=CA |case-type=cv |case-year=2023 |date=July 11, 2023 |defendant=Shein Distribution Corporation et al |doc-number=23 |plaintiff=Krista Perry et al |url=https://interactive.wusa9.com/pdfs/Shein.pdf |acces-date=2024-03-19 |language=en-US}}</ref> The lawsuit also alleged that Shein used artificial intelligence in the process, but what role it actually played is unclear.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 14, 2023 |title=China's Shein hit with lawsuit citing RICO violations, a law originally used against organized crime |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/lawsuit-fast-fashion-retailer-shein-claims-rico-violations-101286000 |access-date=2023-07-15 |website=ABC News |language=en |archive-date=15 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715030405/https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/lawsuit-fast-fashion-retailer-shein-claims-rico-violations-101286000 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weber |first=Harri |date=2023-07-14 |title=Designers sue Shein over AI ripoffs of their work |url=https://techcrunch.com/2023/07/14/designers-sue-shein-over-ai-ripoffs-of-their-work/ |access-date=2023-07-21 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US |archive-date=21 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721202150/https://techcrunch.com/2023/07/14/designers-sue-shein-over-ai-ripoffs-of-their-work/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

An industry analyst expresses that as long as the company still has room to grow, it will be motivated to keep expanding its product offering as quickly as it can and accept that some of the items would not conform to intellectual property norms.<ref name=":2" />

In January 2024, Japanese fashion giant [[Uniqlo]] said that it was suing Shein over copycats of a crossbody pouch. The lawsuit filed in Japan against Shein Japan and two subsidiaries demands the "immediate cessation of sales of the imitation products, and compensation for damages incurred", Uniqlo said in a statement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Uniqlo sues Shein in Japan over sale of round shoulder bag |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/uniqlo-sues-shein-japan-over-sale-round-shoulder-bag-4050866 |access-date=2024-01-17 |website=CNA |language=en |archive-date=17 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117012803/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/uniqlo-sues-shein-japan-over-sale-round-shoulder-bag-4050866 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Data security concerns ===
Shein experienced a data breach in 2018 that compromised the email addresses and encrypted passwords of 6.42 million users.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Over 6 Million Users Hit by Breach at Fashion Retailer SHEIN|url=https://www.securityweek.com/over-6-million-users-hit-breach-fashion-retailer-shein|access-date=2021-11-06|website=www.securityweek.com|date=25 September 2018|archive-date=28 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128170649/https://www.securityweek.com/over-6-million-users-hit-breach-fashion-retailer-shein/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to the [[Attorney General of New York|New York Attorney General]]'s office, the company understated the scale of the breach. The number of affected accounts was actually 39&nbsp;million; credit card information was also compromised, and many users were not notified or required to reset their password afterwards. In 2022, Shein's parent company, Zoetop, was fined $1.9&nbsp;million by [[New York (state)|New York]] state authorities for its inadequate response to the data breach.<ref>{{cite news |date=14 October 2022 |title=Shein owner Zoetop fined $1.9m over data breach response |publisher=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-63255661 |access-date=2022-10-17 |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606202754/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-63255661 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2023, US officials identified data-security risks associated with Shein and [[Temu]] as part of a broader review of Chinese-owned applications.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-04-15 |title=US accuses Shein, Temu of data risks in latest action targeting Chinese-backed apps |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-war/article/3217179/us-accuses-shein-temu-data-risks-latest-action-targeting-chinese-backed-apps |access-date=2023-04-18 |website=[[South China Morning Post]] |language=en |archive-date=14 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614065345/https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-war/article/3217179/us-accuses-shein-temu-data-risks-latest-action-targeting-chinese-backed-apps |url-status=live }}</ref> In December 2023, the [[United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce]] requested more information from Shein on its data privacy practices and its relationship with the [[Chinese Communist Party]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fonrouge |first=Gabrielle |date=2023-12-20 |title=Chair of powerful House committee pushes Shein about data protections, China relationship |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/20/shein-grilled-on-china-relationship-data-privacy-ahead-of-ipo.html |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=[[CNBC]] |language=en |archive-date=21 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231221050526/https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/20/shein-grilled-on-china-relationship-data-privacy-ahead-of-ipo.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2024, ''The Wall Street Journal'' reported that the [[Cyberspace Administration of China]] was scrutinizing Shein's data security practices.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 January 2024 |title=Fashion Giant Faces New IPO Hitch: China's Cybersecurity Police |url=https://www.wsj.com/world/china/fashion-giant-faces-new-ipo-hitch-chinas-cybersecurity-police-70c57561 |access-date=17 January 2024 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |archive-date=17 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117041550/https://www.wsj.com/world/china/fashion-giant-faces-new-ipo-hitch-chinas-cybersecurity-police-70c57561 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 2026, Texas Governor [[Greg Abbott]] prohibited state employees from using Shein on all government devices and networks, citing data security and privacy concerns.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rozen|first=Courtney|last2=Alper|first2=Alexandra|last3=Sherpardson|first3=David|date=January 26, 2026|title=Texas governor bars state employees from using Shein, Alibaba products|url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/texas-governor-bars-state-employees-using-alibaba-temu-products-2026-01-26/|access-date=January 26, 2026|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Carnahan |first=Ashley |date=2026-01-26 |title=Texas Gov Abbott adds popular Chinese electronics, online shopping companies to 'prohibited' tech list |url=https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/texas-gov-abbott-adds-popular-chinese-electronics-online-shopping-companies-prohibited-tech-list |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260224113141/https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/texas-gov-abbott-adds-popular-chinese-electronics-online-shopping-companies-prohibited-tech-list |archive-date=February 24, 2026 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=FOXBusiness |language=en-US}}</ref> In early May 2026, Ireland's Data Protection Commission announced a full-scale investigation into Shein and the amount and types of data about European customers that were being transferred back to China. [[General Data Protection Regulation|GDPR]] regulations in the EU requires that data sent outside the EU, is given the same protections as if it was being sent within the EU.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tobin |first=Sam |date=May 5, 2026 |title=Irish regulator investigates Shein over data transfers to China |url=https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/irish-data-protection-agency-launches-inquiry-into-shein-ireland-2026-05-05/ |access-date=May 16, 2026 |website=Reuters}}</ref>

=== App prohibition in India ===
In June 2020, the Shein app was banned in India due to privacy concerns.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Toh |first=Michelle |date=July 15, 2021 |title=Amazon is helping a Chinese upstart make a comeback in India after its app was banned |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/07/14/tech/shein-india-amazon-chinese-apps-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=2021-08-30 |website=[[CNN]] |archive-date=2 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230402133627/https://www.cnn.com/2021/07/14/tech/shein-india-amazon-chinese-apps-intl-hnk/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mukherjee |first=Vasudha |date=May 19, 2023 |title=Shein is coming back to India. Here's why it was banned in the past |url=https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/shein-is-coming-back-to-india-here-s-why-it-was-banned-in-the-past-123051900498_1.html |access-date=May 20, 2024 |work=[[Business Standard]] |archive-date=20 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520151241/https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/shein-is-coming-back-to-india-here-s-why-it-was-banned-in-the-past-123051900498_1.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Following the [[2020–2021 China–India skirmishes]], the [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] of India classified the Shein app along with 59 other Chinese apps under Section 69A in [[Information Technology Act, 2000|The Information Technology Act, 2000]], saying "[u]pon receiving recent credible inputs that such apps pose threat to sovereignty and integrity of India, the Government of India has decided to disallow the usage [...] both [on] mobile and non-mobile Internet-enabled devices." Section 69A grants the central government the "power to issue directions for blocking public access of any information through any computer resource".<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |agency=PTI |date=2021-10-05 |title=Chinese 'Shein' app blocked but sale of products on other platforms not covered: MeitY to Delhi HC |work=[[The Hindu]] |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/chinese-shein-app-blocked-but-sale-of-products-on-other-platforms-not-covered-meity-to-delhi-hc/article36840260.ece |access-date=2021-11-06 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603043021/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/chinese-shein-app-blocked-but-sale-of-products-on-other-platforms-not-covered-meity-to-delhi-hc/article36840260.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Criticism for offensive images ===
In July 2020, a necklace with a [[swastika]] was removed from the site in response to widespread public criticism; the brand explained that it was a Hindu religious symbol, not a Nazi swastika.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Popular online retailer Shein apologizes for selling swastika necklace after backlash |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/shein-nazi-symbol-swastika-necklace/ |access-date=2021-11-06 |website=[[CBS News]] |archive-date=9 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809110705/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/shein-nazi-symbol-swastika-necklace/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2021, Shein received criticism for offering a phone case with an image of a handcuffed Black man outlined in chalk. Shein issued an apology for the unintentionally offensive image and for using it without the permission of its original designer, who had created the image after the [[killing of Michael Brown]]. He later asked Shein to donate the proceeds from the sales to [[Black Lives Matter]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |title=Online Store Shein Apologized For Selling A Phone Case Depicting A Handcuffed Black Person Outlined In Chalk |url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/ryancbrooks/shein-phone-case-ferguson-apology |access-date=2021-11-06 |website=[[BuzzFeed News]] |archive-date=1 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230501204550/https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/ryancbrooks/shein-phone-case-ferguson-apology |url-status=live }}</ref>
