'''Shopee Pte. Ltd.''', trading as '''Shopee''', is a Singaporean [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[technology company]] that specialises in e-commerce and operates mainly in Southeast Asia.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lee |first=Yoolim |date=8 May 2017 |title=Garena Rebrands as Sea After Raising $550 Million in New Funding |work=Bloomberg |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-05-08/garena-rebrands-as-sea-after-raising-550-million-in-new-funding |access-date=21 March 2018}}</ref>

As of 2023, Shopee is recognized as the largest e-commerce platform in [[Southeast Asia]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Topic: E-commerce platforms in Vietnam |url=https://www.statista.com/topics/12689/e-commerce-platforms-in-vietnam/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241217060722/https://www.statista.com/topics/12689/e-commerce-platforms-in-vietnam/ |archive-date=2024-12-17 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Statista |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-08-15 |title=Shopee Leading The Way In E-Commerce Marketing |url=https://worldbrandaffairs.com/shopee-leading-the-way-in-e-commerce-marketing/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=World Brand Affairs |language=en-GB}}</ref> with a total gross merchandise volume (GMV) of $47.9 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-10-04 |title=Shopee braces for e-commerce battle in Southeast Asia as competitors close in |url=https://kr-asia.com/shopee-braces-for-e-commerce-battle-in-southeast-asia-as-competitors-close-in |access-date=16 November 2024 |website=KrASIA |language=en}}</ref> This figure represents nearly half of the total GMV of  Southeast Asian market. The platform also facilitates online buying and selling for consumers and sellers in [[East Asia]] and [[Latin America]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2022-01-12|title=As Shopee expands aggressively around the world, will it become the 'Amazon of emerging economies'?|url=https://kr-asia.com/as-shopee-expands-aggressively-around-the-world-will-it-become-the-amazon-of-emerging-economies|access-date=2022-01-13|website=KrASIA|language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
Shopee was established in [[Singapore]] in February 2015 as a mobile-focused marketplace that enables users to browse, shop, and sell products.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yap |first=Jacky |date=2015-08-03 |title=Garena And Its Quest To Take Down Carousell With Newly Launched Shopee App |url=https://vulcanpost.com/328891/garena-joins-long-list-companies-trying-take-carousell-newly-launched-shopee-app/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=Vulcan Post |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=VIR |first=Vietnam Investment Review- |date=2017-10-24 |title=Shopee parent company listed on New York Stock Exchange |url=https://vir.com.vn/shopee-parent-company-listed-on-new-york-stock-exchange-53210.html |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Vietnam Investment Review - VIR |language=en}}</ref> The platform integrates logistical and payment support to facilitate transactions and is designed to operate with minimal physical assets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ting |first=Lisabel |date=2015-09-09 |title=Safe, easy shopping with Shopee {{!}} The Straits Times |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/tech/games-apps/safe-easy-shopping-with-shopee |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=The Straits Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Terence |date=6 Nov 2017 |title=How Shopee plans to reign supreme in Southeast Asia’s fashion ecommerce scene |url=https://www.techinasia.com/shopees-plan-win-fashion-ecommerce-southeast-asia |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.techinasia.com |language=en-US}}</ref> 

To enhance its competitive stance against other e-commerce companies, Shopee also launched a website.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tegos |first=Michael |date=24 Nov 2015 |title=Garena’s Shopee could be on its way to beating Carousell in Asia |url=https://www.techinasia.com/shopee-p2p-marketplace-southeast-asia |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.techinasia.com |language=en-US}}</ref> A notable feature of Shopee is its escrow service, ''Shopee Guarantee'', which withholds payments from sellers until the buyers confirm receipt of their orders, thus securing transactions.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |last=Husain |first=Osman |date=11 December 2015 |title=5 disruptive ecommerce startups we saw in 2015 |url=https://www.techinasia.com/5-disruptive-ecommerce-startups-2015 |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=Tech in Asia |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-05-04 |title=Don't fall for scams: Anti-fraud tips and payment safety features to keep you safe while shopping online |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/tech/shopee-dont-fall-for-scams-anti-fraud-tips-and-payment-safety-features-to-keep-you-safe-while-shopping-online |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> 

In 2016, the company launched its seller education platform called ''Shopee University'',<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |title=Managing Director of Shopee Vietnam: Empowering sellers in their journey on e-commerce |url=https://vietnamnews.vn/economy/825779/managing-director-of-shopee-vietnam-empowering-sellers-in-their-journey-on-e-commerce.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106031805/https://vietnamnews.vn/economy/825779/managing-director-of-shopee-vietnam-empowering-sellers-in-their-journey-on-e-commerce.html |archive-date=2024-11-06 |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=vietnamnews.vn |language=en}}</ref> which aims to help train local entrepreneurs and businesses in setting up their online businesses.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.dotdailydose.net/2017/09/08/shopee-teams-up-with-facebook-to-help-leading-retail-brands-strengthen-their-ecommerce-presence/ |title= Shopee teams up with Facebook to help leading retail brands strengthen their eCommerce presence |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date= September 8, 2017 |publisher= dotdailydose|access-date=October 30, 2025 |url-status=live
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251030193230/https://www.dotdailydose.net/2017/09/08/shopee-teams-up-with-facebook-to-help-leading-retail-brands-strengthen-their-ecommerce-presence/ |archive-date=October 30, 2025  }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Cher |first=Benjamin |date=2016-05-05 |title=As market heats up, Shopee launches its own university … kind of |url=https://www.digitalnewsasia.com/startups/market-heats-shopee-launches-its-own-university-kind |access-date=16 November 2024 |website=Digital News Asia |language=en}}</ref> In 2017, Shopee launched ''Shopee Mall'' with 200 brands in Singapore and the Philippines.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 July 2017 |title=Shopee opens online mall for consumers |url=https://sbr.com.sg/retail/more-news/shopee-opens-online-mall-consumers |access-date=10 December 2017 |website=Singapore Business Review}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Online shopping easier with Shopee mall |url=https://manilastandard.net/tech/business0/262630/online-shopping-easier-with-shopee-mall.html |access-date=2021-03-22 |work=Manila Standard |language=en}}</ref> On 3 September 2019, Shopee officially opened its six-story regional headquarters at [[Singapore Science Park]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=2019-09-03 |title=Shopee opens new regional HQ in line with Singapore's push into digital economy |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/shopee-opens-new-regional-hq-in-line-with-singapores-push-into-digital-economy |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> The new building spans {{convert|244,000|sqft|m2}} of space, which can accommodate 3,000 employees and is six times larger than Shopee's previous headquarters at Ascent Building. The building was leased by [[WeWork]] before it was relinquished to Shopee.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=oh_yi_na |date=2019-09-04 |title=PMO {{!}} DPM Heng Swee Keat at the Grand Opening of Shopee Headquarters Building |url=https://www.pmo.gov.sg/Newsroom/DPM-Heng-Swee-Keat-at-the-Grand-Opening-of-Shopee-Headquarters-Building |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Prime Minister's Office Singapore |language=en}}</ref>

Shopee has yet to turn profitable despite increasing its gross profit margin year-on-year in the first half of 2022 which is attributed to faster growth in transaction-based fees and advertising income. Coupled with rising inflation and interest rates as well as setbacks in its internationalisation plans, Shopee laid off staff across multiple markets in June 2022, including employees from [[Indonesia]], [[Thailand]], and [[Vietnam]]. ''ShopeePay'' and ''ShopeeFood'' were also reported to be facing cuts.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Sea's e-commerce arm Shopee to cut staff across Southeast Asia |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Spotlight/DealStreetAsia/Sea-s-e-commerce-arm-Shopee-to-cut-staff-across-Southeast-Asia |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Nikkei Asia |language=en}}</ref>

On 15 September 2022, Sea's CEO, [[Forrest Li]], issued a memo to all employees detailing cost-cutting measures aimed at achieving "self-sufficiency" for the company. These measures involved restrictions on business expenses and a temporary suspension of compensation for Shopee's top executives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandurangi |first=Nidhi |title=Read the memo Singapore billionaire Forrest Li sent to employees of Shopee, the Amazon of Southeast Asia, as the company's losses widen and it prepares for layoffs |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/shopee-layoffs-memo-singapore-billionaire-forrest-li-full-text-2022-9 |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> Another round of job cuts was also announced, which affected employees in Singapore, Indonesia, and China.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yun Ting |first=Choo |date=2022-09-19 |title=Some Singapore staff affected in Shopee's latest job cuts |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/shopee-cuts-singapore-jobs-in-regional-layoffs-says-affected-staff-will-get-appropriate-compensation-packages |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> In the fourth quarter of 2022, Shopee achieved a positive adjusted [[Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization|EBITDA]] for the first time, amounting to $196.1 million, indicating improvements in revenue and operating costs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiang |first=Sheila |date=2023-03-08 |title=Singapore's Sea Group turns profitable for the first time |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/03/08/singapores-sea-group-turns-profitable-for-the-first-time.html |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

In June 2026, [[Sea Ltd|Sea Limited]] expanded its partnership with [[OpenAI]], integrating Shopee into [[ChatGPT]] in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, and Brazil. The integration allows users to receive product recommendations based on conversational queries and follow links to Shopee to complete purchases. Sea and OpenAI also said they were exploring the use of OpenAI's agent technology for shopping-related tasks and providing AI tools to Shopee merchants. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaur |first=Dashveenjit |date=2026-06-23 |title=Is the Shopee ChatGPT integration the blueprint for the future of Southeast Asian e-commerce? |url=https://techwireasia.com/2026/06/hopee-chatgpt-integration-future-southeast-asia-ecommerce/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=TechWire Asia |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Business model ==
Shopee started as a [[consumer-to-consumer]] (C2C) [[marketplace]] but it pivoted into a C2C and [[business-to-consumer]] (B2C) hybrid model.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-05-22 |title=eIQ Insider: The Natural Progression of C2C Business Models, Garena Shopee’s Venture into B2C |url=https://ecommerceiq.asia/garena-business-model-b2c/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220702202731/https://ecommerceiq.asia/garena-business-model-b2c/ |archive-date=2022-07-02 |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=EcommerceIQ - #1 Ecommerce SaaS platform in Southeast Asia |language=en-US}}</ref> The company partners with over 70 courier service providers across markets it serves to provide logistical support for users.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1703399/000119312517312363/d363501df1a.htm |title=Sea Limited Form F-1 |publisher=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission |date=18 October 2017 |access-date=10 December 2017 }}</ref> In [[Singapore]], Shopee collaborates with logistics startup [[Ninja Van]] for item pickup and delivery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hwei |first=Liang |date=2015-12-16 |title=CEO Chris Feng On Shopee's Rise In Southeast Asia, & Avoiding Carouhell |url=https://vulcanpost.com/486471/shopee-garena-marketplace-asia-carouhell/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Vulcan Post |language=en-US}}</ref> Other delivery partners in the region include [[Pos Malaysia]] and [[Pos Indonesia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-06-02 |title=Shopee partners up with Pos Malaysia |url=https://www.marketing-interactive.com/shopee-partners-pos-malaysia |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Marketing-Interactive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bizzy acquires Alpha; Shopee partners Pos Indonesia |url=https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/indonesia-db-b2b-e-commerce-bizzy-acquires-alpha-shopee-partners-pos-indonesia-for-delivery-72245 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=DealStreetAsia |language=en}}</ref> Shopee also partnered with [[Delhivery]] and Ecom Express for deliveries in India before it exited the domestic market.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EXCLUSIVE: Singapore's Shopee clocks over 100,000 orders a day in India, emerges as Amazon & Flipkart challenger |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/startup/exclusive-singapores-shopee-clocks-over-100000-orders-a-day-in-india-emerges-as-amazon-flipkart-challenger-7758731.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250320193112/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/startup/exclusive-singapores-shopee-clocks-over-100000-orders-a-day-in-india-emerges-as-amazon-flipkart-challenger-7758731.html |archive-date=2025-03-20 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> In its early phases of growth, Shopee offered subsidies and free shipping to its users although delivery services were still expensive in the areas it serves.<ref>{{Cite web |last=LatePost |date=2021-03-24 |title=Here's how Lazada lost its lead to Shopee in Southeast Asia (Part 2 of 2) |url=https://kr-asia.com/heres-how-lazada-lost-its-lead-to-shopee-in-southeast-asia-part-2-of-2 |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=KrASIA |language=en}}</ref>

Shopee had also received extreme international attention in 2019 after signing [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese]] [[association football|football]] superstar [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to be the ambassador for the company.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-08-16 |title=Football: Cristiano Ronaldo unveiled as Shopee's latest brand ambassador |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/football-cristiano-ronaldo-unveiled-as-shopees-latest-brand-ambassador |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> That same year, Shopee's 9.9 Super Shopping Day campaign featured a video of Ronaldo dancing to "[[Baby Shark]]" in an advert for the company. The video went [[Viral video|viral]] and became a [[meme]] in the football community, reaching 19 million people. The campaign resulted in a doubling of Shopee's gross orders and a more than tripling of its e-commerce sales.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shopee x Cristiano Ronaldo |url=https://www.thedrum.com/creative-works/project/shopee-x-cristiano-ronaldo |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=The Drum}}</ref>

== Market share ==
In Q4 2017, Shopee became the third most visited e-commerce portal in [[Malaysia]], overtaking Lelong, and became the top app on iOS and Google Play app stores.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who leads e-commerce in Malaysia? Lazada or Shopee? |url=https://e27.co/leads-e-commerce-malaysia-lazada-shopee-20180321/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=e27 |language=en}}</ref> A December 2017 survey revealed that Shopee was the top shopping platform for Indonesian mothers, with 73% preferring it over other platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-07 |title=Shopee found to be the most popular e-commerce site for Indonesian mothers |url=https://www.marketing-interactive.com/shopee-found-to-be-the-most-popular-e-commerce-site-for-indonesian-mothers |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Marketing-Interactive |language=en}}</ref> Despite Shopee's reported GMV growth, these claims faced criticism. [[Lazada]]'s former CEO, Max Bittner, asserted that GMV numbers could be inflated through subsidy schemes and that GMV tends to decline once such subsidies are removed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tech in Asia - Connecting Asia's startup ecosystem |url=https://www.techinasia.com/lazada-vs-sea-whos-top-ecommerce-player-in-southeast-asia |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.techinasia.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Shopee was recognized as top shopping app in Q2 2019 based on monthly active users, total downloads, and website visits, as per a report by iPrice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tan |first=Zhixin |date=22 August 2019 |title=iPrice report has Shopee down as the most popular shopping platform in Southeast Asia |url=https://kr-asia.com/iprice-report-has-shopee-down-as-the-most-popular-shopping-platform-in-southeast-asia |access-date=2019-10-22 |website=KrASIA |language=en-US}}</ref>  During this period, gross orders grew by 92.7% to 246.3 million, compared to 127.8 million in the previous year, and the gross merchandise value (GMV) surged by 72.7% to US$3.8 billion from US$2.2 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-18 |title=e-commerce platform Shopee confident of sustaining strong growth |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2019/10/18/e-commerce-platform-shopee-confident-of-sustaining-strong-growth |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=The Star |language=en}}</ref>

Shopee expanded its operations to Brazil in 2019, marking its first venture into Latin America.<ref name="reutersnoauthor">{{cite news |date=November 1, 2023 |title=Sea's Shopee opens new distribution center in Brazil |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/seas-shopee-opens-new-distribution-center-brazil-2023-11-01 |publisher=Reuters}}</ref> By 2023, Shopee reported engaging with over three million local merchants in Brazil, who contributed to more than 90% of its national sales.<ref name="reutersnoauthor" /> In September 2021, Shopee introduced its marketplace in Poland, followed by launches in Spain and France.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-19 |title=Shopee enters France, Spain, and Poland in aggressive European expansion |url=https://kr-asia.com/shopee-enters-france-spain-and-poland-in-aggressive-european-expansion |access-date=2022-01-13 |website=KrASIA |language=en}}</ref> However, by early 2022, Shopee exited the European markets of France and Spain, retaining only its operations in Poland.<ref name="Bloomberg">{{cite news |last=Poh |first=Olivia |date=1 March 2022 |title=Sea's Shopee Exits France Just Months After Europe Foray |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-01/sea-s-e-commerce-arm-exits-france-a-few-months-into-europe-foray |newspaper=Bloomberg}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Poh |first=Olivia |date=2022-06-14 |title=Sea Cuts Jobs in Shopping, Food in First Major Downsizing |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-14/sea-cuts-jobs-in-shopping-food-in-first-major-downsizing |access-date=2022-06-17 |work=Bloomberg |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Shopee started operations in South Korea to help local merchants reach customers in its existing markets, although it did not establish a consumer-facing platform in [[South Korea]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shopee ramps up hiring in South Korea |url=https://www.techinasia.com/shopee-ramps-south-korea-hiring |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.techinasia.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The following year, the company extended its reach within [[Latin America]] by commencing operations in [[Mexico]], [[Chile]], and [[Colombia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-06 |title=Sea's Shopee to launch in Chile and Colombia |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/seas-shopee-launch-chile-colombia-2021-06-09/ |website=Reuters}}</ref> In November 2021, Shopee entered the Indian market with a soft launch, achieving over one million app installations on the [[Google Play Store]] and handling 100,000 orders a day.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Sahay |first1=Priyanka |last2=Srikanth |first2=Chandra R |date=25 November 2021 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Singapore's Shopee Clocks Over 100,000 Orders A Day In India, Emerges As Amazon & Flipkart Challenger |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/startup/exclusive-singapores-shopee-clocks-over-100000-orders-a-day-in-india-emerges-as-amazon-flipkart-challenger-7758731.html |access-date=2021-11-29 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref> However, Shopee ceased its operations in India in March 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-29 |title=Explained: Why has Shopee shut shop in India? |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/shopee-exit-india-operations-explained-7842028/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> just five months after the launch.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-28 |title=Shopee to close India operations tomorrow. Read its message for shoppers |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/shopee-to-shut-india-operations-from-tomorrow-read-statement-here-11648465062554.html |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=Livemint |language=en}}</ref> As of 2022, Shopee's app recorded 203 million downloads globally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Koetsier |first=John |date=2023-01-04 |title=App tăng like |trans-title=Jan 04, 2023 |url=https://apptanglike.net/ |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> For Q2 of that year, Shopee recorded US$1.7 billion in quarterly revenue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petraeus |first=Michael |date=2022-08-17 |title=Alibaba loses the world to Shopee, as S'pore's hit app now sells more than the Chinese giant |url=https://vulcanpost.com/800023/alibaba-loses-to-shopee-q2-revenue-2022/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=Vulcan Post |language=en-US}}</ref> In September 2022, Shopee ended its local operations in Chile, Colombia, and Mexico, shifting to a cross-border model, and exited Argentina entirely.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-08 |title=Shopee, la competencia de Mercado Libre, abandona la Argentina |url=https://www.perfil.com/noticias/economia/shopee-la-competencia-de-mercado-libre-abandona-la-argentina.phtml |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=Perfil |language=es}}</ref> However, Shopee re-entered Argentina in October 2025, operating a cross-border model to support regional growth, a move reinforced by Argentine media in November 2025.<ref name="AR_ReEntry_2025_Reinforced">{{Cite news |url=https://www.aimdigital.com.ar/politica/shopee-regresa-a-la-argentina-con-envos-gratis-y-fuertes-descuentos.htm |title=Shopee regresa a la Argentina con envíos gratis y fuertes descuentos |work=[[AIM Digital]] |date=2025-11-26 |language=es}}</ref>

Sea Ltd., the company that owns Shopee plunged 22% after an unexpected loss from rising competition. E-commerce growth slowed in the region due to macroeconomic hurdles, resulting in a third-quarter loss in 2023 due to tough competition from Alibaba Group and ByteDance Ltd. Singapore-based Sea (Shopee, Garena, SeaMoney owner) reported revenue up just 4.9% YoY to $3.3B, with Shopee facing heavy marketing spend (up 50%) against TikTok Shop and Lazada. Net loss hit $144M after three profitable quarters, driven by e-commerce losses ($428M) despite Garena's $346M profit decline from falling paying users. In 2025, Shopee delivered strong financials and achieved its third straight profitable year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sea Plunges 22% After Unexpected Loss From Rising Competition |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-11-14/singapore-s-sea-swings-back-to-loss-after-new-rivals-take-a-toll |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250911133308/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-11-14/singapore-s-sea-swings-back-to-loss-after-new-rivals-take-a-toll |archive-date=September 11, 2025 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sea-Limited-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260302039769/en/Sea-Limited-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results |url-status= |archive-date=}}</ref>

In January 2023, the company announced the closure of its Polish operations.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://tvn24.pl/biznes/z-kraju/shopee-polska-koniec-dzialalnosci-w-polsce-komunikat-platformy-st6625760 |title= Platforma Shopee kończy działalność w Polsce |author= <!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date= 12 January 2023 |publisher= TVN24  
|access-date= 8 April 2026 |url-status=live  
|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260408041945/https://tvn24.pl/biznes/z-kraju/shopee-polska-koniec-dzialalnosci-w-polsce-komunikat-platformy-st6625760 |archive-date= 8 April 2026 }}|{{in lang|pl}} </ref> By Q2 2023, Shopee remained the largest online marketplace in Southeast Asia, with a traffic share ranging from 30% to 50% across the region, and also ranked as the leading online shopping platform in Taiwan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiang |first=Sheila |date=2023-05-26 |title=TikTok Shop, a rising threat to Shopee and Lazada in Southeast Asia |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/05/26/tiktok-shop-a-rising-threat-to-shopee-and-lazada-in-southeast-asia.html |access-date=16 November 2024|website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Jono |date=2023-05-30 |title=Shopee Taiwan fined NT$200,000 for customer data breaches |url=https://taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4905586 |access-date=16 November 2024|website=taiwannews.com.tw |language=en}}</ref> In the fourth quarter of 2023, Shopee reported a 46% year-on-year increase in gross orders, reaching 2.5 billion. The gross merchandise value (GMV) for the quarter also rose by 28.6% to US $23.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pramod |first=Mathew |date=2024-03-04 |title=Sea posts first annual profit in 2023 as Shopee clocks strong revenue growth |url=https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/sea-ltd-q4-2023-earnings-386273 |access-date=16 November 2024|website=DealStreetAsia |language=en}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
According to the YouGov's Best Brands Rankings 2026 report, Shopee ranked second in the top 10 brands in Singapore list.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CNA remains among top 10 brands in Singapore: YouGov report|url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/cna-top-10-brands-singapore-yougov-survey-2026-5893596|website=CNA|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en}}</ref>

== Controversies ==
{{Controversy section|date=September 2026}}
=== Meet-and-greet with Blackpink ===
In June 2019, #ShopeeScam trended on Twitter after Shopee released a promotion in the Philippines that offered passes to a meet-and-greet with [[Blackpink]] for the top 568 spenders in their online store.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rose M. Afinidad-Bernardo |first=Deni |date=7 June 2019 |title=Shoppe apologizes for alleged #ShopeeScam at BLACKPINK meet and greet in Manila |agency=The Philippine Star |url=https://www.philstar.com/entertainment/2019/06/07/1924450/shopee-apologizes-alleged-shopeescam-blackpink-meet-and-greet-manila}}</ref> Several fans reported receiving notifications that they had won tickets, but which were unilaterally retracted afterward by Shopee.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} Others posted screenshots that showed Shopee changing their contest mechanics the day before the event. Shopee was investigated by the [[Department of Trade and Industry (Philippines)|Department of Trade and Industry]] for the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Canivel |first=Roy Stephen C. |date=2019-06-07 |title=Online store Shopee probed for BLACKPINK promo |url=https://business.inquirer.net/272111/online-store-shopee-probed-for-blackpink-promo |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=INQUIRER.net |language=en}}</ref>{{needs update|date=December 2021}}

=== Underpaid couriers in Indonesia ===
In April 2021, Shopee faced allegations that it was underpaying its couriers in Indonesia after some riders claimed publicly that their pay per delivered package was reduced by the company to US$0.10 per package, down from US$0.34 in the previous year. Couriers that serve Shopee Express deliveries were also not paid basic monthly salaries, though there is a US$7.90 bonus if they can deliver 40 or more packages in a single workday. There is also no compensation for fuel or parking fees. Shopee responded to the allegations that it has a fair incentive scheme that is in line with Indonesia's market and regulations, and what they offer is "highly competitive" within the industry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florene |first=Ursula |date=2021-04-13 |title=Anger boils in Indonesia as Shopee allegedly underpays its couriers |url=https://kr-asia.com/anger-boils-in-indonesia-as-shopee-allegedly-underpays-its-couriers |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=KrASIA |language=en}}</ref>

=== Rescinded job offers ===
In late August 2022, a user of the Chinese social networking platform Maimai uploaded a post stating that he had relocated as part of a job offer from Shopee to work at the company's headquarters in Singapore. However, the offer was revoked after he disembarked from the plane in Singapore with his family. Multiple job offers were allegedly affected, as other users claimed they had similarly resigned from current positions and terminated housing contracts to join Shopee, only for their offers to be rescinded.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-05 |title=Is Shopee a villain or victim in this turbulent economy? |url=https://kr-asia.com/is-shopee-a-villain-or-victim-in-this-turbulent-economy |access-date=2022-09-13 |website=KrASIA |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=高老头供应链 |date=31 August 2022 |title=跨境电商巨头Shopee大规模毁约：刚落地新加坡，被告知offer没了 |trans-title=Cross-border e-commerce giant Shopee massively rescinds job offers: Just arrived in Singapore, told the offer was gone. |url=https://weibo.com/ttarticle/x/m/show/id/2309404808602857898232?_wb_client_=1 |access-date=2022-09-13 |website=Weibo}}</ref>

=== Toni Gonzaga endorsement ===
On September 28, 2022, Shopee Philippines received backlash when rumors started spreading that the platform would introduce [[Toni Gonzaga]] as its brand ambassador a day after the company's reported massive layoff. This was confirmed the following day at a press conference. While various reasons were pointed for the backlash from the ethical issues with getting a highly-paid endorser to the endorsers' political activities, Gonzaga only appeared on the company's platform for a total of ten days before introducing another endorser for their 11.11 campaign, businessman and singer [[Jose Mari Chan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sho-pissed: Buyers call for mass uninstall, deletion of Shopee after brand teases Toni Gonzaga as new endorser |url=https://coconuts.co/manila/news/sho-pissed-buyers-call-for-mass-uninstall-deletion-of-shopee-after-brand-teases-toni-gonzaga-as-new-endorser/ |access-date=2022-11-10 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2022 |title=Empty cart?: Shopee receives backlash after tapping Toni Gonzaga as endorser |url=https://www.cnnphilippines.com/news/2022/9/30/Shopee-receives-backlash.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110061652/https://www.cnnphilippines.com/news/2022/9/30/Shopee-receives-backlash.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 November 2022}}</ref>

=== Scams and company response ===
In 2023, scammers pretending to be Shopee employees caused over S$750,000 in losses through an online job scam. Shopee and the [[Singapore Police Force]] (SPF) issued a joint announcement to alert the public.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Begum |first=Yasmin |date=May 22, 2023 |title=More than S$750,000 lost to scammers pretending to be Shopee employees |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/more-s750000-lost-scammers-pretending-be-shopee-employees-3506901 |access-date=March 20, 2025 |work=Channel News Asia}}</ref>

In April 2024, Singapore's Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams gave Shopee a favorable rating for its anti-scam measures, including user verification, transaction security and loss remediation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sun |first=David |date=April 11, 2024 |title=Shopee tops latest e-commerce safety ratings; Facebook, Carousell at bottom |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/shopee-improved-scam-safeguards-in-2023-majority-of-e-commerce-scams-now-on-facebook |access-date=March 20, 2024 |website=The Straights Times}}</ref> Also in 2024, Shopee customers lost $399,000 after paying scammers outside the app, based on 179 scam cases reported to police.<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 January 2025 |title=Shopee customers lost $399,000 in 2024 after making payments outside app to scammers |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/shopee-customers-lost-399000-to-scammers-in-2024 |access-date=31 January 2025 |work=The Straits Times}}</ref>

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Video games and Linux
======================================================================

{{Short description|Playing video games on Linux-based operating systems}}
{{Self-published|date=May 2023}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2025}}
{{Video games}}[[Linux|Linux-based operating systems]] can be used for playing [[video game]]s. Because fewer games natively support the Linux kernel than Windows, various software has been made to run [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] games, software, and programs, such as [[Wine (software)|Wine]], [[Cedega (software)|Cedega]], [[DXVK]], and [[Proton (software)|Proton]], and managers such as [[Lutris]] and [[PlayOnLinux]]. The Linux gaming community has a presence on the internet with users who attempt to run games that are not officially supported on Linux.
{{TOC limit|3}}

==History==
{{See also|Open-source video game#History}}

[[File:Nethack releasing a djinni.png|right|thumb|200px|''[[NetHack]]'', a primordial [[Unix]] game]]

Linux gaming started largely as an extension of the already present [[Unix]] [[:Category:Unix games|gaming scene]],<ref>{{cite journal|journal=[[ICGA Journal]]|volume=24|issue=2|date=June 2001|url=https://www.bell-labs.com/usr/dmr/www/ken-games.html| archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20211021/https://www.bell-labs.com/usr/dmr/www/ken-games.html| archive-date=21 October 2021|title=Ken, Unix and Games|first=Dennis|last=Ritchie|pages=67–70 |doi=10.3233/ICG-2001-24202 |author-link=Dennis Ritchie|access-date=19 March 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> which dates back to that [[History of Unix#1960s|system's conception]] in 1969 with the game ''[[Space Travel (video game)|Space Travel]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.silicon.co.uk/cloud/server/tales-tech-history-unix-213133/2|title=Tales In Tech History: Unix|first=Tom|last=Jowitt|website=Silicon UK|date=26 May 2017|access-date=5 March 2023|quote=''The developers wanted to play the game on a PDP-7, a minicomputer built by Digital Equipment Corp found in the corner of their building. But the game couldn’t be run run on more modern (and hence costly) equipment, as computing resource was a precious commodity back then. By the summer of 1969 they had developed the new Unix OS that could run the computer game and in 1971 the first ever edition of Unix was released. A second edition of Unix arrived in December 1972 and was rewritten in the higher-level language C.''}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://medium.com/@joseph.crick/lessons-from-the-development-of-unix-8a324caaf1b4|title=Lessons from the Development of Unix|first=Joseph|last=Crick|date=12 December 2017|website=[[Medium (website)|Medium]]|access-date=18 March 2023}}</ref>{{Self-published inline|date=May 2023}} and the [[History of Unix#1970s|first edition]] in 1971,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cse.yorku.ca/~utn/2031/Notes/unix_hist.pdf|title=The Strange Birth and Long Life of Unix|publisher=[[IEEE Spectrum]]|first=Warren|last=Toomey|date=December 2011|quote=''Apart from the text-processing and general system applications, the first edition of Unix included games such as blackjack, chess, and tic-tac-toe.''}}</ref> with both systems sharing many similar titles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ligurio.github.io/awesome-ttygames/|title=Unix ASCII games|first=Sergey|last=Bronnikov|website=[[GitHub]]|access-date=18 March 2023}}</ref>{{Self-published inline|date=May 2023}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxfocus.org/English/November1999/article118.html|title=Tux's secret obsession – Gaming under Linux|website=LinuxFocus|first=Harald|last=Radke|date=5 November 1999|access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref> These games were mostly either arcade and parlour type games or text adventures using libraries like [[Curses (programming library)|curses]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Allen Holm |first=Joshua |date=21 June 2017|title=Revisit Colossal Cave with Open Adventure |url=https://opensource.com/article/17/6/revisit-colossal-cave-adventure-open-adventure |website=[[Opensource.com]] |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ubuntupit.com/best-ascii-games-on-linux/|website=Ubuntu Pit|title=Top 20 Best ASCII Games on Linux System|first=Mehedi|last=Hasan|date=24 November 2022|access-date=18 March 2023}}</ref> A notable example of this are the "[[Berkley Software Distribution|BSD]] Games", a collection of [[interactive fiction]] and other [[Text-based game|text-mode amusements]].<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Gagné|first=Marcel |date=1 September 2000|title=The Ghost of Fun Times Past|url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/4169 |magazine=[[Linux Journal]]|access-date=20 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607182135/http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/4169 |archive-date=7 June 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Lawrence|last=Woodman|date=11 August 2009|title=My Top 10 Classic Text Mode BSD Games|url=https://techtinkering.com/2009/08/11/my-top-10-classic-text-mode-bsd-games/ |website=TechTinkering|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref> The [[free software]] philosophy and [[open-source software|open-source]] methodology which drove the development of the operating system in general also spawned the creation of various early free games.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stallman|first=Richard |author-link=Richard Stallman|title=Linux and the GNU System|url=https://www.gnu.org/gnu/linux-and-gnu.html |publisher=[[GNU Project]]|access-date=20 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319145123/http://www.gnu.org/gnu/linux-and-gnu.html |archive-date=19 March 2017 |quote=''Some of our system components, the programming tools, became popular on their own among programmers, but we wrote many components that are not tools. We even developed a chess game, GNU Chess, because a complete system needs games too.''}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wen|first=Howard |date=21 November 2001|title=Building Freeciv: An Open Source Strategy Game|url=http://www.linuxdevcenter.com/pub/a/linux/2001/11/21/freeciv.html |website=LinuxDevCenter.com|access-date=14 April 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081229073619/http://www.linuxdevcenter.com/pub/a/linux/2001/11/21/freeciv.html |archive-date=29 December 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Popular early titles included ''[[Netrek]]'' and the various ''[[Asteroids (video game)|XAsteroids]]'', ''XBattle'', ''[[XBill]]'', ''[[Breakout (video game)|XBoing]]'', ''[[Bomberman|X-Bomber]]'', ''[[XConq]]'', ''[[Digger (video game)|XDigger]]'', ''[[Tetris|XEmeraldia]]'', ''XEvil'', ''[[Galaga|XGalaga]]'', ''[[Backgammon|XGammon]]'', ''[[Lunar Lander (video game genre)|XLander]]'', ''[[Conway's Game of Life|XLife]]'', ''[[Mahjong|XMahjong]]'', ''[[Minesweeper (video game)|XMine]]'', ''XSoldier'', ''[[XPilot]]'', ''[[Chase (video game)|XRobots]]'', ''[[Rubik's Cube|XRubiks]]'', ''[[Shogi|XShogi]]'', ''[[Lode Runner|XScavenger]]'', ''[[Tetris|XTris]]'', ''[[Tron (video game)|XTron]]'', ''[[Tic-tac-toe|XTic]]'' and ''XTux'' games using the [[X Window System]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Armstrong|url=https://zerker.ca/home/old-x-games.html|title=Old X Games|website=Zerk Zone|date=18 November 2020|access-date=14 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Hamish |date=10 January 2022 |title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer – Part 8: Shovelware with a Penguin |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/01/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-8-shovelware-with-a-penguin/| website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=9 February 2023}}</ref> Other games targeted or also supported the [[SVGAlib]] library allowing them to run without a [[windowing system]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.developer.com/guides/easy-graphics-a-beginners-guide-to-svgalib/|website=Developer.com|title=Easy graphics: A beginner's guide to SVGAlib|first=Jay|last=Link|date=30 September 1999|access-date=29 September 2023|archive-date=29 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929145330/https://www.developer.com/guides/easy-graphics-a-beginners-guide-to-svgalib/|url-status=dead}}</ref> such as ''[[LinCity]]'', ''[[Maelstrom (1992 video game)|Maelstrom]]'', ''Sasteroids'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://groups.google.com/g/comp.os.linux.announce/c/os3OUbGEbRk/m/G1Nz3lV0AiQJ|title=Sasteroids v1.0 release (vga arcade game)|first=Brad|last=Pitzel|date=12 February 1994|access-date=1 October 2023}}</ref> and ''SABRE''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://linuxgazette.net/issue30/ayers3.html|website=[[Linux Gazette]]|title=Sabre: An Svgalib Flight Sim|first=Larry|last=Ayers|date=1 July 1998|access-date=29 September 2023}}</ref> The [[General Graphics Interface]] was also used<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linuxjournal.com/article/160|title=Linux-GGI Project|first=Andreas|last=Beck|date=1 November 1996|access-date=20 December 2023|website=[[Linux Journal]]}}</ref> for games like ''U.R.B.A.N The Cyborg Project''<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Hamish |date=12 March 2024 |title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer Part 40: The Cyborg Project |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/03/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-40-the-cyborg-project/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=13 March 2024}}</ref> and ''[[Duke Nukem (video game)#Reception|Dave Gnukem]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lwn.net/2000/0106/bigpage.php3|title=Software Announcements|date=6 January 2000|access-date=21 January 2024|website=Linux Weekly News}}</ref> ported from [[DOS]]. As the operating system itself grew and expanded, the amount of free and open-source games also increased in scale and complexity, with both [[Video game clone|clones]] of historically popular releases beginning with ''[[BZFlag]]'', ''LinCity'', and ''[[Freeciv]]'',<ref>{{cite web|last=Fox|first=Alexander |date=5 January 2018|title=The Best Open Source Clones of Great Old Games|url=https://www.maketecheasier.com/best-open-source-clones-of-great-old-games/ |website=Make Tech Easier|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref> and original creations such as ''[[Rocks'n'Diamonds]]'', ''[[Cube (video game)|Cube]]'', ''[[The Battle for Wesnoth]]'', and ''[[Tux Racer]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Swati|last=Maskara|url=https://www.technorms.com/71807/best-open-source-games|title=33 Best Open Source Games That Are Forever Free To Play|publisher=TechNorms|date=3 March 2021|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref>

===1994===
[[File:Doom ingame 2.png|thumb|250px|left|''[[Doom (1993 video game)|Doom]]'' was one of the first major commercial games to be released for Linux.]]

The beginning of Linux as a gaming platform for commercial video games is widely credited to have begun in 1994 when [[Dave D. Taylor]] ported the game ''[[Doom (1993 video game)|Doom]]'' to Linux, and many other systems, during his spare time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/1 |title=DOOM |first=Michael K. |last=Johnson |date=1 December 1994 |access-date=23 April 2023 |publisher=[[Linux Journal]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/3180|title=Getting Started with Quake|publisher=[[Linux Journal]]|date=1 January 1999|last=Zimbinski|first=Bob}}</ref> [[Shareware]] copies of the game were included on various Linux discs,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linuxjournal.com/article/3248|title=Red Hat LINUX Secrets, Second Edition|first=Duane|last=Hellums|date=1 March 1999|access-date=2 July 2023|website=[[Linux Journal]]|quote=''It would be nice to see some extra CD goodies included, such as Doom and Quake which are freely available elsewhere.''}}</ref> including those packed in with [[reference book]]s.<ref>{{cite book |last=Tackett |first=Jack |author-link=|date=1997 |title=Special Edition. Using Linux |url=https://www.abebooks.com/servlet/BookDetailsPL?bi=31119018510&searchurl=an%3Djack%2Btackett%26sortby%3D17%26tn%3Dusing%2Blinux%2Bspecial%2Bedition&cm_sp=snippet-_-srp1-_-title2 |location=United States |publisher=Que Corporation |page=287 |isbn=9780470485460 |quote=''The X Windows version supplied on the accompanying Slackware CD-ROM in the /contrib directory is a complete hareware version. (The Red Hat distribution automatically installs the game during installation.) Although this version runs on 386 computers, it was built to run on high-end 486 systems. If you run DOOM on a 386 with a small amount of physical RAM, be prepared to be disappointed; the game will be too slow to be enjoyable. You need lots of horse-power to play DOOM under Linux.''}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Barkakati |first=Naba |author-link=|date=1996 |title=Linux Secrets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HnqBQgAACAAJ |location=United States |publisher=IDG Books Worldwide |page=96 |isbn=9781568847986 |quote=''This disk set contains a collection of well-known UNIX games (X is not required), such as Hangman, Dungeon, and Snake. The set also includes id Software's DOOM. (This game comes in two versions, one runs under X, and the other runs without X.) You may want to install this disk set just so you can try out DOOM.''}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Parker |first=Tim |author-link=|date=1996 |title=Linux Unleashed |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IZ5kQgAACAAJ|location=United States |publisher=Macmillan Computer Publishing |page=981 |isbn=0672313723 |quote=''DOOM - This exciting, though controversially gory, game is now ported to Linux as well. Complete with sound support and exquisite graphics, this Linux port does its DOS counterpart justice.''}}</ref>

''[[Ancient Domains of Mystery]]'' was also released for Linux in 1994 by [[Thomas Biskup]], building on the [[roguelike]] legacy of games such as ''[[Moria (1983 video game)|Moria]]'' and its descendent ''[[Angband (video game)|Angband]]'', but more specifically ''[[Hack (video game)|Hack]]'' and ''[[NetHack]]''.

===1995===
From there Taylor would also help found the development studio Crack dot Com, which released the video game ''[[Abuse (video game)|Abuse]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.loonygames.com/content/1.10/guest/|title=So Long, Crack.com|publisher=loonygames|access-date=4 August 2011|archive-date=21 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021165111/http://www.loonygames.com/content/1.10/guest/|url-status=dead}}</ref> with the game's Linux port even being distributed by Linux vendors [[Red Hat]]<ref>{{cite press release |title=Partnership with Crack dot Com Brings Games to Linux |url=http://www.redhat.com/about/news/press-archive/1997/10/press-crackdotcom |publisher=[[Red Hat]] |date=7 October 1997 |access-date=31 July 2014}}</ref> and [[Caldera (company)|Caldera]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Anonymous |date=2000 |title=Maximum Linux Security: A Hacker's Guide to Protecting Your Linux Server and Workstation, Volume 1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WCfjE_TzmIAC |location=United States |publisher=[[Sams Publishing]] |page=121 |isbn=9780672316708 |quote=''A classic, and very easy-to-follow SUID attack is the on the file /usr/lib/games/abuse/ abuse.console—part of a game that was distributed with Open Linux 1.1 and Red Hat 2.1. Yes, you read that right: Even a game can be a security risk to the system.''}}</ref> The studio's never finished ''[[Golgotha (video game)|Golgotha]]'' was also slated to be released by Red Hat in box.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/okay-dave-taylor-why-linux/1100-2467851/|title=Okay, Dave Taylor: Why Linux?|website=[[GameSpot]]|first=Harley|last=Jebens|date=26 April 2000|access-date=17 March 2023}}</ref>

In 1991 DUX Software contracted Don Hopkins to port ''[[SimCity (1989 video game)|SimCity]]'' to Unix,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://virtuallyfun.com/2022/12/30/simcity-for-unix-liberated/|website=Virtually Fun|title=SimCity for Unix Liberated|first=Antoni|last=Sawicki|date=30 December 2022|access-date=4 March 2023}}</ref> which he ported to Linux in 1995 and eventually released as open source for the [[OLPC XO]] laptop.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.donhopkins.com/drupal/|title=History and Future of OLPC SimCity – Micropolis|access-date=17 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113113239/http://www.donhopkins.com/drupal/|archive-date=13 January 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A website named The Linux Game Tome, also known as HappyPenguin after its [[URL]], was begun by [[Tessa Lau]] in 1995 to catalogue games created for or ported to Linux from the [[ibiblio|SunSITE]] game directories and other classic X11 games for a set of just over 100 titles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=[ANNC] The Linux Game Tome on the Web |url=https://groups.google.com/g/comp.os.linux.misc/c/NzXFbdSJ1rY |access-date=16 December 2023 |website=groups.google.com}}</ref>

===1996–1997===
[[id Software]], the original developers of ''Doom'', also [[id Software#Linux gaming|continued to]] release their products for Linux. Their game ''[[Quake (video game)|Quake]]'' was ported to Linux via [[X11]] in 1996, once again by Dave D. Taylor working in his free time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.blankmaninc.com/david-taylor-interview |title='Dave Taylor Interview – game developer' |publisher=blankmaninc.com |date=27 October 2012 |access-date=4 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140723204846/http://www.blankmaninc.com/david-taylor-interview/ |archive-date=23 July 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://linux.omnipotent.net/article.php?article_id=11261|title=How To Install Quake 1|publisher=Linux.com|date=15 November 2000|last=Mrochuk|first=Jeff|access-date=16 March 2011|archive-date=1 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220401073212/http://linux.omnipotent.net/article.php?article_id=11261|url-status=dead}}</ref> An [[SVGALib]] version was also later produced by Greg Alexander in 1997 using recently leaked source code, but was later mainlined by id.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Hamish |date=27 February 2023 |title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer – Part 27: Lost Souls |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/02/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-27-lost-souls/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=27 February 2023}}</ref> Later id products continued to be ported by [[Zoid Kirsch]]<ref>{{cite web|title=An interview with Dave "Zoid" Kirsch of linux quake fame|url=http://linuxpower.org/display_item.phtml?id=105|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19990910231358/http://linuxpower.org/display_item.phtml?id=105|website=Linux Power|first1=Barath|last1=Raghavan|first2=Jeremy|last2=Katz|first3=Jack|last3=Moffitt|archive-date=10 September 1999|date=19 February 1999|access-date=27 February 2023}}</ref> and [[Timothee Besset]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgames.com/?dataloc=articles/ttimo/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040924113843/http://www.linuxgames.com/?dataloc=articles/ttimo/|title=Interview with id Software's Timothee Besset|first=Dustin|last=Reyes|website=LinuxGames|date=22 August 2004|archive-date=24 September 2004|access-date=27 February 2023}}</ref> a practice that continued until the studio's acquisition by [[ZeniMax Media]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/121945-John-Carmack-Argues-Against-Native-Linux-Games |title=John Carmack Argues Against Native Linux Games |first=Andy |last=Chalk |date=6 February 2013 |access-date=29 September 2013 |publisher=[[The Escapist (magazine)|The Escapist]] |archive-date=21 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121193621/http://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/121945-John-Carmack-Argues-Against-Native-Linux-Games |url-status=dead}}</ref> Initially, Zoid Kirsch was responsible for maintaining the Linux version of Quake and porting QuakeWorld to Linux.

''[[Inner Worlds (video game)|Inner Worlds]]'' was released for and developed on Linux.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sleepless.com/iw/article.html |title=Internet Based Software Development |publisher=Sleepless Software Inc |date=19 September 2001 |last=Hitchens |first=Joe |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011231003158/http://sleepless.com/iw/article.html |archive-date=31 December 2001}}</ref> ''The UNIX Book of Games'', a 1996 publication by Janice Winsor, described various games with an accompanying CD-ROM containing executables and source code for [[Linux]] and [[SCO Unix]].<ref>{{cite web|title=REVIEW – The UNIX Book of Games|url=https://accu.org/bookreviews/1998/dicks_871/|website=[[ACCU (organisation)|ACCU]]|first=Steve|last=Dicks|date=December 1998|access-date=17 March 2023}}</ref>

===1998===
[[File:SDL Layers.svg|right|thumb|The Simple DirectMedia Layer provided platform independent abstraction.]]

The Linux Game Tome was taken over by Bob Zimbinski in 1998 eventually growing to over 2000 entries, sponsored by retailer Penguin Computing and later [[Linux Game Publishing|LGP]] until it went down in 2013, although mirrors still exist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linux.com/news/site-review-linux-game-tome|website=[[Linux.com]]|title=Site review: Linux Game Tome|first=Tina|last=Gasperson|date=16 December 2004|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/news/ODc5OA|title=LGP Has Been Down For A Month And A Half|website=[[Phoronix]]|first=Michael|last=Larabel|date=18 November 2010|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref>

The site LinuxGames covered news and commentary from November 1998 until its host Atomicgamer went down in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/top-4-websites-free-linux-games/ |title=Top 4 Websites To Discover Free Linux Games |first=Danny |last=Stieben |date=6 February 2013 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=Make Use Of}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://digitalconqurer.com/general/best-web-places-to-find-amazing-free-linux-games/ |title=Best Web Places to Find Amazing Free Linux Games |first=Amol |last=Wagh |date=14 September 2011 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=Digital Conqueror}}</ref> It was established by Marvin Malkowski, head of the Telefragged gaming network, alongside Al Koskelin and Dustin Reyes;<ref>{{cite web |url=http://edition.cnn.com/TECH/computing/9907/01/linuxgame.idg/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010514234141/http://edition.cnn.com/TECH/computing/9907/01/linuxgame.idg/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 May 2001|title=You can tell a lot about an OS from its games |first=Joe |last=Barr |date=1 July 1999 |access-date=14 August 2023 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> Reyes died 8 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dawe|first=Liam |date=14 August 2023|title=Rest in peace Dustin 'Crusader' Reyes, a pioneer of Linux gaming news |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/08/rest-in-peace-dustin-crusader-reyes-a-pioneer-of-linux-gaming-news/ |website=GamingOnLinux|access-date=14 August 2023}}</ref>

Zoid Kirsch from id Software ported Quake II to Linux. Two programmers from [[Origin Systems|Origin]] ported ''[[Ultima Online]]'' to Linux and MP Entertainment released an adventure game ''[[Hopkins FBI]]'' for Linux<ref>{{cite web|url=http://reverser.hut.ru/old/linux.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040229150312/http://reverser.hut.ru/old/linux.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 February 2004|title=Ultima Online for Linux}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071028191834/http://linux.omnipotent.net/article.php?article_id=6937|url=http://linux.omnipotent.net/article.php?article_id=6937|title=Hopkins FBI|publisher=[[Linux.com]]|date=9 February 2000|archive-date=28 October 2007|last=Kuhnash|first=Jeremy}}</ref>

On 9 November 1998, a new software firm called [[Loki Software]] was founded by Scott Draeker, a former lawyer who became interested in porting games to Linux after being introduced to the system through his work as a software licensing attorney.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/3521|title=Interview: Scott Draeker and Sam Lantinga, Loki Entertainment|work=[[Linux Journal]]|date=1 August 1999}}</ref> Loki, although a commercial failure, is credited with the birth of the modern Linux game industry.<ref name="Lynch">{{cite web|url=https://www.infoworld.com/article/3117295/remembering-lokis-linux-games-from-the-90s.html|title=Remembering Loki's Linux games from the '90s|first=Jim|last=Lynch|website=[[InfoWorld]]|date=7 September 2016|access-date=26 February 2023}}</ref> Loki developed several free software tools, such as the Loki installer (also known as Loki Setup),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.macologist.org/viewtopic.php?t=607 |title=Interview with Ryan Gordon: Postal2, Unreal & Mac Gaming – Macologist |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050309061407/http://www.macologist.org/viewtopic.php?t=607 |archive-date=9 March 2005}}</ref> and supported the development of the [[Simple DirectMedia Layer]],<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030511174315/http://www-106.ibm.com/developerworks/library/l-making-linux-fun/|url=http://www-106.ibm.com/developerworks/library/l-making-linux-fun/|title=SDL: Making Linux fun|first=Sam|last=Lantinga|author-link=Sam Lantinga|date=1 September 1999|access-date=15 December 2023|archive-date=11 May 2003|website=[[IBM]]|url-status=live}}</ref> and starting the [[OpenAL]] audio library project.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/4400|title=The Story of OpenAL|publisher=[[Linux Journal]]|date=1 January 2001|last=Kreimeier|first=Bernd}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.gamespy.com/legacy/articles/loki_a.shtm|title=Loki and the Linux World Expo – GameSpy chats with Linux legend Scott Draeker about the future of Linux gaming|publisher=GameSpy|last=Hills|first=James|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060315020137/http://archive.gamespy.com/legacy/articles/loki_a.shtm|archive-date=15 March 2006}}</ref> These are still often credited as being the cornerstones of Linux game development.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.itworld.com/article/2785732/open-source-tools/does-ragnarok-for-loki-spell-doom-for-linux-games-.html|title=Does Ragnarok for Loki Spell Doom for Linux Games?|first=Eric|last=Foster-Johnson|access-date=9 February 2016|archive-date=29 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829175620/http://www.itworld.com/article/2785732/open-source-tools/does-ragnarok-for-loki-spell-doom-for-linux-games-.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> They were also responsible for bringing nineteen high-profile games to the platform before its closure in 2002.

===1999===
Loki published ''[[Civilization: Call to Power]]'', ''[[Eric's Ultimate Solitaire]]'', Heretic II, Heroes of Might and Magic III, Railroad Tycoon II: Gold Edition, Quake III: Arena, and Unreal Tournament for Linux.<ref name=":04">{{Cite journal |last=Mielewczik |first=Michael |title=Spielspass pur. Kommerzielle Linux-Spiele. |journal=PC Magazin LINUX |volume=2/2007 |pages=80–83}}</ref>
 
Loki's initial success also attracted other firms to invest in the Linux gaming market, such as Tribsoft, [[Hyperion Entertainment]], [[Macmillan Publishers (United States)|Macmillan Digital Publishing USA]], Titan Computer, [[Xatrix Entertainment]], [[Philos Laboratories]], and [[Vicarious Visions]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespy.com/articles/492/492050p1.html|website=[[GameSpy]]|title=Is Linux Gaming here to stay?|first=James|last=Hills|date=1 March 2001|access-date=7 December 2023}}</ref>

The ports of ''Quake'' and ''Quake II'' were released physically by [[Macmillan Computer Publishing]] USA,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Macmillan+Says+%27Let+the+Linux+Games+Begin%21%27%3B+Market+Leader+in+Linux...-a054913355|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305020245/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Macmillan+Says+%27Let+the+Linux+Games+Begin%21%27%3B+Market+Leader+in+Linux...-a054913355|website=[[Business Wire]]|title=Macmillan Says 'Let the Linux Games Begin!'; Market Leader in Linux Software & Books Offers 'Quake' & 'Civilization'|access-date=3 March 2018|archive-date=5 March 2016|date=17 June 1999|url-status=dead}}</ref> while ''Quake III'' was released for Linux by [[Loki Software]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnn.com/2000/TECH/computing/03/09/quake3.linux.idg/index.html|title=Quake III Arena on Linux|first=Rawn|last=Shah|website=[[CNN]]|date=9 March 2000|access-date=27 February 2023}}</ref> Red Hat had previously passed on publishing ''Quake'' for Linux, since it was not [[open-source]] at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slashdot.org/articles/98/11/05/105224.shtml|title=Red Hat not Interested in Publishing Id Games|website=[[Slashdot]]|author=CmdrTaco|date=5 November 1998|access-date=12 September 2023}}</ref>

Philos Laboratories released a Linux version of ''[[Theocracy (computer game)|Theocracy]]'' on the retail disk. Ryan "Ridah" Feltrin from Xatrix Entertainment released a Linux version of ''[[Kingpin: Life of Crime]]''.

BlackHoleSun Software released ''Krilo'' and Futureware 2001 released a trading simulation Würstelstand for Linux.<ref name="Wilson">{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Hamish |date=16 January 2023 |title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer – Part 21: Fluffy Bunnies |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/01/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-21-fluffy-bunnies/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=2 February 2023}}</ref>

The [[Indrema Entertainment System]] (also known as the L600) was also in development since 1999 as a Linux-based [[Home video game console|game console]] and [[digital media player]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/article-29793|title=Indrema to bring Linux to the masses?|author=Gestalt|date=21 November 2000|access-date=7 December 2023|website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Game start-up faces major rivals with Linux console |first=Stephen |last=Shankland |url=https://www.cnet.com/culture/game-start-up-faces-major-rivals-with-linux-console/|access-date=7 December 2023 |work=[[CNET]] |date=2 January 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Game Arrives Only in Dreams |first=Farhad |last=Manjoo |url=https://www.wired.com/2001/03/game-arrives-only-in-dreams/|access-date=7 December 2023 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |date=13 March 2001}}</ref> but production halted in 2001 due to a lack of investment,<ref>{{cite news |title=Plans for Linux game console fizzle |first=David |last=Becker |url=https://www.cnet.com/culture/plans-for-linux-game-console-fizzle/ |access-date=7 December 2023 |work=[[CNET]] |date=2 January 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Linux games console fragged |first=Tony |last=Smith |url=https://www.theregister.com/2001/04/11/linux_games_console_fragged/ |access-date=7 December 2023 |work=[[The Register]] |date=11 April 2001}}</ref> although the TuxBox project attempted a continuation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linux.com/news/tuxbox-rising-indremas-ashes/|title=TuxBox: Rising from Indrema's ashes|date=18 April 2001|first=Grant|last=Gross|website=Linux.com|access-date=7 December 2023}}</ref>

===2000===
Loki published Descent 3, Heavy Gear II, SimCity 3000, and Soldier of Fortune for Linux. They also released the expansion Descent 3: Mercenary as the downloadable Linux installer.<ref name=":04"/>

Hyperion Entertainment ported Sin to Linux published by Titan Computer. Vicarious Visions ported the space-flight game ''[[Terminus (2000 video game)|Terminus]]'' to Linux. [[Mountain King Studios]] released a port of ''[[Raptor: Call of the Shadows]]'' and CipSoft published the Linux client of Tibia.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://happypenguin.org/show?Raptor%20-%20Call%20of%20the%20Shadows|title=The Linux Game Tome: Raptor – Call of the Shadows |author=|url-status=usurped<!--Not stated-->|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221230935/http://happypenguin.org/show?Raptor%20-%20Call%20of%20the%20Shadows |archive-date=21 February 2012}} on [[The Linux Game Tome]]</ref>

Boutell.com ported ''[[Exile III: Ruined World]]'' to Linux, which was a game created by [[Spiderweb Software]].

During this time Michael Simms founded [[Linux Game Publishing#Tux Games|Tux Games]], one of the first online Linux game retailers,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.linuxgamepublishing.com/2009/05/15/lgp-history-pt-1-how-lgp-came-to-be/ |title=Linux Game Publishing Blog, LGP History pt 1: How LGP came to be |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713212344/http://blog.linuxgamepublishing.com/2009/05/15/lgp-history-pt-1-how-lgp-came-to-be/ |archive-date=13 July 2011}}</ref> later followed by Fun 4 Tux,<ref>{{cite web |last=Dawe|first=Liam |date=30 June 2011|title=Gameolith – The Linux Game Download Store |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2011/06/gameolith-the-linuxacircreg-game-download-store/ |website=GamingOnLinux|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref> Wupra,<ref>{{cite web |last=Bush|first=Josh |date=11 September 2018|title=Cheese talks to himself (about Proton and the history of modern Linux gaming) |url=http://cheesetalks.net/proton-linux-gaming-history.php |website=CheeseTalks|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref> ixsoft, and LinuxPusher.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/news/MTY1MDQ|title=Linux Game Publishing Remains Dormant|website=[[Phoronix]]|first=Michael|last=Larabel|date=1 April 2014|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref>

The period also saw a number of commercial compilations released,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/12/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-36-entertainment-for-x-windows/|title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer Part 36: Entertainment for X
